Enhanced PGC-1α activity counters the energetic and oxidative deficits underlying neurodegeneration. The directionality is SIRT1 → PGC-1α → neuronal resilience. This axis is a leading explanation for how SIRT1 activation benefits Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, and other neurodegenerative models.

nodes.label: Resveratrol (high-calorie diet mice)
nodes.description: In mice on a high-calorie diet, resveratrol increases mitochondrial number and function, an effect accompanied by elevated SIRT1 and PGC-1α activity. This shift counters diet-induced metabolic dysfunction by improving oxidative capacity. The directionality is resveratrol upstream, activating SIRT1/PGC-1α to drive mitochondrial biogenesis. The finding helped popularize resveratrol as a CR-mimetic against diet-induced obesity.

nodes.label: Blood glucose and insulin
nodes.description: Resveratrol treatment lowers blood glucose and circulating insulin in animals on a high-calorie diet, improving glycemic control. These metabolic benefits are linked to SIRT1/AMPK activation and improved insulin sensitivity in liver and muscle. The directionality is resveratrol → SIRT1/AMPK → reduced glycemia. Caveats include that human trials have been inconsistent, likely owing to poor bioavailability.

nodes.label: SIRT3 gene variant (intron 5 enhancer)
nodes.description: A polymorphism in an intron-5 enhancer of the SIRT3 gene is associated with exceptional longevity (age beyond 90 years) specifically in men. The variant is thought to alter SIRT3 expression or regulation, conferring enhanced mitochondrial stress resistance. The directionality is genetic variation associated with, and putatively causal of, prolonged lifespan. As a correlation, it supports but does not prove that higher SIRT3 activity promotes human longevity.

nodes.label: Male longevity beyond 90 years
nodes.description: A polymorphism in an intron-5 enhancer of the SIRT3 gene is associated with exceptional longevity (age beyond 90 years) specifically in men. The variant is thought to alter SIRT3 expression or regulation, conferring enhanced mitochondrial stress resistance. The directionality is genetic variation associated with, and putatively causal of, prolonged lifespan. As a correlation, it supports but does not prove that higher SIRT3 activity promotes human longevity.

nodes.label: SIRT1 allele variants
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Several single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the human SIRT1 gene are significantly associated with systemic energy expenditure in Finnish cohorts, suggesting that SIRT1 variation influences metabolic rate. These variants may alter SIRT1 expression or activity, shifting how individuals burn fuel. The directionality is genetic SIRT1 variation linked to energy-expenditure phenotype. As with most GWAS associations, effect sizes are modest and context-dependent.

nodes.label: Androgen receptor (Lys630)
nodes.description: SIRT1 binds the androgen receptor and deacetylates it at Lys630 within the lysine motif, repressing AR transcriptional activity and its oncogenic signaling in prostate tissue. This enzymatic modification dampens AR-driven proliferative programs. The directionality is SIRT1 acting upstream to inhibit AR. This axis is relevant to prostate cancer, where SIRT1 can oppose androgen-dependent tumor growth.

nodes.label: HOXA10 (homeobox transcription factor)
nodes.description: SIRT2 interacts with HOXA10, a conserved homeobox transcription factor critical for embryonic cell-type determination and adult tissue homeostasis. The interaction suggests SIRT2 influences HOXA10-dependent transcriptional programs, though the precise deacetylation outcome is less characterized. The directionality is SIRT2 engaging HOXA10 as a partner/substrate. This connection links SIRT2 to developmental regulation and possibly to differentiation defects in disease.

nodes.label: Hes1 and Hey2 (bHLH repressors)
nodes.description: SIRT1 physically interacts with the bHLH transcriptional repressors Hes1 and Hey2 both in vitro and in vivo, modulating their ability to repress target promoters. Deacetylation by SIRT1 can alter the DNA-binding or co-repressor recruitment of these factors. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatically tuning Hes1/Hey2 repression. This intersects with Notch and VEGF signaling and with SIRT1's neuroprotective regulation of BDNF.

nodes.label: Developmental defects
nodes.description: SIRT1-null mice are markedly smaller, grow slowly, and show defects in eye morphogenesis and cardiac septation, revealing SIRT1's role in normal development. These phenotypes indicate that SIRT1 is not merely a stress-response protein but is required for organogenesis. The directionality is SIRT1 deficiency causing structural developmental abnormalities. The perinatal lethality of many knockouts limited study, prompting tissue-specific models.

nodes.label: Sterility
nodes.description: Surviving SIRT1 knockout mice of both sexes are sterile: males have low sperm counts and females fail to ovulate, implicating SIRT1 in gametogenesis and reproductive endocrine control. The defect reflects failed differentiation and stress responses in gonadal tissues. The directionality is SIRT1 loss upstream of reproductive failure. This shows SIRT1 is essential for germ-cell development and fertility.

nodes.label: Nmnat (NAD+ biosynthetic enzyme)
nodes.description: Nmnat, the NAD+-biosynthetic enzyme, protects axons from Wallerian degeneration largely by raising NAD+ and thereby activating SIRT1, which supports axonal survival after injury. The protection is upstream of SIRT1-dependent maintenance of mitochondrial and chromatin function in neurons. The directionality is Nmnat → NAD+ → SIRT1 → axonal protection. This established a key NAD+/sirtuin axis in neuronal resilience.

nodes.label: Axonal/Wallerian degeneration (via SIRT1)
nodes.description: Nmnat, the NAD+-biosynthetic enzyme, protects axons from Wallerian degeneration largely by raising NAD+ and thereby activating SIRT1, which supports axonal survival after injury. The protection is upstream of SIRT1-dependent maintenance of mitochondrial and chromatin function in neurons. The directionality is Nmnat → NAD+ → SIRT1 → axonal protection. This established a key NAD+/sirtuin axis in neuronal resilience.

nodes.label: Smad7 (Lys60, Lys70)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates Smad7 at Lys60 and Lys70, which enhances Smad7's recognition by the E3 ligase Smurf1 and targets it for ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation. This accelerates turnover of the TGF-β inhibitory Smad, modulating TGF-β pathway intensity. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic marking of Smad7 for destruction. The consequence is context-dependent regulation of TGF-β signaling rather than simple inhibition.

nodes.label: SIRT1 deacetylation of Smad7
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: By promoting degradation of Smad7, SIRT1 deacetylation tempers TGF-β signaling in glomerular mesangial cells and protects them from TGF-β-dependent apoptosis. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts on Smad7 to relieve a pro-apoptotic TGF-β output. This renoprotective mechanism is relevant to diabetic nephropathy and other glomerulopathies. It illustrates how sirtuin control of a single substrate can determine cell fate in injury.

nodes.label: TGF-β-dependent glomerular apoptosis
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: By promoting degradation of Smad7, SIRT1 deacetylation tempers TGF-β signaling in glomerular mesangial cells and protects them from TGF-β-dependent apoptosis. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts on Smad7 to relieve a pro-apoptotic TGF-β output. This renoprotective mechanism is relevant to diabetic nephropathy and other glomerulopathies. It illustrates how sirtuin control of a single substrate can determine cell fate in injury.

nodes.label: Histone H2A.Z (Lys115, Lys121)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates Lys115 and Lys121 of the histone variant H2A.Z, a mark that licenses H2A.Z for ubiquitination and proteasome-dependent degradation. Removing these acetyl groups thus destabilizes H2A.Z at chromatin. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic modification upstream of H2A.Z clearance. Because H2A.Z promotes pathological hypertrophy, its removal is protective in the heart.

nodes.label: SIRT1 deacetylation of H2A.Z
nodes.description: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation and degradation of H2A.Z helps protect the heart from failure by removing a histone variant that drives maladaptive cardiac hypertrophic gene programs. The directionality is SIRT1 → H2A.Z loss → attenuated hypertrophy. This is a mechanistically plausible explanation for why SIRT1 activation is cardioprotective, though the in vivo evidence carries moderate confidence (0.75). It links chromatin dynamics directly to heart disease resistance.

nodes.label: p300 (Lys1020, Lys1024)
nodes.description: SIRT1 negatively regulates the histone acetyltransferase p300 by deacetylating it at Lys1020 and Lys1024, reducing p300's enzymatic and coactivator activity. This counterbalances p300-driven acetylation of chromatin and transcription factors. The directionality is SIRT1 inhibiting a major acetyltransferase, creating a rheostat between acetylation and deacetylation. This crosstalk helps SIRT1 enforce repression of inflammatory and growth genes.

nodes.label: Oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells
nodes.description: SIRT2 is expressed in oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells, the myelin-forming glia of CNS and PNS respectively, where it deacetylates α-tubulin and regulates microtubule stability. Its presence in myelinating cells ties SIRT2 to axonal support and myelin integrity. The directionality is SIRT2 acting within glia to control cytoskeletal dynamics. Dysregulation is implicated in demyelinating and neurodegenerative conditions.

nodes.label: Muscle cells (myogenesis)
nodes.description: SIRT1 inhibits myogenesis by deacetylating histones H3K9 and H3K14 at the promoters of myogenin and myosin heavy chain, repressing muscle-gene expression. This keeps myoblasts in a less differentiated state under certain conditions. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of suppressed muscle differentiation. However, SIRT1 can also support muscle maintenance under stress, so context matters.

nodes.label: Osteoblasts (vs adipocytes)
nodes.description: SIRT1 activators promote osteoblast differentiation while suppressing adipocyte formation from mesenchymal progenitors, biasing lineage commitment toward bone. This effect is linked to SIRT1's repression of PPAR-γ and support of RUNX2/osteogenic programs. The directionality is SIRT1 favoring osteogenesis over adipogenesis. The association carries moderate confidence (0.75) but has therapeutic implications for osteoporosis. Importantly, it complements SIRT1's opposing action on myogenesis, underscoring context dependence.

nodes.label: p33ING1b
nodes.description: In hepatocarcinoma, p33ING1b binds SIRT1 and blocks its ability to deacetylate p53, thereby preserving p53's transcriptional activity, including repression of α-fetoprotein (AFP). This relieves SIRT1-mediated inhibition of p53 tumor suppression. The directionality is p33ING1b antagonizing SIRT1 at the p53 node. The interaction reveals a tissue-specific brake on SIRT1's pro-survival, potentially oncogenic, action.

nodes.label: p53 (in hepatocarcinoma)
nodes.description: In hepatocarcinoma, p33ING1b binds SIRT1 and blocks its ability to deacetylate p53, thereby preserving p53's transcriptional activity, including repression of α-fetoprotein (AFP). This relieves SIRT1-mediated inhibition of p53 tumor suppression. The directionality is p33ING1b antagonizing SIRT1 at the p53 node. The interaction reveals a tissue-specific brake on SIRT1's pro-survival, potentially oncogenic, action.

nodes.label: Adiponectin gene expression (via FOXO1-C/EBPα)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO1 and enhances its interaction with C/EBPα, a combination that drives transcription of the adiponectin gene and raises circulating adiponectin. Adiponectin in turn improves insulin sensitivity and has anti-inflammatory effects. The directionality is SIRT1 → FOXO1/C/EBPα → adiponectin expression. This links SIRT1 to beneficial adipokine secretion and metabolic health.

nodes.label: Adiponectin
nodes.description: Administration of adiponectin to obese, high-fat-fed mice improves insulin sensitivity and lowers blood glucose, reflecting its role as a insulin-sensitizing adipokine. It acts through AdipoR1/2 receptors to activate AMPK and PPAR-α pathways that enhance fatty-acid oxidation. The directionality is adiponectin upstream of improved insulin action. Because SIRT1 raises adiponectin, this forms part of SIRT1's anti-diabetic circuitry.

nodes.label: β-amyloid neuropathology (Alzheimer's mouse model)
nodes.description: In mouse models engineered to develop Alzheimer's-like pathology, caloric restriction prevents accumulation of β-amyloid neuropathology, an effect consistent with SIRT1-driven reductions in neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. The directionality is CR upstream of reduced amyloid burden. This supports the hypothesis that CR protects the brain through sirtuin-mediated resilience. Human translation remains uncertain but motivates lifestyle interventions in neurodegeneration.

nodes.label: PGC-1α knockout mice
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Mice lacking PGC-1α are markedly more sensitive to neuronal loss induced by MPTP (a dopaminergic toxin) and kainic acid (an excitotoxin), revealing PGC-1α's role in neuronal stress resistance. Because SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, this sensitivity indirectly implicates the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis in neuroprotection. The directionality is PGC-1α deficiency → heightened vulnerability. The phenotype mirrors features of Parkinson's and other neurodegenerative models.

nodes.label: MPTP and kainic acid neuronal damage
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Mice lacking PGC-1α are markedly more sensitive to neuronal loss induced by MPTP (a dopaminergic toxin) and kainic acid (an excitotoxin), revealing PGC-1α's role in neuronal stress resistance. Because SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, this sensitivity indirectly implicates the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis in neuroprotection. The directionality is PGC-1α deficiency → heightened vulnerability. The phenotype mirrors features of Parkinson's and other neurodegenerative models.
nodes.norm_label: mptp and kainic acid neuronal damage

nodes.label: NAD+-dependent enzyme
nodes.description: The sirtuin family comprises seven mammalian members (SIRT1–SIRT7) plus the ancestral yeast Sir2, all sharing an NAD+-dependent catalytic core that performs deacetylation and ADP-ribosylation. They differ in subcellular localization—nuclear (SIRT1, SIRT6, SIRT7), cytoplasmic (SIRT2), and mitochondrial (SIRT3, SIRT4, SIRT5)—which dictates their substrate portfolios. The directionality is that NAD+ is the obligate co-substrate for every family member. This unifying dependence ties sirtuin activity to the cellular energy and redox state.

nodes.label: Glutamate dehydrogenase
nodes.description: SIRT4 inhibits glutamate dehydrogenase by mono-ADP-ribosylation, reducing conversion of glutamate to α-ketoglutarate and limiting anaplerotic carbon entry into the TCA cycle. The directionality is SIRT4 enzymatic suppression of GDH. This restrains amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion and mitochondrial ATP generation. It marks SIRT4 as a metabolic brake within mitochondria.

nodes.label: rRNA transcription
nodes.description: SIRT7 regulates rRNA transcription by activating RNA polymerase I and deacetylating histone H3K18 at ribosomal DNA, controlling ribosome biogenesis and protein synthetic capacity. The directionality is SIRT7 upstream of Pol I activity and ribosome production. Because excessive ribosome biogenesis fuels proliferation, this activity aligns SIRT7 with growth and, in cancer, with tumor promotion. It also ties SIRT7 to nucleolar stress responses.

nodes.label: Daratumumab
nodes.description: Daratumumab (Darzalex, first approved 2015) and isatuximab (Sarclisa, approved 2020/2021) are IgG1 monoclonal antibodies that bind distinct epitopes on CD38, a cell-surface ectoenzyme. By engaging CD38 on malignant plasma cells, daratumumab triggers antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement-dependent killing. The directionality is the antibody acting on CD38-expressing cells. Although primarily an anticancer agent, depleting CD38 also reduces NAD+ consumption, indirectly favoring sirtuin activity.

nodes.label: Isatuximab
nodes.description: Isatuximab (Sarclisa) is an IgG1 anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody, approved around 2020/2021, that binds a different CD38 epitope than daratumumab. It mediates direct apoptosis and immune effector functions against CD38+ multiple myeloma cells. The directionality is antibody → CD38 engagement → tumor cell death. Like daratumumab, it also lowers CD38 ectoenzyme activity, indirectly preserving NAD+ for sirtuins.

nodes.label: Multiple myeloma
nodes.description: Daratumumab is a frontline anti-CD38 antibody therapy for multiple myeloma, where CD38 is highly expressed on malignant plasma cells. Its clinical efficacy stems from direct and immune-mediated elimination of these cells. The directionality is daratumumab upstream of myeloma cell clearance. Beyond oncology, its CD38 inhibition has the secondary effect of sparing NAD+ pools that sirtuins depend on.

nodes.label: PDE4 (phosphodiesterase 4)
nodes.description: Resveratrol competitively inhibits cAMP phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4), the enzyme that degrades cAMP to AMP, thereby slowing cAMP clearance. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of PDE4 inhibition. This indirect action raises intracellular cAMP, which then engages the Epac1/Ca2+/AMPK/NAMPT cascade that further activates SIRT1. It is one arm of resveratrol's dual (direct plus indirect) SIRT1-activation mechanism.

nodes.label: PDE4 inhibition (resveratrol)
nodes.description: Inhibiting PDE4 prevents cAMP degradation, so intracellular cAMP accumulates after resveratrol exposure. The directionality is PDE4 inhibition → elevated cAMP. Elevated cAMP then activates the exchange protein Epac1, propagating a calcium and AMPK signal that ultimately boosts NAD+ and SIRT1. This pathway explains how resveratrol can activate SIRT1 even through non-allosteric means.

nodes.label: intracellular cAMP
nodes.description: Inhibiting PDE4 prevents cAMP degradation, so intracellular cAMP accumulates after resveratrol exposure. The directionality is PDE4 inhibition → elevated cAMP. Elevated cAMP then activates the exchange protein Epac1, propagating a calcium and AMPK signal that ultimately boosts NAD+ and SIRT1. This pathway explains how resveratrol can activate SIRT1 even through non-allosteric means.

nodes.label: cAMP (elevated)
nodes.description: High intracellular cAMP activates Epac1 (Exchange Protein directly Activated by cAMP), a guanine-nucleotide-exchange factor that triggers downstream signaling independent of PKA. The directionality is cAMP upstream of Epac1 activation. Epac1 then stimulates calcium release from the ER, linking cAMP to Ca2+-dependent kinases. This step is pivotal in resveratrol's indirect SIRT1-activation cascade.

nodes.label: Epac1
nodes.description: High intracellular cAMP activates Epac1 (Exchange Protein directly Activated by cAMP), a guanine-nucleotide-exchange factor that triggers downstream signaling independent of PKA. The directionality is cAMP upstream of Epac1 activation. Epac1 then stimulates calcium release from the ER, linking cAMP to Ca2+-dependent kinases. This step is pivotal in resveratrol's indirect SIRT1-activation cascade.

nodes.label: Epac1 activation
nodes.description: Epac1 activation induces calcium release from the endoplasmic reticulum into the cytoplasm, raising cytosolic Ca2+ that serves as a second messenger. The directionality is Epac1 upstream of cytoplasmic Ca2+ elevation. The Ca2+ surge then activates CaMKKβ, bridging cAMP signaling to AMPK. This couples resveratrol's PDE4 inhibition to metabolic kinase activation.

nodes.label: Ca2+ release (ER → cytoplasm)
nodes.description: Epac1 activation induces calcium release from the endoplasmic reticulum into the cytoplasm, raising cytosolic Ca2+ that serves as a second messenger. The directionality is Epac1 upstream of cytoplasmic Ca2+ elevation. The Ca2+ surge then activates CaMKKβ, bridging cAMP signaling to AMPK. This couples resveratrol's PDE4 inhibition to metabolic kinase activation.

nodes.label: Ca2+ surge (cytoplasmic)
nodes.description: The cytoplasmic calcium surge activates calmodulin-dependent protein kinase kinase β (CaMKKβ), which phosphorylates and activates AMPK, the central cellular energy sensor. The directionality is Ca2+ → CaMKKβ → AMPK phosphorylation. Activated AMPK then induces NAMPT and raises NAD+, closing the loop on SIRT1 activation. This is a key branch point linking calcium flux to metabolic homeostasis.

nodes.label: CaMKKβ → AMPK
nodes.description: The cytoplasmic calcium surge activates calmodulin-dependent protein kinase kinase β (CaMKKβ), which phosphorylates and activates AMPK, the central cellular energy sensor. The directionality is Ca2+ → CaMKKβ → AMPK phosphorylation. Activated AMPK then induces NAMPT and raises NAD+, closing the loop on SIRT1 activation. This is a key branch point linking calcium flux to metabolic homeostasis.

nodes.label: AMPK (activated)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Activated AMPK increases expression of NAMPT, the rate-limiting enzyme of the NAD+ salvage pathway that converts nicotinamide to NMN. The directionality is AMPK upstream of NAMPT induction. More NAMPT elevates intracellular NAD+, the obligate co-substrate for sirtuins. This AMPK→NAMPT→NAD+ axis is a major indirect route by which resveratrol and exercise activate SIRT1.

nodes.label: NAMPT upregulation
nodes.description: NAMPT is the rate-limiting enzyme in the NAD+ salvage pathway, so its upregulation raises cellular NAD+ levels and fuels sirtuin activity. The directionality is NAMPT increase → NAD+ increase → enhanced sirtuin function. This is the terminal step of resveratrol's indirect activation cascade. Preserving NAD+ via NAMPT (or CD38 inhibition) is a common theme across sirtuin-activating strategies.

nodes.label: SIRT1 deacetylation of FOXO3a
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Deacetylated FOXO3a transcriptionally upregulates endogenous antioxidant enzymes, prominently mitochondrial SOD2 and catalase, bolstering ROS scavenging. The directionality is SIRT1/FOXO3a upstream of increased antioxidant capacity. This reduces oxidative damage in resveratrol-treated cells and animals. It is a central mechanism for sirtuin-mediated protection against aging and metabolic disease.

nodes.label: SOD2 (Superoxide Dismutase 2)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Deacetylated FOXO3a transcriptionally upregulates endogenous antioxidant enzymes, prominently mitochondrial SOD2 and catalase, bolstering ROS scavenging. The directionality is SIRT1/FOXO3a upstream of increased antioxidant capacity. This reduces oxidative damage in resveratrol-treated cells and animals. It is a central mechanism for sirtuin-mediated protection against aging and metabolic disease.

nodes.label: SIRT1 deacetylation of NF-κB
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: By deacetylating NF-κB, SIRT1 reduces transcription of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, dampening the inflammatory transcriptome. The directionality is SIRT1/NF-κB upstream of lower cytokine output. This is mechanistically important in atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration, and metabolic inflammation. Resveratrol leverages this axis to curb chronic low-grade inflammation.

nodes.label: Pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: By deacetylating NF-κB, SIRT1 reduces transcription of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, dampening the inflammatory transcriptome. The directionality is SIRT1/NF-κB upstream of lower cytokine output. This is mechanistically important in atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration, and metabolic inflammation. Resveratrol leverages this axis to curb chronic low-grade inflammation.

nodes.label: SIRT1 (resveratrol-activated)
nodes.description: Resveratrol-activated endothelial SIRT1 increases eNOS expression and deacetylates/activates it, enhancing nitric-oxide production and promoting vasodilation. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of eNOS activation. Improved NO bioavailability lowers vascular tone and protects against endothelial dysfunction. This underlies resveratrol's cardiovascular and 'French paradox' associations.

nodes.label: SIRT1 activation (resveratrol)
nodes.description: Through the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α pathway, resveratrol reduces hepatic steatosis in diet-induced obesity models by enhancing fatty-acid oxidation and mitochondrial function while limiting lipogenesis. The directionality is SIRT1 activation upstream of reduced liver fat accumulation. This demonstrates a translational metabolic benefit of sirtuin activation. Human efficacy, however, is limited by resveratrol's poor bioavailability.

nodes.label: Hepatic steatosis (fatty liver)
nodes.description: Through the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α pathway, resveratrol reduces hepatic steatosis in diet-induced obesity models by enhancing fatty-acid oxidation and mitochondrial function while limiting lipogenesis. The directionality is SIRT1 activation upstream of reduced liver fat accumulation. This demonstrates a translational metabolic benefit of sirtuin activation. Human efficacy, however, is limited by resveratrol's poor bioavailability.

nodes.label: Hormetic (biphasic) dose-response
nodes.description: Resveratrol shows a hormetic, biphasic dose-response: at low-to-moderate doses it acts as a mild stressor that triggers beneficial adaptive responses such as sirtuin activation and antioxidant defense, whereas at very high doses it can produce off-target or pro-oxidant effects. The directionality is dose determining outcome, not simple monotonic benefit. This complicates dosing in therapeutics. It also rationalizes why modest, diet-like exposures may be more effective than pharmacological megadoses.

nodes.label: Oral bioavailability
nodes.description: Resveratrol undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism—glucuronidation and sulfation in gut and liver—yielding very low systemic free concentrations after oral intake. The directionality is oral administration → rapid conjugation → poor bioavailability. This undermines many preclinical benefits when translating to humans. Strategies such as the red-wine matrix, nanoparticle delivery, or combining with quercetin/ethanol aim to improve exposure.

nodes.label: MnSOD (K68, K122)
nodes.description: Honokiol-activated SIRT3 deacetylates MnSOD at Lys68 and Lys122, markedly increasing its superoxide-scavenging activity in the mitochondrial matrix. The directionality is SIRT3 enzymatic activation of MnSOD. Enhanced MnSOD lowers mitochondrial ROS and protects against oxidative injury. This is a principal mechanism for honokiol's cardiorenal and neuroprotective effects.

nodes.label: OSCP (ATP synthase subunit)
nodes.description: Honokiol-activated SIRT3 deacetylates OSCP, a subunit of the mitochondrial F1Fo-ATP synthase, optimizing coupling of proton flux to ATP synthesis. The directionality is SIRT3 enzymatic tuning of ATP synthase. Improved coupling boosts cellular energy output while limiting proton-leak-associated ROS. This contributes to honokiol's metabolic and cardioprotective actions.

nodes.label: Renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis
nodes.description: Honokiol suppresses renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis by activating SIRT3, which inhibits the NF-κB/TGF-β1 pathway and limits fibrogenic signaling in kidney tubules. The directionality is honokiol → SIRT3 → antifibrotic transcription. This reduces collagen deposition and inflammatory infiltrate. It illustrates SIRT3's broad tissue-protective role beyond the heart.

nodes.label: Dihydromyricetin
nodes.description: Dihydromyricetin (DHM), a flavonoid from vine tea, activates SIRT3 mitochondrial deacetylase activity, leading to MnSOD deacetylation and lowered ROS. The directionality is DHM upstream of SIRT3 activation. This mitochondrial action underlies DHM's hepatoprotective and metabolic benefits. DHM also activates AMPK, synergizing with SIRT3 via NAD+ elevation.

nodes.label: UBCS039
nodes.description: UBCS039 is the first synthetic, selective allosteric activator of SIRT6, binding its distal hydrophobic pocket and stimulating deacetylase activity (EC50 ≈ 38 μM). The directionality is UBCS039 binding SIRT6 to enhance its catalytic output. It preferentially engages the deacetylase function and drives chromatin compaction and tumor-suppressive programs. UBCS039 helped validate SIRT6 as a druggable longevity target.

nodes.label: MDL-801
nodes.description: MDL-801 is a potent, cell-permeable synthetic allosteric activator of SIRT6 that binds the hydrophobic pocket and stimulates its deacetylase activity (EC50 ≈ 10.3 μM). The directionality is MDL-801 upstream of SIRT6 activation. It mirrors UBCS039 but with greater potency and cell permeability. MDL-801 mitigates kidney fibrosis and suppresses glycolytic, tumor-promoting metabolism.

nodes.label: Cyanidin
nodes.description: Cyanidin, a natural anthocyanidin from red berries, increases SIRT6 activity by over 50-fold in certain in vitro assays, making it one of the most powerful natural SIRT6 activators. The directionality is cyanidin upstream of SIRT6 stimulation. Its potency suggests strong binding to the SIRT6 activation pocket. This links berry polyphenols to SIRT6-dependent metabolic and anti-aging effects.

nodes.label: H3K9ac and H3K56ac
nodes.description: Activated SIRT6 rapidly deacetylates histone H3K9ac and H3K56ac at chromatin, promoting compaction and facilitating DNA-repair and silencing programs. The directionality is SIRT6 enzymatic removal of these active marks. Loss of H3K56ac in particular is associated with genome stability and stress resistance. This chromatin action underlies SIRT6's roles in longevity and tumor suppression.

nodes.label: Glycolysis (Warburg effect)
nodes.description: By suppressing glycolysis and pushing tumor cells toward oxidative metabolism or autophagy, SIRT6 activators such as UBCS039 display tumor-suppressive activity. The directionality is SIRT6 activation upstream of reduced Warburg glycolysis. This restrains the aerobic-glycolytic phenotype that fuels cancer growth. It is a mechanistic rationale for SIRT6 activation in oncology.

nodes.label: CPS1 (carbamoyl phosphate synthase 1)
nodes.description: SIRT5 desuccinylates and activates carbamoyl phosphate synthase 1 (CPS1), the rate-limiting enzyme of the urea cycle, enhancing ammonia detoxification into urea. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of CPS1. This is especially important during fasting or high-protein load when nitrogen must be cleared. It exemplifies SIRT5's role as a regulator of mitochondrial acyl-metabolism.

nodes.label: SIRT2 overactivity
nodes.description: Direct SIRT2 activation is generally avoided therapeutically because overactivity is linked to neurotoxicity in neurodegenerative contexts, where excessive deacetylation may impair microtubule and protein-homeostasis defenses. The directionality is SIRT2 overactivity associated with neuronal damage. Consequently, SIRT2 inhibitors are pursued for Parkinson's and Huntington's disease. This contrasts with most other sirtuins, where activation is sought.

nodes.label: Neurotoxicity
nodes.description: Direct SIRT2 activation is generally avoided therapeutically because overactivity is linked to neurotoxicity in neurodegenerative contexts, where excessive deacetylation may impair microtubule and protein-homeostasis defenses. The directionality is SIRT2 overactivity associated with neuronal damage. Consequently, SIRT2 inhibitors are pursued for Parkinson's and Huntington's disease. This contrasts with most other sirtuins, where activation is sought.

nodes.label: SIRT2 inhibitors (AGK2, AK-7, SirReal2)
nodes.description: Selective SIRT2 inhibitors such as AGK2, AK-7, and SirReal2 are investigated in neurodegenerative disease models because blocking SIRT2 preserves α-tubulin acetylation and protects neurons from aggregation toxicity. The directionality is SIRT2 inhibition → microtubule stability → neuroprotection. These agents rescue dopaminergic neurons from α-synuclein toxicity and confer ischemic protection. The approach exploits the inverse therapeutic logic of SIRT2 versus other sirtuins.

nodes.label: Parkinson's and Huntington's disease
nodes.description: Selective SIRT2 inhibitors such as AGK2, AK-7, and SirReal2 are investigated in neurodegenerative disease models because blocking SIRT2 preserves α-tubulin acetylation and protects neurons from aggregation toxicity. The directionality is SIRT2 inhibition → microtubule stability → neuroprotection. These agents rescue dopaminergic neurons from α-synuclein toxicity and confer ischemic protection. The approach exploits the inverse therapeutic logic of SIRT2 versus other sirtuins.

nodes.label: NMN (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide)
nodes.description: NMN is a direct NAD+ precursor that, once converted to NAD+, serves as a universal indirect pan-sirtuin activator by supplying the obligate co-substrate for all seven sirtuins. The directionality is NMN → NAD+ → sirtuin activation. It raises NAD+ levels that decline with age, restoring sirtuin function systemically. NMN (with NR) is a leading nutraceutical strategy to counteract age-related sirtuin attenuation.

nodes.label: Universal indirect pan-sirtuin activator
nodes.description: NMN is a direct NAD+ precursor that, once converted to NAD+, serves as a universal indirect pan-sirtuin activator by supplying the obligate co-substrate for all seven sirtuins. The directionality is NMN → NAD+ → sirtuin activation. It raises NAD+ levels that decline with age, restoring sirtuin function systemically. NMN (with NR) is a leading nutraceutical strategy to counteract age-related sirtuin attenuation.

nodes.label: NR (Nicotinamide Riboside)
nodes.description: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is an NAD+ precursor that raises cellular NAD+ and thereby indirectly activates all seven sirtuins by supplying their shared co-substrate. The directionality is NR → NAD+ → pan-sirtuin activation. Like NMN, NR reverses age-related NAD+ decline and restores sirtuin-dependent maintenance. It is a leading nutraceutical approach to broadly engage sirtuin biology.

nodes.label: H3K18
nodes.description: SIRT7 is highly localized to the nucleolus and deacetylates histone H3K18 (H3K18ac), a mark associated with active rDNA transcription, thereby repressing ribosome biogenesis when deacetylated. The directionality is SIRT7 enzymatic removal of H3K18ac. Because excess ribosome production fuels growth and cancer, this repressive action can be tumor-suppressive in some contexts. It also stabilizes pericentric heterochromatin, supporting genome stability.

nodes.label: NF-κB signaling pathway
nodes.description: SIRT1 inhibits NF-κB transcriptional activity by deacetylating the p65/RelA subunit at Lys310, preventing optimal promoter engagement. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of suppressed NF-κB signaling. This lowers chronic inflammation linked to aging and atherosclerosis. It is one of the best-established anti-inflammatory mechanisms of SIRT1.

nodes.label: Histone H3K9
nodes.description: SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 at the promoters of NF-κB target genes, reducing their transcription and thereby dampening inflammation. The directionality is SIRT6 enzymatic chromatin repression of NF-κB-driven loci. This complements SIRT6's direct actions and underscores its anti-inflammatory role. Loss of SIRT6 elevates H3K9ac and inflammatory output.

nodes.label: NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses
nodes.description: SIRT6 overexpression suppresses NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses, as shown in models such as osteoarthritis development where cytokine production is reduced. The directionality is SIRT6 upstream of inhibited NF-κB inflammation. This protection arises from both chromatin deacetylation and p65 degradation. It positions SIRT6 as a nuclear inflammation brake.

nodes.label: SIRT7-kidney-specific knockout
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Kidney-specific SIRT7 knockout mice show diminished inflammation with reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 and suppressed nuclear NF-κB p65 accumulation, indicating SIRT7 normally promotes renal NF-κB activation. The directionality is SIRT7 loss → less nuclear p65 → lower inflammation. This is somewhat counterintuitive given SIRT7's usual anti-inflammatory renal role elsewhere, underscoring context dependence. It suggests SIRT7 can be pro-inflammatory in specific renal settings.

nodes.label: spliced X-box binding protein 1
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates spliced X-box-binding protein 1 (XBP1s) downstream of an AMPKα-dependent pathway in macrophages, and deacetylated XBP1s then inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome assembly. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic modification of XBP1s → NLRP3 suppression. This couples endoplasmic-reticulum stress responses to sirtuin control of inflammation. It is a key mechanism in atherosclerotic and metabolic disease.

nodes.label: miR-217
nodes.description: The microRNA miR-217 negatively regulates SIRT1 by binding its 3'UTR and repressing translation, thereby diminishing SIRT1's anti-inflammatory and metabolic functions. The directionality is miR-217 upstream of lowered SIRT1. Downregulation of miR-217 mitigates inflammatory responses via the SIRT1/AMPK/NF-κB axis. This exemplifies miRNA fine-tuning of sirtuin abundance.

nodes.label: miR-543
nodes.description: miR-543 represses SIRT1 expression post-transcriptionally, and its downregulation reduces inflammation by strengthening the SIRT1/AMPK/NF-κB signaling pathway. The directionality is miR-543 upstream of SIRT1 suppression. This places miR-543 among miRNAs that calibrate inflammatory tone. Modulating such miRNAs is a potential anti-inflammatory strategy.

nodes.label: miR-378
nodes.description: miR-378 reduces SIRT1 activity and facilitates NF-κB-TNFα inflammatory signaling, in part by targeting the 5'-AMPK subunit gamma-2. The directionality is miR-378 → SIRT1 inhibition → NF-κB activation. This links a metabolic miRNA to sirtuin-controlled inflammation. It illustrates how miRNA networks gate sirtuin protective effects.

nodes.label: MCPIP1
nodes.description: MCPIP1 (monocyte chemoattractant protein-induced protein 1), an RNase, alleviates inflammatory responses by promoting SIRT1 expression through modulation of miR-9. The directionality is MCPIP1 upstream of increased SIRT1. Higher SIRT1 then suppresses NF-κB-driven inflammation. This reveals an anti-inflammatory circuit centered on SIRT1 induction.

nodes.label: p53/miR-22 axis
nodes.description: SIRT1 targets the p53/miR-22 axis to suppress inflammation, lowering expression of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS). The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of repressed p53/miR-22-inflammatory output. This intersects SIRT1's control of p53 with miRNA-mediated gene silencing. It broadens SIRT1's anti-inflammatory repertoire beyond NF-κB.

nodes.label: PTP1B
nodes.description: SIRT1 increases insulin sensitivity and lowers blood glucose by downregulating protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B), a key negative regulator of insulin receptor signaling. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of PTP1B suppression. Reduced PTP1B prolongs insulin-receptor phosphorylation and signaling. This is a direct mechanism for SIRT1's antidiabetic actions.

nodes.label: CREB
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates CREB (cAMP response element-binding protein), particularly at Lys136, modulating its transcriptional regulation of lipid-metabolism genes. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic tuning of CREB activity. Deacetylated CREB alters target-gene programs controlling lipogenesis and energy balance. This links SIRT1 to cAMP-coupled metabolic regulation.

nodes.label: HNF4α
nodes.description: SIRT2 prevents liver steatosis and lipid metabolic disorders by deacetylating hepatocyte nuclear factor 4α (HNF4α), a master regulator of hepatic lipid and drug-metabolizing genes. The directionality is SIRT2 enzymatic activation of HNF4α. This maintains lipid homeostasis and protects against fatty liver. It adds a hepatic metabolic function to SIRT2's repertoire.

nodes.label: AMPK/PGC-1α pathway
nodes.description: SIRT3 activates the AMPK/PGC-1α pathway, driving mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming toward oxidative phosphorylation and biogenesis. The directionality is SIRT3 upstream of AMPK/PGC-1α. This enhances energy production and stress resistance while limiting glycolytic reliance. It is a core mechanism for SIRT3's metabolic and cardioprotective benefits.

nodes.label: Nrf2 signaling
nodes.description: Overexpression of SIRT6 in the brain via in vivo gene transfer enhances Nrf2 signaling and reduces oxidative stress, linking SIRT6 to antioxidant transcription. The directionality is SIRT6 upstream of Nrf2 pathway activation. This complements SIRT6's AMPK/MnSOD/catalase axis. It reinforces SIRT6's role in neuronal and systemic antioxidant defense.

nodes.label: JAK2/STAT3 pathway
nodes.description: SIRT6 inhibits the Janus kinase 2/STAT3 pathway, suppressing growth and survival signaling in gastric cancer (GC). The directionality is SIRT6 upstream of JAK2/STAT3 blockade. This restrains STAT3-driven proliferation and is part of SIRT6's tumor-suppressive repertoire. It adds a cytokine-receptor-linked mechanism to SIRT6's anti-cancer actions.

nodes.label: Cervical cancer progression
nodes.description: SIRT2 expression is decreased in cervical cancer tissue versus adjacent normal tissue, and higher SIRT2 predicts favorable survival, indicating it suppresses cervical cancer progression. The directionality is SIRT2 loss associated with, and putatively enabling, tumor advancement. Its deacetylase actions on metabolic and mitotic substrates likely enforce differentiation and genome stability. This adds to the context-dependent tumor-suppressor face of SIRT2.

nodes.label: ACC1
nodes.description: SIRT3 deacetylates acetyl-CoA carboxylase 1 (ACC1), upregulating its activity and promoting de novo lipogenesis that can fuel invasion and metastasis of cervical cancer cells. The directionality is SIRT3 enzymatic activation of ACC1 → lipid synthesis. This reveals a tumor-promoting facet of SIRT3 in certain cancers, contrasting its usual protective role. It highlights that SIRT3's metabolic effects are context-dependent.

nodes.label: LC3
nodes.description: SIRT1 promotes autophagy in endothelial and cancer cells by deacetylating LC3, a key autophagy protein required for autophagosome formation and flux. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic modification of LC3 → enhanced autophagy. This supports cellular clearance of damaged organelles and proteins. It is one of several SIRT1 substrates (with Beclin-1, Atg5, Atg7, ULK1) that license autophagy.

nodes.label: IGF-Akt signaling
nodes.description: SIRT6 blocks IGF-Akt signaling and thereby cardiac hypertrophy development by targeting c-Jun, interrupting a pro-hypertrophic survival pathway. The directionality is SIRT6 upstream of IGF-Akt repression. This protects the heart from maladaptive growth. It complements SIRT6's anti-fibrotic actions in cardiovascular tissue.

nodes.label: NFATc2
nodes.description: SIRT2 binds and deacetylates the nuclear factor of activated T-cell c2 (NFATc2) transcription factor, regulating its transcriptional activity in immune and cardiovascular contexts. The directionality is SIRT2 enzymatic tuning of NFATc2. Because NFATc2 drives interleukin and hypertrophic gene programs, its deacetylation influences inflammation and cardiac remodeling. It links SIRT2 to calcineurin/NFAT signaling.

nodes.label: Cardiac fibrosis
nodes.description: SIRT4 contributes to cardiac fibrosis; global SIRT4 knockout in mice confers resistance to angiotensin-II infusion by suppressing fibrotic deposition. The directionality is SIRT4 upstream of profibrotic signaling. This aligns with SIRT4's general tendency to promote pathological remodeling. It contrasts with the antifibrotic SIRT1/SIRT3/SIRT6 members.

nodes.label: SERCA2a
nodes.description: Pharmacological activation of SIRT1 restores SERCA2a activity by deacetylating it at Lys492, improving calcium reuptake into the sarcoplasmic reticulum of cardiomyocytes. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic activation of SERCA2a. Better SERCA2a function enhances contractility and opposes heart failure. This is a direct mechanism for SIRT1's cardioprotection.

nodes.label: Lox-1-mediated foam cell formation
nodes.description: SIRT1 activation reduces lectin-like oxidized-LDL receptor-1 (Lox-1)-mediated foam cell formation by suppressing NF-κB signaling in vascular cells. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of inhibited Lox-1 scavenging of ox-LDL. This limits macrophage lipid loading, a key early step in atherosclerosis. It is a vascular anti-atherogenic action of SIRT1.

nodes.label: VSMC proliferation and migration
nodes.description: SIRT7 regulates vascular smooth-muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation and migration through the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, limiting the neointimal hyperplasia that drives vascular disease. The directionality is SIRT7 upstream of VSMC quiescence. By restraining VSMC activation, SIRT7 protects against atherosclerotic and restenotic remodeling. It adds a vascular-stability role to SIRT7.

nodes.label: MDL-800
nodes.description: MDL-800 is a bis-benzenesulfonamide prodrug and potent, selective SIRT6 activator (EC50 = 10.3 μM) that stimulates SIRT6 deacetylase activity. The directionality is MDL-800 allosteric activation of SIRT6. It mirrors UBCS039 but with greater potency and cell permeability, mitigating kidney fibrosis and tumor glycolysis. It is a lead chemical tool for SIRT6 biology.

nodes.label: EX-527 (Selisistat)
nodes.description: EX-527 (Selisistat) is the first known selective, cell-permeable SIRT1 inhibitor (IC50 = 0.098 μM) with minimal activity against SIRT2/3. The directionality is EX-527 blocking SIRT1 catalysis. It is used to dissect SIRT1-dependent phenotypes and was explored clinically for Huntington's disease. As a SIRT1 blocker, its effects contrast with STACs like resveratrol.

nodes.label: SirReal2
nodes.description: SirReal2 is a potent SIRT2 inhibitor (IC50 = 0.14 μM) with minimal effects on SIRT1 and SIRT3, exploiting a SIRT2-specific binding pocket. The directionality is SirReal2 blocking SIRT2 deacetylase activity. It is a key chemical probe for SIRT2 biology in neurodegeneration and cancer. Selectivity makes it valuable for isolating SIRT2-specific effects.

nodes.label: Suramin
nodes.description: Suramin, a polyanionic urea derivative, inhibits sirtuins with IC50 values of ~297 nM, 1150 nM, and 22 μM for SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT5 respectively, showing relative selectivity for SIRT5 at higher concentrations. The directionality is suramin blocking sirtuin catalysis. Its broad activity limits specificity, but it remains a tool to probe SIRT5. Clinically, suramin is an antiparasitic and anticancer agent with off-target sirtuin effects.

nodes.label: TGF-β1-induced apoptosis and fibrosis
nodes.description: Overexpression of SIRT1 abolishes TGF-β1-induced apoptosis and fibrosis and suppresses CTGF expression in mouse kidney, protecting renal tissue from TGF-β1 insult. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of suppressed TGF-β1 pathology. This renoprotective action operates via deacetylation of TGF-β pathway components. It supports SIRT1 activation as a strategy against kidney fibrosis.

nodes.label: TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation
nodes.description: Genetic knockdown and chemical inhibition of SIRT2 attenuate TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation and MDM2 expression, reducing fibrogenic responses. The directionality is SIRT2 inhibition → less TGF-β1 fibroblast activation. This is unusual because it implies SIRT2 can promote, rather than suppress, fibrosis in this context. It underscores the context-dependence of sirtuin-fibrosis relationships.

nodes.label: pyruvate dehydrogenase E1α
nodes.description: Pyruvate dehydrogenase E1α (PDH E1α) becomes hyperacetylated at Lys385 in tubular epithelial cells after TGF-β1 stimulation and is deacetylated by SIRT3, modulating pyruvate entry into the TCA cycle. The directionality is SIRT3 enzymatic activation of PDH. This links mitochondrial metabolism to TGF-β1-driven kidney injury. It shows SIRT3 buffering metabolic dysfunction during fibrosis.

nodes.label: osteogenic transdifferentiation of VSMCs
nodes.description: SIRT6 suppresses osteogenic transdifferentiation of vascular smooth-muscle cells via repression of runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2), limiting vascular calcification. The directionality is SIRT6 upstream of inhibited VSMC osteogenesis. This protects against stiffening of vessels in atherosclerosis and aging. It is a vascular-homeostasis function of SIRT6.

nodes.label: UUO-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis
nodes.description: The SIRT6 activator MDL-800 mitigates unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO)-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis, validating SIRT6 activation therapeutically. The directionality is MDL-800 → SIRT6 activation → renal protection. This complements other evidence that SIRT6 restrains TGF-β/Smad3 fibrogenesis. It supports SIRT6 as a target for chronic kidney disease.
nodes.norm_label: uuo-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis

nodes.label: T helper type 1 cells development
nodes.description: Dendritic-cell SIRT1 knockout drives T helper 1 (Th1) cell development and promotes inflammation, indicating SIRT1 normally restrains Th1 polarization. The directionality is DC SIRT1 upstream of suppressed Th1 differentiation. This tempers cell-mediated inflammatory responses. It demonstrates SIRT1's immunoregulatory role in antigen presentation.

nodes.label: SIRT6 deficiency (macrophages)
nodes.description: SIRT6 deficiency in macrophages increases acetylation and stability of FoxO1, leading to sustained FoxO1 protein and an inflammatory state. The directionality is SIRT6 loss → hyperacetylated, stabilized FoxO1. Because SIRT6 normally deacetylates FoxO1, its absence prolongs FoxO1 signaling. This reveals a macrophage-intrinsic mechanism linking SIRT6 to inflammation resolution.

nodes.label: GLUT2
nodes.description: SIRT6 deacetylates FoxO1 and subsequently increases expression of glucose-dependent transporter 2 (GLUT2) in pancreatic β-cells. The directionality is SIRT6 → FoxO1 → GLUT2 induction. Higher GLUT2 restores glucose sensing and appropriate insulin release. This complements SIRT6's role in β-cell metabolic health.

nodes.label: Preadipocyte differentiation
nodes.description: SIRT5 inhibits preadipocyte differentiation and lipid deposition by activating AMPK and repressing MAPK signaling pathways. The directionality is SIRT5 upstream of suppressed adipogenesis. This keeps progenitors from becoming lipid-laden fat cells. It positions mitochondrial SIRT5 as a negative regulator of fat accumulation.

nodes.label: Autophagosome-lysosome fusion
nodes.description: TFEB is a master transcription factor for lysosomal biogenesis and autophagy that plays a critical role in autophagosome–lysosome fusion and clearance of cargo. The directionality is TFEB upstream of autophagic-lysosomal execution. Because SIRT2 stabilizes TFEB mRNA, SIRT2 indirectly promotes this fusion. It links sirtuins to the terminal degradative step of autophagy.

nodes.label: LDHB
nodes.description: SIRT5-induced deacetylation of lactate dehydrogenase B (LDHB) triggers hyperactivation of autophagy, a process implicated in tumorigenesis. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic modification of LDHB → autophagy surge. This connects mitochondrial acyl-metabolism control to lysosomal clearance. The net effect can be context-dependent in cancer biology.

nodes.label: SIRT5-mediated deacetylation of LDHB
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Deacetylation of LDHB by SIRT5 hyperactivates autophagy, accelerating cellular self-digestion and influencing tumor cell survival and metabolism. The directionality is SIRT5/LDHB upstream of autophagic hyperactivation. This can support tumor cell fitness under stress but may also provoke cell-death programs. It exemplifies SIRT5's role at the autophagy–metabolism interface.

nodes.label: Hyperactivation of autophagy
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Deacetylation of LDHB by SIRT5 hyperactivates autophagy, accelerating cellular self-digestion and influencing tumor cell survival and metabolism. The directionality is SIRT5/LDHB upstream of autophagic hyperactivation. This can support tumor cell fitness under stress but may also provoke cell-death programs. It exemplifies SIRT5's role at the autophagy–metabolism interface.

nodes.label: Nkx3.2
nodes.description: SIRT6 deacetylates histone H3K9 at the promoters of Nkx3.2 and related genes, altering chromatin accessibility to regulate their transcription. The directionality is SIRT6 enzymatic chromatin repression at Nkx3.2 loci. This underlies SIRT6's control of GATA5 and ERK1/2 expression. It shows SIRT6 acting as a locus-specific transcriptional regulator.

nodes.label: GATA5
nodes.description: SIRT6 induces expression of GATA-binding protein 5 (GATA5) by deacetylating H3K9 at the Nkx3.2 promoter, preventing endothelial injury. The directionality is SIRT6 upstream of GATA5 induction. GATA5 supports endothelial integrity and opposes dysfunction. This is a vascular-protective transcriptional output of SIRT6.

nodes.label: Polyphenol stilbene (3,4',5-trihydroxystilbene)
nodes.description: Resveratrol is the polyphenolic stilbene 3,4',5-trihydroxystilbene, a plant defensive compound produced under stress such as pathogen attack or UV exposure. Its chemical structure features three phenolic hydroxyls that confer redox activity and enable binding to sirtuin and phosphodiesterase targets. The directionality is resveratrol as the small-molecule upstream activator of SIRT1. Though a weak direct antioxidant, its biological impact flows mainly through signaling modulation.

nodes.label: Grape skin
nodes.description: Resveratrol is found concentrated in grape skins, where it contributes to the anti-atherosclerotic benefits attributed to red wine consumption. The directionality is dietary resveratrol upstream of vascular protection. Skin content is modest and matrix-dependent, influencing how much reaches circulation. This botanical source motivated the 'French paradox' hypothesis.

nodes.label: Traditional East Asian medicine (Veratrum formosanum)
nodes.description: Resveratrol-containing plants such as Veratrum formosanum have long been used in traditional East Asian medicine, foreshadowing modern interest in the compound. The directionality is the traditional botanical use upstream of contemporary pharmacological study. This ethnobotanical precedent parallels other stilbene-bearing remedies. It is historical context rather than a mechanistic claim.

nodes.label: Endothelial cells from lipid damage
nodes.description: Resveratrol protects endothelial cells from lipid (e.g., oxidized-LDL) damage, helping preserve vascular barrier and nitric-oxide function. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of endothelial protection. This action is mediated through SIRT1/eNOS and antioxidant pathways. It is a foundational vascular benefit supporting resveratrol's cardiovascular reputation.

nodes.label: Vasodilation via nitric oxide synthesis modulation
nodes.description: Resveratrol promotes vasodilation by modulating nitric-oxide synthesis, principally via SIRT1-mediated activation of eNOS. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of NO-dependent relaxation. Improved vasodilation lowers vascular resistance and blood pressure. This is a direct mechanism behind its cardiovascular effects.
nodes.norm_label: vasodilation via nitric oxide synthesis modulation

nodes.label: Platelet aggregation
nodes.description: Resveratrol inhibits platelet aggregation, reducing thrombotic risk and complementing its vascular benefits. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of suppressed platelet activation. This also creates a bleeding-risk caveat when combined with anticoagulants. It is one of several anti-atherothrombotic actions of the compound.

nodes.label: Smooth muscle cell proliferation
nodes.description: Resveratrol inhibits vascular smooth-muscle cell proliferation, limiting neointimal hyperplasia and atherosclerotic plaque growth. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of suppressed VSMC expansion. This restrains the remodeling that narrows vessels. It complements its anti-platelet and vasodilatory effects.

nodes.label: Coronary relaxation
nodes.description: Resveratrol enhances coronary relaxation, reduces ventricular arrhythmias, and inhibits platelet aggregation and smooth-muscle proliferation, collectively protecting the heart. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of improved coronary function. These integrated effects support myocardial perfusion under stress. They reinforce resveratrol's cardioprotective profile.

nodes.label: Ventricular arrhythmias
nodes.description: Resveratrol reduces ventricular arrhythmias in preclinical models, likely via antioxidant, ion-channel, and eNOS-modulating actions. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of reduced arrhythmogenesis. This adds an electrophysiological benefit to its cardiovascular profile. It is observed in animal studies with uncertain human translation.

nodes.label: Glucose metabolism
nodes.description: Resveratrol improves glucose metabolism and reduces LDL while elevating HDL, improving the lipid profile in metabolic models. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of better glycemic and lipoprotein control. These effects are largely SIRT1/AMPK-dependent. Human outcomes are limited by poor bioavailability.

nodes.label: Direct antioxidant (weaker than vitamin C)
nodes.description: Resveratrol is a relatively poor direct antioxidant, weaker than vitamin C or cysteine at scavenging free radicals in vitro. The directionality is that its redox-scavenging capacity is minor. Its biological benefits therefore arise mainly from signaling modulation (SIRT1, AMPK, eNOS) rather than stoichiometric antioxidant action. This corrects the simplistic 'antioxidant' framing of resveratrol.

nodes.label: Anti-viral effects
nodes.description: Resveratrol demonstrates antiviral effects in some experimental systems, though the evidence base is moderate (confidence 0.75) and mechanism-dependent. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of viral inhibition in those models. Potential mechanisms include modulation of host stress and inflammatory pathways. Clinical relevance remains preliminary.

nodes.label: Anti-neoplastic effects
nodes.description: Resveratrol shows anti-neoplastic effects in preclinical models, including cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis induction, though confidence is moderate (0.75). The directionality is resveratrol upstream of suppressed tumor phenotype in those systems. Mechanisms may involve SIRT1, AMPK, and NF-κB modulation. Robust human anticancer efficacy is unproven.

nodes.label: Vasculature
nodes.description: SIRT1 is highly expressed in the vasculature, including endothelial and smooth-muscle cells, positioning it as a central regulator of vascular homeostasis. The directionality is constitutive vascular abundance enabling rapid SIRT1 responses to metabolic and shear stress. This expression pattern underlies its roles in vasodilation, inflammation, and atherosclerosis. Loss of vascular SIRT1 promotes endothelial dysfunction.

nodes.label: Angiogenic activity during vascular remodeling
nodes.description: SIRT1 modulates angiogenic activity during vascular remodeling and growth, influencing endothelial sprouting and vessel stability in a context-dependent manner. The directionality is SIRT1 tuning angiogenic signaling. It can either promote or restrain angiogenesis depending on oxygen and metabolic cues. This reflects SIRT1's integration of stress and metabolic inputs in the vessel wall.

nodes.label: Angiotensin II type 1 receptor expression
nodes.description: SIRT1 downregulates angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1R) expression in vascular smooth-muscle cells, reducing angiotensin-II signaling. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of AT1R suppression. Lower AT1R diminishes vasoconstriction and hypertensive signaling. This contributes to SIRT1's antihypertensive actions.

nodes.label: TIMP3 (tissue metalloproteinase 3)
nodes.description: SIRT1 regulates tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase 3 (TIMP3), an endogenous inhibitor of matrix metalloproteinases that defends against vascular inflammation and remodeling. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of TIMP3 regulation. By preserving TIMP3, SIRT1 limits extracellular-matrix degradation and inflammatory infiltration in vessels. This adds a matrix-protective dimension to SIRT1's vascular role.

nodes.label: Nuclear SIRT1 (enhanced by resveratrol)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
nodes.description: Nuclear SIRT1, enhanced by resveratrol, induces superoxide dismutase in cardiomyocytes, an antioxidant enzyme that suppresses cell death under stress. The directionality is nuclear SIRT1 upstream of SOD induction. This is a cardiomyoprotective output of resveratrol's SIRT1 activation. It complements SIRT1's eNOS and metabolic cardiac actions.

nodes.label: Superoxide dismutase in cardiomyocytes
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
nodes.description: Nuclear SIRT1, enhanced by resveratrol, induces superoxide dismutase in cardiomyocytes, an antioxidant enzyme that suppresses cell death under stress. The directionality is nuclear SIRT1 upstream of SOD induction. This is a cardiomyoprotective output of resveratrol's SIRT1 activation. It complements SIRT1's eNOS and metabolic cardiac actions.

nodes.label: SIRT3-deficient mice
nodes.description: SIRT3-deficient mice develop severe cardiac hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis when challenged with a hypertrophic stimulus, revealing SIRT3's protective role in the heart. The directionality is SIRT3 loss → pathological cardiac remodeling. This is driven by elevated ROS and impaired mitochondrial function. It mirrors the resistance seen when SIRT3 is overexpressed.

nodes.label: Severe cardiac hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis
nodes.description: SIRT3-deficient mice develop severe cardiac hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis when challenged with a hypertrophic stimulus, revealing SIRT3's protective role in the heart. The directionality is SIRT3 loss → pathological cardiac remodeling. This is driven by elevated ROS and impaired mitochondrial function. It mirrors the resistance seen when SIRT3 is overexpressed.
nodes.norm_label: severe cardiac hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis

nodes.label: SIRT3-overexpressing mice
nodes.description: Transgenic mice overexpressing SIRT3 are significantly resistant to stimuli-induced cardiac hypertrophy, the inverse of the SIRT3-null phenotype. The directionality is SIRT3 gain → hypertrophy resistance. This protection arises from better mitochondrial ROS control and metabolic flexibility. It validates SIRT3 as a cardiac therapeutic target.

nodes.label: Stimuli-induced cardiac hypertrophy
nodes.description: Transgenic mice overexpressing SIRT3 are significantly resistant to stimuli-induced cardiac hypertrophy, the inverse of the SIRT3-null phenotype. The directionality is SIRT3 gain → hypertrophy resistance. This protection arises from better mitochondrial ROS control and metabolic flexibility. It validates SIRT3 as a cardiac therapeutic target.

nodes.label: SIRT7-deficient mice
nodes.description: SIRT7-deficient mice show extensive myocardial fibrosis, high basal apoptosis, and cardiomyopathy, reflecting SIRT7's role in maintaining cardiac homeostasis. The directionality is SIRT7 loss → fibrotic cardiomyopathy. This contrasts with contexts where SIRT7 promotes fibrosis under stress. It indicates SIRT7 is overall required for myocardial integrity.

nodes.label: Extensive myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyopathy
nodes.description: SIRT7-deficient mice show extensive myocardial fibrosis, high basal apoptosis, and cardiomyopathy, reflecting SIRT7's role in maintaining cardiac homeostasis. The directionality is SIRT7 loss → fibrotic cardiomyopathy. This contrasts with contexts where SIRT7 promotes fibrosis under stress. It indicates SIRT7 is overall required for myocardial integrity.

nodes.label: Red wine matrix
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
nodes.description: Resveratrol achieves efficacious levels only when ingested within the red-wine matrix, which contains co-constituents that slow its metabolism and improve exposure. The directionality is matrix components upstream of better resveratrol bioavailability. This helps resolve discrepancies between in vitro potency and in vivo human trials. It supports whole-food over isolated-compound approaches.

nodes.label: Resveratrol bioavailability
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
nodes.description: Resveratrol achieves efficacious levels only when ingested within the red-wine matrix, which contains co-constituents that slow its metabolism and improve exposure. The directionality is matrix components upstream of better resveratrol bioavailability. This helps resolve discrepancies between in vitro potency and in vivo human trials. It supports whole-food over isolated-compound approaches.

nodes.label: ~8–14 minutes
nodes.description: Resveratrol has a very short plasma half-life of roughly 8–14 minutes because of rapid conjugation and clearance. The directionality is rapid metabolism upstream of low systemic exposure. This severely limits the duration of any SIRT1 activation after a single dose. Sustained-release or matrix strategies are needed for durable effects.

nodes.label: Cytochrome P450
nodes.description: Hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes contribute to resveratrol catabolism, alongside phase-II conjugation, determining its metabolic fate. The directionality is CYP enzymes upstream of resveratrol clearance. This hepatic handling caps bioavailability. It is relevant to drug–drug interactions and dosing.

nodes.label: Cytochrome P450 activity
nodes.description: Resveratrol both is metabolized by and inhibits cytochrome P450 activity, creating a self-reinforcing effect on its own clearance and on co-administered drugs. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of CYP inhibition. This can alter the pharmacokinetics of other medications. It is a clinically relevant interaction caveat.

nodes.label: Quercetin and ethanol
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
nodes.description: Quercetin and ethanol, red-wine constituents, augment resveratrol activity possibly by inhibiting its catabolic enzymes and improving exposure (moderate confidence 0.75). The directionality is these co-compounds upstream of enhanced resveratrol effect. This helps explain the matrix/bioavailability phenomenon. It suggests combination formulations could improve efficacy.

nodes.label: Resveratrol activity
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
nodes.description: Quercetin and ethanol, red-wine constituents, augment resveratrol activity possibly by inhibiting its catabolic enzymes and improving exposure (moderate confidence 0.75). The directionality is these co-compounds upstream of enhanced resveratrol effect. This helps explain the matrix/bioavailability phenomenon. It suggests combination formulations could improve efficacy.

nodes.label: French Paradox
nodes.description: The French paradox describes lower cardiovascular-disease incidence in some French populations despite high-fat diets, often attributed in part to moderate wine (and resveratrol) consumption. The directionality is moderate wine intake upstream of reduced CVD in this epidemiological observation. Causality is debated, with diet and lifestyle confounders. Resveratrol's vascular actions provide a plausible—but not proven—mechanism.

nodes.label: Reduced CVD incidence with moderate wine consumption despite high-fat diet
nodes.description: The French paradox describes lower cardiovascular-disease incidence in some French populations despite high-fat diets, often attributed in part to moderate wine (and resveratrol) consumption. The directionality is moderate wine intake upstream of reduced CVD in this epidemiological observation. Causality is debated, with diet and lifestyle confounders. Resveratrol's vascular actions provide a plausible—but not proven—mechanism.
nodes.norm_label: reduced cvd incidence with moderate wine consumption despite high-fat diet

nodes.label: Bleeding risk with concurrent anticoagulant use
nodes.description: Because resveratrol inhibits platelet aggregation, concurrent use with anticoagulants such as heparin or warfarin may increase bleeding risk. The directionality is resveratrol plus anticoagulant upstream of heightened bleeding liability. This is a practical safety caveat for supplementation. Clinicians advise caution in anticoagulated patients.
nodes.norm_label: bleeding risk with concurrent anticoagulant use

nodes.label: SIRT1 downregulation of angiotensin II type 1 receptor
nodes.description: SIRT1-mediated downregulation of AT1R expression produces antihypertensive effects; in vivo, resveratrol-driven SIRT1 elevation reduces angiotensin-II-induced hypertension. The directionality is SIRT1/AT1R suppression upstream of lower blood pressure. This couples SIRT1 activation to vascular tone control. It is a mechanistic basis for resveratrol's antihypertensive actions.
nodes.norm_label: sirt1 downregulation of angiotensin ii type 1 receptor

nodes.label: Anti-hypertensive effects
nodes.description: SIRT1-mediated downregulation of AT1R expression produces antihypertensive effects; in vivo, resveratrol-driven SIRT1 elevation reduces angiotensin-II-induced hypertension. The directionality is SIRT1/AT1R suppression upstream of lower blood pressure. This couples SIRT1 activation to vascular tone control. It is a mechanistic basis for resveratrol's antihypertensive actions.

nodes.label: Beclin1
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates Beclin-1 at multiple lysines, promoting its interaction with the class III PI3K Vps34 and enhancing autophagy initiation and flux. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic licensing of Beclin-1. This supports autophagosome formation and cellular clearance. It is a central SIRT1 autophagy substrate alongside LC3, Atg5, Atg7, and ULK1.

nodes.label: FoxO1 (pancreatic β cells)
nodes.description: In pancreatic β-cells, SIRT6 deacetylates FoxO1 and increases GLUT2 expression to maintain glucose-sensing ability and systemic glucose tolerance. The directionality is SIRT6 enzymatic activation of FoxO1 in β-cells. This preserves insulin secretory competence under metabolic challenge. It mirrors SIRT6's broader metabolic-protective phenotype.

nodes.label: Nrf2 (via Keap1 modification)
nodes.description: SIRT1 activates Nrf2 by modifying Keap1 structure, leading to Nrf2 nuclear translocation and expression of antioxidant genes. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of Nrf2 activation. This is a canonical cytoprotective axis against oxidative and electrophilic insult. It complements SIRT1's direct antioxidant substrate actions.

nodes.label: CPS1
nodes.description: SIRT5 desuccinylates and activates carbamoyl phosphate synthase 1 (CPS1), the rate-limiting enzyme of the urea cycle, enhancing ammonia detoxification into urea. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of CPS1. This is especially important during fasting or high-protein load when nitrogen must be cleared. It exemplifies SIRT5's role as a regulator of mitochondrial acyl-metabolism and nitrogen homeostasis.

nodes.label: NLRP3 inflammasome (via AMPKα/XBP1)
nodes.description: SIRT1 protects against inflammation by deacetylating and attenuating NLRP3 activity via the AMPKα/XBP1 pathway in macrophages. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic suppression of NLRP3 through XBP1s. This couples ER-stress responses to innate immune regulation. It is a refined mechanistic view of SIRT1's anti-inflammasome action.

nodes.label: Heart failure (via SERCA2a deacetylation)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates SERCA2a at Lys492, restoring its activity and improving cardiac contractility in heart failure. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic rescue of SERCA2a. Better calcium handling opposes the systolic dysfunction of failure. This is a direct mechanistic rationale for SIRT1 activation in cardiomyopathy.

nodes.label: TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling
nodes.description: SIRT6 prevents TGF-β1-induced lung myofibroblast differentiation by inactivating TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling, limiting fibrogenesis. The directionality is SIRT6 upstream of TGF-β1/Smad3 blockade. This complements SIRT6's other antifibrotic actions in heart and kidney. It positions SIRT6 as a broad suppressor of Smad3-driven fibrosis.

nodes.label: MFN2 (at K655, K662)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates mitofusin 2 (MFN2) at Lys655 and Lys662, regulating mitochondrial fusion and quality control; loss of SIRT1 causes defective autophagy linked to impaired MFN2 function. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic modification of MFN2. This connects sirtuin activity to mitochondrial dynamics and mitophagy. It is relevant to neurodegenerative and metabolic disease where fusion is perturbed.

nodes.label: p53 at Lys379
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates p53 specifically at Lys379, inhibiting p53-dependent apoptosis and promoting cell survival under genotoxic stress. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic inactivation of p53 at this site. This is one of several lysines (including Lys317/370) targeted by SIRT1. The net effect is cytoprotection that can be oncogenic in established tumors.

nodes.label: AMPK (preadipocyte differentiation)
nodes.description: SIRT5 inhibits preadipocyte differentiation by activating AMPK and repressing MAPK signaling, analogous to its broader adipogenesis-blocking role. The directionality is SIRT5 upstream of AMPK activation in adipogenic progenitors. Activated AMPK shifts cells away from lipogenesis. It reaffirms SIRT5 as a negative regulator of fat formation.

nodes.label: Nicotinamide to NMN
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: NAMPT condenses nicotinamide with 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP) to form NMN, the rate-limiting step of the NAD+ salvage pathway. The directionality is NAMPT upstream of NMN/NAD+ biosynthesis. This recovers nicotinamide that would otherwise feedback-inhibit sirtuins. AMPK and SIRT1 both induce NAMPT, creating a positive loop for NAD+ and sirtuin activity.

nodes.label: TGF-beta1
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: TGF-β1 binds the type II receptor (TβRII), which recruits and phosphorylates the type I receptor (TβRI), leading to phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of SMAD2/3 to drive fibrotic transcription. The directionality is TGF-β1 upstream of SMAD3 activation. This canonical pathway is the main driver of pathological fibrosis across organs. Sirtuins such as SIRT6 and SIRT7 intersect this axis at multiple points.

nodes.label: SMAD3
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: TGF-β1 binds the type II receptor (TβRII), which recruits and phosphorylates the type I receptor (TβRI), leading to phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of SMAD2/3 to drive fibrotic transcription. The directionality is TGF-β1 upstream of SMAD3 activation. This canonical pathway is the main driver of pathological fibrosis across organs. Sirtuins such as SIRT6 and SIRT7 intersect this axis at multiple points.

nodes.label: Pathological fibrosis
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: TGF-β1 activates SMAD3-dependent transcription of pro-fibrotic genes (COL1A1, COL3A1, FN1, ACTA2, TIMP1), driving collagen deposition and tissue scarring in multiple organs. The directionality is TGF-β1 upstream of fibrogenesis. This makes TGF-β1 a central target in fibrosis therapeutics. Sirtuins that inhibit SMAD3 signaling (SIRT6, SIRT7) are antifibrotic.

nodes.label: BRCA1
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: BRCA1 is recruited to DNA double-strand breaks by the MRN complex, promotes end resection, and facilitates RAD51 loading via PALB2/BRCA2 to execute homologous recombination repair. The directionality is BRCA1 upstream of high-fidelity DSB repair. Loss of BRCA1 cripples HR, increasing mutation and cancer risk. Sirtuins such as SIRT2 support BRCA1 localization to damage sites.

nodes.label: Homologous recombination repair
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: BRCA1 is recruited to DNA double-strand breaks by the MRN complex, promotes end resection, and facilitates RAD51 loading via PALB2/BRCA2 to execute homologous recombination repair. The directionality is BRCA1 upstream of high-fidelity DSB repair. Loss of BRCA1 cripples HR, increasing mutation and cancer risk. Sirtuins such as SIRT2 support BRCA1 localization to damage sites.

nodes.label: BRCA1 deficiency
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Loss of BRCA1 triggers increased autophagy as a compensatory survival mechanism in breast and ovarian cancers, buffering the viability impact of defective homologous recombination. The directionality is BRCA1 deficiency upstream of autophagic upregulation. This metabolic rewiring can be co-opted by tumors. It connects genome-maintenance failure to lysosomal clearance pathways.

nodes.label: Compensatory autophagy
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Loss of BRCA1 triggers increased autophagy as a compensatory survival mechanism in breast and ovarian cancers, buffering the viability impact of defective homologous recombination. The directionality is BRCA1 deficiency upstream of autophagic upregulation. This metabolic rewiring can be co-opted by tumors. It connects genome-maintenance failure to lysosomal clearance pathways.

nodes.label: BRCA1 mutation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
