nodes.description: BRCA1-deficient tumors are exquisitely sensitive to PARP inhibitors because blocking base-excision (PARP) repair in the setting of defective homologous recombination causes catastrophic, lethal DNA damage (synthetic lethality). The directionality is BRCA1 mutation upstream of PARP-inhibitor vulnerability. This is a cornerstone of precision oncology. It illustrates how repair-pathway context determines therapeutic selectivity.

nodes.label: PARP inhibitors (synthetic lethality)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: BRCA1-deficient tumors are exquisitely sensitive to PARP inhibitors because blocking base-excision (PARP) repair in the setting of defective homologous recombination causes catastrophic, lethal DNA damage (synthetic lethality). The directionality is BRCA1 mutation upstream of PARP-inhibitor vulnerability. This is a cornerstone of precision oncology. It illustrates how repair-pathway context determines therapeutic selectivity.

nodes.label: Caspase-3 (at Ser150)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: p38 MAPK phosphorylates caspase-3 at Ser150, suppressing its proteolytic activity; this inhibition is reversed by the phosphatase PP2A. The directionality is p38 upstream of caspase-3 inhibition. This provides a survival signal that tempers apoptosis under certain stresses. It shows stress kinases can directly restrain executioner caspases.

nodes.label: ULK1, ATG13, FIP200, ATG101
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: ULK1 functions within a stable initiation complex containing ATG13, FIP200 (RB1CC1), and ATG101, which nucleates autophagosome formation in response to nutrient status. The directionality is the complex upstream of autophagy initiation. SIRT1 deacetylates and activates ULK1 within this complex. This positions sirtuins at the top of the autophagic machinery.

nodes.label: ULK1 (at Ser757)
nodes.description: Under nutrient-rich conditions, mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 at Ser757, disrupting its interaction with AMPK and suppressing autophagy. The directionality is mTORC1 upstream of ULK1 inhibition. This couples nutrient abundance to autophagic restraint. Sirtuin/AMPK activation opposes mTORC1 to relicense ULK1.

nodes.label: STRAD and MO25 for activity
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: LKB1 requires binding to STRAD and MO25 to exit the nucleus and gain full kinase activity; without this scaffold it remains inactive. The directionality is STRAD/MO25 upstream of LKB1 activation. SIRT1/AMPK deacetylate/phosphorylate LKB1 to modulate its localization. This gating is essential for LKB1's role as the master AMPK kinase.

nodes.label: Thr172
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: LKB1 is the primary upstream kinase phosphorylating AMPK at Thr172 in the activation loop, increasing AMPK activity over a hundred-fold. The directionality is LKB1 upstream of AMPK activation. This couples energy sensing to metabolic reprogramming. Sirtuins feed into this node via LKB1 deacetylation and AMPK-dependent NAD+ elevation.

nodes.label: LKB1 deficiency
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Germline loss-of-function mutations in STK11 (LKB1) cause Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, characterized by hamartomatous polyps and elevated cancer risk. The directionality is LKB1 deficiency upstream of this cancer predisposition. This highlights LKB1 as a critical tumor suppressor and metabolic regulator. Its connection to AMPK/sirtuin axes explains the metabolic features.

nodes.label: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Germline loss-of-function mutations in STK11 (LKB1) cause Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, characterized by hamartomatous polyps and elevated cancer risk. The directionality is LKB1 deficiency upstream of this cancer predisposition. This highlights LKB1 as a critical tumor suppressor and metabolic regulator. Its connection to AMPK/sirtuin axes explains the metabolic features.

nodes.label: Beclin1 BH3 domain
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: The BH3 domain of Beclin1 binds anti-apoptotic Bcl-2/Bcl-xL proteins, which sequester it and inhibit autophagy, linking apoptosis and autophagy regulation. The directionality is Bcl-2 upstream of Beclin1 sequestration. SIRT1 deacetylation of Beclin1 modulates this interaction. This illustrates the molecular crosstalk between cell-death and clearance pathways.

nodes.label: Bcl-2 anti-apoptotic proteins
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: The BH3 domain of Beclin1 binds anti-apoptotic Bcl-2/Bcl-xL proteins, which sequester it and inhibit autophagy, linking apoptosis and autophagy regulation. The directionality is Bcl-2 upstream of Beclin1 sequestration. SIRT1 deacetylation of Beclin1 modulates this interaction. This illustrates the molecular crosstalk between cell-death and clearance pathways.

nodes.label: Four distinct class III PI3K complexes
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Beclin1 scaffolds four class III PI3K complexes (I/Atg14L, II/UVRAG, III/UVRAG+Rubicon, IV/Bif-1) that regulate autophagy at initiation, nucleation, and maturation stages. The directionality is Beclin1 upstream of autophagosome machinery assembly. SIRT1 deacetylates Beclin1 to enhance Vps34 activity. This makes Beclin1 a hub integrating sirtuin signals into autophagy.
nodes.norm_label: four distinct class iii pi3k complexes

nodes.label: Tumour suppressor (glutamine metabolism)
nodes.description: SIRT4 acts as a tumor suppressor by inhibiting GDH and restricting glutamine-derived anaplerosis into the TCA cycle, starving cancer cells of carbon for proliferation. The directionality is SIRT4 upstream of suppressed glutamine metabolism. This limits the glutamine addiction of tumors. It is a context where SIRT4 opposes, rather than promotes, growth.

nodes.label: MTPα (fatty acid oxidation)
nodes.description: SIRT4 suppresses fatty-acid oxidation in liver by inhibiting the mitochondrial trifunctional protein α subunit (MTPα), promoting lipid accumulation under nutrient-replete conditions. The directionality is SIRT4 upstream of reduced β-oxidation. This contrasts with SIRT3/SIRT5, which support fat oxidation. It positions SIRT4 as a mitochondrial anabolic brake.

nodes.label: H3K18ac
nodes.description: SIRT7 possesses NAD+-dependent deacetylase activity with high selectivity for histone H3 lysine 18 acetylation (H3K18ac), a mark of active transcription at rDNA and elsewhere. The directionality is SIRT7 enzymatic removal of H3K18ac. Deacetylation at pericentric heterochromatin maintains genomic stability and silences repetitive elements. This substrate specificity underlies SIRT7's roles in ribosome biogenesis and chromatin integrity.

nodes.label: Replicative lifespan
nodes.description: Overexpression of SIRT7 extends the replicative lifespan of primary human cells by maintaining rDNA stability and reducing mitochondrial dysfunction. The directionality is SIRT7 gain upstream of prolonged cellular lifespan. This mirrors the pro-longevity roles of other sirtuins. It supports a broadly conserved lifespan-promoting function for the family.

nodes.label: 1.5 to 3 mg per liter
nodes.description: Typical red wine contains 1.5–3 mg/L trans-resveratrol (up to ~5.8 mg/L in some cool-climate wines), with a 5-ounce glass providing only ~0.3 mg. The directionality is wine content upstream of modest resveratrol intake. This low dose highlights why drinking alone may not reach pharmacologic exposures. It contextualizes the 'French paradox' and matrix-bioavailability discussion.

nodes.label: 0.15 to 1.3 mg per 100g
nodes.description: Raw red grapes contain roughly 0.15–1.3 mg resveratrol per 100 g, mostly in the skins, making dietary intake from fruit modest. The directionality is grape content upstream of limited resveratrol exposure. Skin concentration explains why wine, not flesh, carries most of the compound. It reinforces that supplementation, not diet alone, reaches high doses.

nodes.label: Vine Tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata)
nodes.description: Vine tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata) leaves contain 20–30% dihydromyricetin (DHM) by weight, so 1–1.5 g dry leaf suffices for a ~300 mg therapeutic dose. The directionality is botanical source upstream of DHM availability. DHM is a potent SIRT3/AMPK activator. This makes vine tea a practical natural source of the compound.

nodes.label: Cyanidin-3-glucoside
nodes.description: Black elderberries provide roughly 350–450 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100 g fresh fruit, with ~70–85 g reaching a 300 mg therapeutic dose. The directionality is berry content upstream of anthocyanin intake. Cyanidin is a powerful natural SIRT6 activator. It positions elderberry as a dietary SIRT6-modulating food.

nodes.label: 350 to 450 mg per 100g
nodes.description: Black elderberries provide roughly 350–450 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100 g fresh fruit, with ~70–85 g reaching a 300 mg therapeutic dose. The directionality is berry content upstream of anthocyanin intake. Cyanidin is a powerful natural SIRT6 activator. It positions elderberry as a dietary SIRT6-modulating food.

nodes.label: Water
nodes.description: Honokiol is highly lipophilic with very poor water solubility, so hot-water tea extraction is inefficient and ethanol tinctures or supercritical CO2 extracts are needed for therapeutic dosing. The directionality is physicochemical property upstream of formulation requirement. Its lipophilicity also aids cell and mitochondrial membrane penetration, supporting SIRT3 engagement. This is a practical caveat for honokiol use.

nodes.label: Dual mechanism (direct + indirect)
nodes.description: Resveratrol activates SIRT1 through both direct allosteric binding at the NTD (Glu230) and an indirect cascade via PDE4/cAMP/Epac1/Ca2+/CaMKKβ/AMPK/NAMPT/NAD+. The directionality is resveratrol upstream of dual SIRT1 activation. The indirect limb raises NAD+ to fuel SIRT1, amplifying the direct effect. This dual mechanism explains resveratrol's robust pleiotropic metabolic benefits.

nodes.label: Tenovin-6
nodes.description: Tenovin-6 inhibits SIRT2 with IC50 = 10 µM, making SIRT2 its more potent sirtuin target compared with SIRT1. The directionality is Tenovin-6 blocking SIRT2 catalysis. By inhibiting SIRT2 deacetylation, it can protect neurons and reactivate p53. It is a chemical probe distinguishing SIRT2 from other sirtuins.

nodes.label: Tenovins
nodes.description: By inhibiting SIRT1/SIRT2-mediated deacetylation, Tenovins promote p53 hyperacetylation and reactivation of p53-dependent transcriptional networks. The directionality is Tenovin-mediated sirtuin inhibition upstream of p53 activation. This restores p53 tumor-suppressive function in cells where sirtuins silence it. It is the basis for Tenovins' anticancer activity.

nodes.label: p53 (via hyperacetylation)
nodes.description: By inhibiting SIRT1/SIRT2-mediated deacetylation, Tenovins promote p53 hyperacetylation and reactivation of p53-dependent transcriptional networks. The directionality is Tenovin-mediated sirtuin inhibition upstream of p53 activation. This restores p53 tumor-suppressive function in cells where sirtuins silence it. It is the basis for Tenovins' anticancer activity.

nodes.label: Xenograft models
nodes.description: Tenovin-1 and Tenovin-6 significantly delay tumor growth in human cancer mouse xenografts (BL2 and ARN8) at single-digit micromolar concentrations. The directionality is Tenovin treatment upstream of reduced tumor growth. This effect is attributed to p53 reactivation and sirtuin inhibition. It validates sirtuin inhibition as an anticancer strategy in p53-wild-type tumors.

nodes.label: Splitomicin
nodes.description: Splitomicin inhibits human SIRT1 with IC50 = 96 µM in vitro by blocking NAD+-dependent deacetylation. The directionality is Splitomicin upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It is an early-tool sirtuin inhibitor used to probe SIRT1 phenotypes. Its moderate potency limits in vivo utility.

nodes.label: NF-κB p65
nodes.description: Splitomicin reduces intracellular deacetylase activity, causing hyperacetylation and enhanced nuclear translocation of NF-κB p65, amplifying inflammatory transcription. The directionality is Splitomicin (sirtuin inhibition) upstream of increased NF-κB signaling. This demonstrates the converse of SIRT1's normal anti-inflammatory action. It shows experimentally that sirtuin tone sets inflammatory set-points.

nodes.label: Ischemic preconditioning cardioprotection
nodes.description: In ischemic-preconditioning models, Splitomicin reverses protective lysine deacetylation and abolishes preconditioning-induced cardioprotection. The directionality is Splitomicin (sirtuin inhibition) upstream of lost cardiac protection. This indicates sirtuin deacetylase activity is required for ischemic tolerance. It argues that sirtuin activation, not inhibition, protects the heart.

nodes.label: Cambinol
nodes.description: Cambinol inhibits human SIRT1 with IC50 = 56 µM by blocking access to both NAD+ and acetyl-lysine substrate-binding regions. The directionality is Cambinol upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It also inhibits SIRT2, with minimal activity against SIRT3 or class I/II HDACs. Cambinol sensitizes cancer cells to chemotherapy and suppresses invasion.

nodes.label: Cancer cell migration and invasion
nodes.description: In hepatocellular and lung cancer cells, Cambinol impairs migration and invasion in a dose-dependent manner, consistent with sirtuin inhibition reducing metastatic behaviors. The directionality is Cambinol upstream of suppressed motility. This suggests sirtuin blockers may limit metastasis. It complements Cambinol's chemotherapy-sensitizing effects.

nodes.label: Cancer cells to chemotherapy
nodes.description: Cambinol combination with chemotherapeutic agents dramatically sensitizes cancer cells to chemotherapy-induced apoptosis. The directionality is Cambinol upstream of enhanced chemosensitivity. By inhibiting SIRT1/2, it removes survival signals that protect tumor cells. This supports sirtuin inhibition as a chemosensitization strategy.

nodes.label: Salermide
nodes.description: Salermide is a potent synthetic sirtuin inhibitor with improved potency against SIRT1 relative to the parent compound sirtinol. The directionality is Salermide blocking SIRT1 deacetylase activity. This reactivates proapoptotic genes silenced by SIRT1 in cancer. It is a research and anticancer chemical probe.

nodes.label: Proapoptotic genes (via H4K16ac)
nodes.description: Salermide inhibits SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of H4K16, leading to epigenetic reactivation of proapoptotic genes aberrantly repressed in cancer cells. The directionality is Salermide → H4K16 hyperacetylation → apoptosis gene expression. This removes a chromatin-based survival brake. It is a mechanistic rationale for sirtuin-inhibitor cancer therapy.

nodes.label: Cancer cell lines (MOLT4, MDA-MB-231, RKO)
nodes.description: Salermide induces robust apoptosis in leukemia (MOLT4), breast (MDA-MB-231), and colon (RKO) cancer cells, validating broad antitumor activity. The directionality is Salermide treatment upstream of cancer-cell death. This is consistent with SIRT1/2 inhibition removing survival signaling. It supports sirtuin blockers as anticancer agents.

nodes.label: Colorectal cancer stem cells
nodes.description: Salermide inhibits colorectal carcinoma cancer-stem-cell self-renewal and reduces tumorigenesis, targeting the resilient stem-cell fraction. The directionality is Salermide upstream of stem-cell suppression. This is important because stem cells drive relapse. It extends sirtuin-inhibitor effects to the tumor-initiation compartment.

nodes.label: Sirtinol
nodes.description: Sirtinol inhibits SIRT1 with IC50 ≈ 131 µM, preventing deacetylation of histones and non-histone targets. The directionality is Sirtinol upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It is the parent compound of salermide and a classic sirtuin research tool. Its weaker potency spurred development of derivatives like salermide.

nodes.label: Senescence-like growth arrest
nodes.description: Sirtinol induces senescence-like growth arrest in human lung cancer H1299 cells, consistent with sirtuin inhibition engaging tumor-suppressive programs. The directionality is Sirtinol upstream of growth arrest. This phenotype mirrors aspects of SIRT1 loss. It suggests sirtuin blockers can blunt proliferation.

nodes.label: Apoptotic and autophagic cell death (MCF-7)
nodes.description: In MCF-7 breast cancer cells, sirtinol triggers both apoptotic and autophagic programmed cell death, reflecting disrupted survival homeostasis. The directionality is Sirtinol upstream of dual cell-death activation. This is attributed to SIRT1/2 inhibition removing anti-apoptotic deacetylation. It illustrates the pleiotropic anticancer potential of sirtuin blockers.

nodes.label: CD38 inhibitor 78c
nodes.description: 78c is a highly potent, selective, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of CD38 NAD+-glycohydrolase activity. The directionality is 78c upstream of CD38 blockade. By stopping NAD+ consumption, it spares the co-substrate for sirtuins. This is a leading age-reversal NAD+-preservation strategy.

nodes.label: CD38 (NAD+-glycohydrolase)
nodes.description: 78c is a highly potent, selective, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of CD38 NAD+-glycohydrolase activity. The directionality is 78c upstream of CD38 blockade. By stopping NAD+ consumption, it spares the co-substrate for sirtuins. This is a leading age-reversal NAD+-preservation strategy.

nodes.label: NAD+ levels
nodes.description: By selectively inhibiting CD38, 78c prevents age-related NAD+ degradation, keeping cellular pools high in aged animals. The directionality is CD38 inhibition upstream of preserved NAD+. Higher NAD+ then fuels sirtuin and other NAD+-dependent enzymes. This reverses a hallmark of aging.

nodes.label: Sirtuin activity (SIRT1, SIRT3)
nodes.description: 78c indirectly boosts SIRT1 and SIRT3 by maintaining NAD+ co-substrate availability, restoring their deacetylase function in aged tissue. The directionality is NAD+ preservation upstream of sirtuin reactivation. This is an indirect 'pan-sirtuin' approach distinct from direct STACs. It links CD38 pharmacology to longevity pathways.

Administration of 78c to naturally aged male mice yields about a 14% lifespan extension, demonstrating in vivo geroprotective efficacy. The directionality is CD38 inhibition upstream of prolonged lifespan. This effect is attributed to restored NAD+/sirtuin function. It validates CD38 as a longevity drug target.

nodes.label: NMN and NR
nodes.description: 78c enhances the efficacy of NAD+ precursors NMN and NR by preventing their rapid CD38-mediated degradation, combining supply and preservation. The directionality is 78c + precursors upstream of amplified NAD+ and sirtuin activation. This synergy is a rational anti-aging combination. It overcomes the limited durability of precursors alone.

nodes.label: Fucoidan
nodes.description: Fucoidan (notably Fucoidan-FV) activates SIRT6 by increasing its protein abundance and enhancing its mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity. The directionality is fucoidan upstream of SIRT6 activation. Unlike most SIRT6 activators, it preferentially stimulates the ADP-ribosyltransferase function. This yields antifibrotic and LINE-1-suppressing effects.

nodes.label: LINE-1 expression (HGPS fibroblasts)
nodes.description: Fucoidan-FV (50–100 µg/mL) reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria (HGPS) patient-derived fibroblasts, indicating suppressed retrotransposition. The directionality is fucoidan/SIRT6 upstream of LINE-1 silencing. This addresses a progeria-associated chromatin defect. It supports SIRT6 in repetitive-element control.

nodes.label: Healthspan and lifespan (aged mice)
nodes.description: SIRT6-activating fucoidan extends healthspan and lifespan in aged wild-type mice, confirming in vivo geroprotection. The directionality is fucoidan upstream of improved survival and function. This mirrors the longevity association of centenarian SIRT6 variants. It positions fucoidan as a natural SIRT6-targeted intervention.

nodes.label: ML385
nodes.description: ML385 binds the NRF2 bZIP domain, blocking its heterodimerization with small Maf proteins and preventing ARE-driven antioxidant transcription. The directionality is ML385 upstream of NRF2 inhibition. Because SIRT1 activates NRF2, ML385 can be used to disrupt that axis experimentally. It is a tool to dissect NRF2-dependent cytoprotection.

nodes.label: AGK2
nodes.description: AGK2 is a highly selective SIRT2 inhibitor (IC50 = 3.5 µM) with over 10-fold selectivity over SIRT1 and SIRT3. The directionality is AGK2 blocking SIRT2. Its selectivity makes it the preferred probe for SIRT2-specific biology. It rescues neurons in Parkinson's models, supporting SIRT2 inhibition therapeutically.

nodes.label: α-synuclein-mediated toxicity
nodes.description: AGK2-mediated SIRT2 inhibition prevents deacetylation of α-tubulin and microtubule elements, suppressing aggregation and protecting dopaminergic neuron viability in Parkinson's models. The directionality is AGK2/SIRT2 inhibition upstream of neuronal rescue. This targets the microtubule instability underlying synuclein toxicity. It is a leading SIRT2-inhibition neurodegenerative strategy.

nodes.label: Ischemic stroke
nodes.description: AGK2 confers neuroprotection under ischemic/hypoxic conditions by suppressing phospho-JNK and FOXO3a and preventing caspase-3 cleavage. The directionality is AGK2/SIRT2 inhibition upstream of reduced neuronal death. This broadens AGK2's neuroprotective utility beyond proteinopathy. It reinforces the inverse therapeutic logic for SIRT2.

nodes.label: SIRT6 centenarian variants (N308K/A313S)
nodes.description: Centenarian-associated SIRT6 variants (N308K/A313S) elevate endogenous SIRT6 protein through a weakened interaction with vimentin, independent of mRNA changes. The directionality is variant → reduced vimentin binding → higher SIRT6. This suggests protein stability, not expression, drives the longevity phenotype. It links a human genetic finding to SIRT6 abundance.

nodes.label: SIRT6 protein levels
nodes.description: Centenarian-associated SIRT6 variants (N308K/A313S) elevate endogenous SIRT6 protein through a weakened interaction with vimentin, independent of mRNA changes. The directionality is variant → reduced vimentin binding → higher SIRT6. This suggests protein stability, not expression, drives the longevity phenotype. It links a human genetic finding to SIRT6 abundance.

nodes.label: SIRT6 N308K mutation
nodes.description: The N308K substitution selectively reduces SIRT6–vimentin interaction, which normally promotes SIRT6 degradation, thereby increasing SIRT6 protein levels. The directionality is N308K upstream of weakened vimentin binding. This stabilizes SIRT6 and enhances its functional output. It is the molecular explanation for the centenarian variant phenotype.

nodes.label: Vimentin
nodes.description: The N308K substitution selectively reduces SIRT6–vimentin interaction, which normally promotes SIRT6 degradation, thereby increasing SIRT6 protein levels. The directionality is N308K upstream of weakened vimentin binding. This stabilizes SIRT6 and enhances its functional output. It is the molecular explanation for the centenarian variant phenotype.

nodes.label: SIRT6 deacetylase activity
nodes.description: Despite higher SIRT6 protein, centenarian hMSCs show increased histone acetylation at H3K9, H3K18, and H3K27, confirming reduced deacetylase activity. The directionality is variant upstream of weaker deacetylation. This indicates the longevity benefit may hinge more on ADP-ribosyltransferase than deacetylase function. It reframes how 'active' SIRT6 should be interpreted.

nodes.label: Replicative senescence (hMSCs)
nodes.description: At late passages, centenarian-variant hMSCs show more Ki67-positive proliferating cells and fewer SA-β-gal-positive senescent cells, demonstrating delayed replicative senescence. The directionality is CentSIRT6 upstream of senescence delay. This is a cellular correlate of exceptional human longevity. It supports SIRT6 as a senescence-modulating factor.

nodes.label: Progerin-induced stress
nodes.description: Centenarian SIRT6 variants ameliorate multiple aging phenotypes in progerin-expressing hMSCs: higher Ki67, reduced SA-β-gal, decreased p16/p21, reduced IL-6, and increased Lamin B1. The directionality is CentSIRT6 upstream of progerin-stress resistance. This shows the variant buffers premature-aging (HGPS) pathology. It ties SIRT6 to laminopathy resilience.

nodes.label: LINE-1 derepression (under progerin stress)
nodes.description: Under progerin-induced stress, centenarian-variant hMSCs better maintain LINE-1 repression, with reduced ORF1p and ORF2p proteins. The directionality is CentSIRT6 upstream of continued LINE-1 silencing. This protects genome integrity against retrotransposition. It connects the ADP-ribosyltransferase gain to repetitive-element control.

nodes.label: AAV-CentSIRT6
nodes.description: AAV-mediated delivery of centenarian SIRT6 reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts, validating the variant's silencing function in progeria. The directionality is CentSIRT6 expression upstream of LINE-1 reduction. This is a proof-of-concept gene-therapy approach to laminopathy. It extends the SIRT6/LINE-1 axis to a treatable model.

nodes.label: LINE-1 in HGPS fibroblasts
nodes.description: AAV-mediated delivery of centenarian SIRT6 reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts, validating the variant's silencing function in progeria. The directionality is CentSIRT6 expression upstream of LINE-1 reduction. This is a proof-of-concept gene-therapy approach to laminopathy. It extends the SIRT6/LINE-1 axis to a treatable model.

nodes.label: KAP1
nodes.description: SIRT6 mono-ADP-ribosylates KAP1 (a transcriptional corepressor), a modification that licenses recruitment of heterochromatin protein HP1α to repetitive DNA. The directionality is SIRT6 enzymatic ADP-ribosylation of KAP1. This is distinct from its deacetylase action and is selectively enhanced by fucoidan and centenarian variants. It is a key chromatin-silencing mechanism.

nodes.label: SIRT6/KAP1
nodes.description: SIRT6-mediated mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1 recruits HP1α to package LINE-1 retrotransposons into heterochromatin, silencing their expression. The directionality is SIRT6/KAP1 upstream of HP1α tethering. This protects genome stability by containing mobile elements. It explains how SIRT6 loss derepresses LINE-1.

nodes.label: HP1alpha (to LINE-1 heterochromatin)
nodes.description: SIRT6-mediated mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1 recruits HP1α to package LINE-1 retrotransposons into heterochromatin, silencing their expression. The directionality is SIRT6/KAP1 upstream of HP1α tethering. This protects genome stability by containing mobile elements. It explains how SIRT6 loss derepresses LINE-1.

nodes.label: TFEB (at K116)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates TFEB at Lys116, enhancing its nuclear translocation and transcriptional activity to drive the CLEAR autophagic/lysosomal gene program. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic activation of TFEB. This promotes lysosomal biogenesis and autophagic flux. It links SIRT1 to the terminal degradative arm of autophagy alongside ULK1/Beclin-1.

nodes.label: BMAL1
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates BMAL1, a core circadian transcription factor, gating circadian NAD+ oscillations and coupling metabolic state to clock gene expression. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic tuning of BMAL1. This places sirtuins at the interface of circadian rhythm and metabolism. It explains how NAD+ rhythms drive daily transcriptional programs.

nodes.label: Atg5
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates Atg5, enhancing autophagosome formation as part of its autophagy-promoting function. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic activation of Atg5. Atg5 is essential for LC3 lipidation and autophagosome elongation. This adds another core autophagy protein to SIRT1's substrate list.

nodes.label: Atg7
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates Atg7, promoting autophagy initiation and autophagosome formation. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic activation of Atg7, the E1-like enzyme that conjugates LC3 to phosphatidylethanolamine. This reinforces SIRT1's broad control of autophagic machinery. It complements SIRT1 actions on ULK1, Beclin-1, Atg5, and LC3.

nodes.label: LXR (Liver X Receptor)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates the liver X receptor (LXR), a nuclear receptor that regulates cholesterol metabolism and efflux. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic modulation of LXR. This influences reverse cholesterol transport and lipid homeostasis. It expands SIRT1's role in cardiovascular and metabolic regulation.

nodes.label: PML-mediated premature senescence
nodes.description: In mouse embryonic fibroblasts, SIRT1 rescues cells from PML-mediated premature senescence by deacetylating and inhibiting p53, relieving the senescence program. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of senescence rescue. This requires the PML–p53–SIRT1 nuclear-body axis. It shows SIRT1 can oppose proliferative arrest when appropriately engaged.

nodes.label: ROCK1 (neurons)
nodes.description: SIRT1 downregulates ROCK1 expression in neurons, which induces α-secretase (ADAM10) activity relevant to amyloid precursor processing and Alzheimer's prevention under caloric restriction. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of ROCK1 suppression → α-secretase induction. This shifts APP cleavage away from amyloidogenic β-secretase. It links SIRT1 to reduced amyloidogenesis.

nodes.label: DNA double-strand breaks (RCM)
nodes.description: During DNA repair, SIRT1 relocalizes to double-strand breaks where it deacetylates repair factors, a central mechanism of the Information Theory of Aging (RCM) framework. The directionality is DNA damage upstream of SIRT1 relocalization. This consumes NAD+ and redistributes chromatin modifiers, proposed to drive epigenetic drift. It is a key node in Sinclair's RCM model of aging.

nodes.label: FOXO3a (to induce SOD2, Catalase)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO3a, which then transcriptionally induces SOD2, catalase, and glutathione-biosynthesis genes, protecting cells against oxidative stress. The directionality is SIRT1 → FOXO3a → antioxidant enzyme induction. This is a canonical longevity-associated stress-resistance program. It underlies much of SIRT1's cytoprotective reputation.

nodes.label: α-tubulin
nodes.description: SIRT2 is the first identified tubulin deacetylase, with α-tubulin as its most characterized substrate; deacetylation regulates microtubule stability and dynamics. The directionality is SIRT2 enzymatic tuning of α-tubulin acetylation. Reduced α-tubulin acetylation is linked to neurodegeneration, explaining why SIRT2 inhibitors protect neurons. It is the mechanistic basis for SIRT2's mitotic and axonal roles.

nodes.label: CDC14B
nodes.description: The phosphatase CDC14B dephosphorylates SIRT2, triggering its ubiquitination and 26S proteasomal degradation, which promotes exit from mitosis. The directionality is CDC14B upstream of SIRT2 destabilization. This couples SIRT2 turnover to cell-cycle progression. It ensures SIRT2 levels fall as cells complete division.

nodes.label: OPA1 (at Lys926, Lys931)
nodes.description: SIRT3 deacetylates OPA1 at Lys926 and Lys931 within its GTPase domain, raising OPA1 GTPase activity and enhancing mitochondrial fusion during stress. The directionality is SIRT3 enzymatic activation of OPA1. This preserves mitochondrial network integrity under damage. It links SIRT3 to mitochondrial dynamics and quality control.

nodes.label: Mitochondrial fusion (via OPA1)
nodes.description: Through OPA1 deacetylation, SIRT3 enhances mitochondrial fusion during stress, maintaining a connected, healthy mitochondrial network. The directionality is SIRT3 → OPA1 → fusion. Fused mitochondria better share membrane potential and dilute damage. This protects against fragmentation and bioenergetic collapse.

nodes.label: Obese mouse BAT
nodes.description: Brown adipose tissue of obese mice shows reduced SIRT3 protein and decreased mitochondrial protein expression, linking obesity to impaired thermogenic capacity. The directionality is obesity upstream of lower SIRT3. This blunts cold-induced and basal mitochondrial function. It connects metabolic disease to sirtuin attenuation.

nodes.label: Phylogenetic Class II (evolutionarily ancient)
nodes.description: SIRT4 is classified in phylogenetic Class II, which includes sirtuins from bacteria, insects, nematodes, mould, and protozoa—among the most ancient sirtuin lineages. The directionality is evolutionary placement, not a causal pathway. This antiquity implies conserved mitochondrial metabolic roles. It situates SIRT4 early in sirtuin evolution.

nodes.label: HMGCS2 (ketogenesis)
nodes.description: SIRT5 desuccinylates and activates HMGCS2 (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase 2), the rate-limiting enzyme of ketone-body synthesis, supporting energy production during fasting. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of HMGCS2. This promotes ketogenesis when carbohydrate is scarce. It is a fasting-adaptive function of SIRT5.

nodes.label: LCAD and ACADS (fatty acid β-oxidation)
nodes.description: SIRT5 desuccinylates multiple fatty-acid β-oxidation enzymes including LCAD and ACADS, coordinating mitochondrial lipid catabolism. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of these acyl-CoA dehydrogenases. This supports energy harvest from fat. It exemplifies SIRT5's broad desuccinylase control of metabolism.

nodes.label: IDH2 and SDHA (TCA cycle)
nodes.description: SIRT5 desuccinylates TCA-cycle enzymes IDH2 and SDHA, tuning their activity and coordinating mitochondrial energy metabolism. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic modulation of TCA flux. This helps match oxidation to demand during fasting or stress. It reinforces SIRT5's role as a central mitochondrial metabolic regulator.

nodes.label: SOD1 (via desuccinylation)
nodes.description: SIRT5 activates superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) through desuccinylation, enhancing NADPH production and glutathione recycling for ROS detoxification. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of SOD1. This bolsters cytosolic antioxidant capacity. It extends SIRT5's protective actions beyond the mitochondria's own enzymes.

nodes.label: IDH2 (via desuccinylation)
nodes.description: SIRT5 activates IDH2 through desuccinylation, enhancing its NADPH-producing activity and thereby supporting glutathione reduction and ROS scavenging. The directionality is SIRT5 upstream of IDH2-dependent redox buffering. This complements SOD1 activation in antioxidant defense. It shows SIRT5's desuccinylation broadly strengthens reductive capacity.

nodes.label: Phylogenetic Class III (prokaryotic origin)
nodes.description: SIRT5 is the sole mammalian member of phylogenetic Class III, a group distributed widely across prokaryotes, marking it as one of the most ancient mammalian sirtuins. The directionality is evolutionary classification. Its prokaryotic origin aligns with SIRT5's fundamental mitochondrial metabolic functions. This situates SIRT5 at the root of sirtuin biology.

nodes.label: HMGCS2
nodes.description: SIRT5 regulates ketogenesis by desuccinylating HMGCS2, the rate-limiting enzyme of ketone-body synthesis, enabling fuel production during fasting. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of HMGCS2. This is a fasting-adaptive, energetically protective action. It reaffirms SIRT5's role in coordinating catabolic flux.

nodes.label: MTPα (mitochondrial trifunctional protein α)
nodes.description: SIRT4 suppresses fatty-acid oxidation in liver by inhibiting the mitochondrial trifunctional protein α subunit (MTPα), promoting lipid accumulation under nutrient-replete conditions. The directionality is SIRT4 upstream of reduced β-oxidation. This contrasts with SIRT3/SIRT5, which support fat oxidation. It positions SIRT4 as a mitochondrial anabolic brake.

nodes.label: ICE Mouse
nodes.description: The ICE (Induced Changes in Epigenetics) Mouse uses inducible I-PpoI expression to introduce targeted double-strand breaks that are repaired without introducing mutations. The directionality is I-PpoI upstream of controlled DSB formation. This lets researchers trigger DNA damage alone, isolating epigenetic from mutational effects. It is the experimental engine of the RCM model.

nodes.label: I-PpoI endonuclease
nodes.description: The ICE (Induced Changes in Epigenetics) Mouse uses inducible I-PpoI expression to introduce targeted double-strand breaks that are repaired without introducing mutations. The directionality is I-PpoI upstream of controlled DSB formation. This lets researchers trigger DNA damage alone, isolating epigenetic from mutational effects. It is the experimental engine of the RCM model.

nodes.label: RCM-driven epigenetic aging
nodes.description: Induction of DSBs in the ICE Mouse, followed by repair, produces accelerated epigenetic aging and physiological decline without mutagenesis, supporting the RCM (rizortho/Reversible-Cellular-Memory) hypothesis. The directionality is DSB repair upstream of epigenetic aging. This argues aging can arise from information loss, not just damage. It is a cornerstone experiment for the Information Theory of Aging.

nodes.label: Information Theory of Aging
nodes.description: Because the ICE Mouse phenotype occurs without mutations, it is attributed to loss of epigenetic information rather than hardware damage, supporting the Information Theory of Aging. The directionality is mutation-free DSB repair upstream of information loss. This reframes aging as a software, not hardware, failure. It is a foundational claim of Sinclair's theory.

nodes.label: I-PpoI
nodes.description: I-PpoI recognizes and cleaves a specific ~15–20 bp sequence within rRNA gene repeats, generating sequence-specific double-strand breaks. The directionality is I-PpoI upstream of targeted DSBs. Its specificity makes it ideal for the ICE Mouse's controlled damage. This enables reproducible epigenetic-aging studies.

nodes.label: Sequence-specific double-strand breaks
nodes.description: I-PpoI recognizes and cleaves a specific ~15–20 bp sequence within rRNA gene repeats, generating sequence-specific double-strand breaks. The directionality is I-PpoI upstream of targeted DSBs. Its specificity makes it ideal for the ICE Mouse's controlled damage. This enables reproducible epigenetic-aging studies.

nodes.label: David Sinclair
nodes.description: David Sinclair identified SIRT1 as a mediator of caloric-restriction benefits and, in a landmark 2003 study, discovered resveratrol as a sirtuin-activating compound (STAC). The directionality is the discovery establishing SIRT1/STAC centrality to longevity. This launched the modern sirtuin field. It connects basic yeast findings to mammalian therapeutics.

nodes.label: SIRT1 as CR mediator
nodes.description: David Sinclair identified SIRT1 as a mediator of caloric-restriction benefits and, in a landmark 2003 study, discovered resveratrol as a sirtuin-activating compound (STAC). The directionality is the discovery establishing SIRT1/STAC centrality to longevity. This launched the modern sirtuin field. It connects basic yeast findings to mammalian therapeutics.

nodes.label: Resveratrol as STAC
nodes.description: In 2003, Sinclair showed resveratrol extends yeast lifespan via Sir2 and later demonstrated parallel effects in higher organisms, discovering it as the first STAC. The directionality is the discovery upstream of the STAC concept. This catalyzed decades of sirtuin-drug development. It remains a seminal finding in geroscience.

nodes.label: Sirtris Pharmaceuticals
nodes.description: Sinclair co-founded Sirtris Pharmaceuticals (later acquired by GlaxoSmithKline) to develop STACs such as SRT1720 and SRT2104 as therapeutics. The directionality is the academic discovery translated into a company. This drove clinical translation of sirtuin activators. It illustrates the bench-to-bedside path of sirtuin research.

nodes.label: ICE Mouse model
nodes.description: The Sinclair lab developed the ICE Mouse to test the RCM hypothesis using mutation-free double-strand breaks. The directionality is the model enabling tests of epigenetic aging. This provided key evidence for the Information Theory of Aging. It is a methodological contribution alongside the theoretical framework.

nodes.label: SIRT1 (via Hes1 deacetylation)
nodes.description: SIRT1 directly regulates BDNF transcription by deacetylating and repressing Hes1, a transcriptional repressor of BDNF, thereby relieving inhibition and promoting neuronal survival. The directionality is SIRT1 → Hes1 deacetylation → BDNF induction. This links sirtuin activity to neurotrophic support. It is a mechanism for SIRT1's neuroprotective and cognitive benefits.

nodes.label: SIRT1/PGC-1α
nodes.description: SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, which co-activates the BDNF promoter, linking mitochondrial biogenesis to neurotrophic support. The directionality is SIRT1/PGC-1α upstream of BDNF transcription. This couples energy metabolism to neuronal growth-factor expression. It reinforces the metabolic–neurotrophic axis of SIRT1.

nodes.label: BDNF promoter
nodes.description: SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, which co-activates the BDNF promoter, linking mitochondrial biogenesis to neurotrophic support. The directionality is SIRT1/PGC-1α upstream of BDNF transcription. This couples energy metabolism to neuronal growth-factor expression. It reinforces the metabolic–neurotrophic axis of SIRT1.

nodes.label: BDNF and NAD+ levels
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Exercise raises both BDNF and NAD+ levels, and SIRT1 may mediate exercise-induced BDNF upregulation in the hippocampus. The directionality is exercise upstream of BDNF/NAD+ elevation. Higher NAD+ fuels SIRT1, which then supports BDNF. This provides a mechanistic bridge between physical activity, sirtuins, and brain health.

nodes.label: BDNF (via SIRT1/FoxO)
nodes.description: Caloric restriction and intermittent fasting elevate BDNF through SIRT1/FoxO-dependent pathways, contributing to cognitive resilience against aging. The directionality is CR upstream of BDNF elevation via SIRT1/FoxO. This neuroprotective adaptation complements CR's systemic benefits. It motivates CR and fasting for brain health.

nodes.label: PCAF
nodes.description: SIRT1 physically interacts with and deacetylates PCAF (p300/CBP-associated factor), a histone acetyltransferase, within regulatory complexes at muscle-gene promoters. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic inhibition of PCAF. This counterbalances acetylation during myogenic regulation. It shows SIRT1 tuning acetyltransferase partners, not only substrates.

nodes.label: PCAF/GCN5
nodes.description: The positive histone acetyltransferases PCAF and GCN5 acetylate the myogenic transcription factor MyoD, enhancing its DNA-binding and recruitment of transcriptional machinery. The directionality is PCAF/GCN5 upstream of MyoD activation. This promotes muscle differentiation. SIRT1 opposes this by deacetylating both PCAF and MyoD.

nodes.label: MyoD
nodes.description: The positive histone acetyltransferases PCAF and GCN5 acetylate the myogenic transcription factor MyoD, enhancing its DNA-binding and recruitment of transcriptional machinery. The directionality is PCAF/GCN5 upstream of MyoD activation. This promotes muscle differentiation. SIRT1 opposes this by deacetylating both PCAF and MyoD.

nodes.label: MEF2D (at Lys424)
nodes.description: HDAC4 possesses SUMO E3 ligase activity and sumoylates MEF2D at Lys424, locking it into an inactive, transcription-repressing state. The directionality is HDAC4 upstream of MEF2D inactivation. This regulates muscle-gene expression independently of sirtuins. It is included as a parallel chromatin regulatory mechanism contextualizing SIRT1's muscle actions.

nodes.label: PML-IV
nodes.description: Upon oncogenic stress, the PML-IV isoform recruits both p53 and SIRT1 into PML nuclear bodies, assembling a stress-responsive regulatory hub. The directionality is PML-IV upstream of p53/SIRT1 compartmentalization. Within these bodies, SIRT1 deacetylates p53 to shape the senescence/apoptosis decision. It connects PML bodies to sirtuin-mediated tumor suppression.

nodes.label: p53 and SIRT1 to nuclear bodies
nodes.description: Upon oncogenic stress, the PML-IV isoform recruits both p53 and SIRT1 into PML nuclear bodies, assembling a stress-responsive regulatory hub. The directionality is PML-IV upstream of p53/SIRT1 compartmentalization. Within these bodies, SIRT1 deacetylates p53 to shape the senescence/apoptosis decision. It connects PML bodies to sirtuin-mediated tumor suppression.
nodes.norm_label: p53 and sirt1 to nuclear bodies

nodes.label: PML
nodes.description: PML-IV overexpression is sufficient to induce p53-dependent premature senescence, and loss of PML accelerates tumorigenesis, establishing PML as a tumor suppressor. The directionality is PML upstream of senescence. This process engages SIRT1 and p53 at PML nuclear bodies. It contextualizes SIRT1's role in proliferation arrest.

nodes.label: Premature cellular senescence
nodes.description: PML-IV overexpression is sufficient to induce p53-dependent premature senescence, and loss of PML accelerates tumorigenesis, establishing PML as a tumor suppressor. The directionality is PML upstream of senescence. This process engages SIRT1 and p53 at PML nuclear bodies. It contextualizes SIRT1's role in proliferation arrest.

nodes.label: Mediterranean Diet
nodes.description: The Mediterranean Diet's resveratrol content is proposed to activate SIRT1, linking the dietary pattern to longevity pathways (moderate confidence 0.75). The directionality is diet-derived resveratrol upstream of SIRT1 activation. This is one of several polyphenol-mediated mechanisms of the diet. Human causality is inferential rather than proven.

nodes.label: SIRT1 (via resveratrol)
nodes.description: The Mediterranean Diet's resveratrol content is proposed to activate SIRT1, linking the dietary pattern to longevity pathways (moderate confidence 0.75). The directionality is diet-derived resveratrol upstream of SIRT1 activation. This is one of several polyphenol-mediated mechanisms of the diet. Human causality is inferential rather than proven.

nodes.label: Cardiovascular Disease risk
nodes.description: The PREDIMED trial showed that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with olive oil or nuts significantly reduced major cardiovascular events. The directionality is dietary pattern upstream of lower CVD incidence. Polyphenols including resveratrol may engage SIRT1, but the effect is multifactorial. It is a clinically validated dietary intervention.

nodes.label: Lipid profile (raises HDL, reduces LDL oxidation)
nodes.description: The Mediterranean Diet raises HDL while reducing LDL oxidation through its polyphenol-rich components, improving the overall lipid profile. The directionality is diet upstream of favorable lipid changes. This contributes to its cardiovascular protection. Resveratrol and other polyphenols are putative SIRT1-engaging contributors.
nodes.norm_label: lipid profile (raises hdl, reduces ldl oxidation)

nodes.label: SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio
nodes.description: The SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio defines the hormetic window—the dose range over which mitochondrial stress triggers adaptive responses rather than damage. The directionality is the ratio upstream of the adaptive-vs-harmful threshold. Because SIRT3 is protective and SIRT4 is detrimental, a high ratio broadens resilience. Caloric restriction and youth raise this ratio; aging lowers it.

nodes.label: SIRT3 (and downregulates SIRT4)
nodes.description: Caloric restriction upregulates SIRT3 and downregulates SIRT4, shifting the SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio toward a protective, oxidative-phosphorylation-promoting state. The directionality is CR upstream of the ratio shift. This counters the age-related pattern of declining SIRT3 and rising SIRT4. It is a core mechanism of CR's metabolic benefits.

nodes.label: Declining SIRT3 and rising SIRT4
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Aging is associated with declining SIRT3 activity and rising SIRT4, which narrows the hormetic window and increases vulnerability to mitochondrial stressors. The directionality is aging upstream of the altered ratio. This shift favors oxidant stress and metabolic inflexibility. Restoring the ratio (e.g., via CR or NAD+ precursors) is a proposed anti-aging strategy.

nodes.label: STACs
nodes.description: Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) such as resveratrol lower the Km of SIRT1 for its peptide/NAD+ substrates, amplifying deacetylation efficiency. The directionality is STAC binding upstream of enhanced catalytic rate. This allosteric effect is the defining action of a STAC. It underlies the metabolic and longevity benefits attributed to these molecules.

nodes.label: SIRT1 KM for substrates
nodes.description: Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) such as resveratrol lower the Km of SIRT1 for its peptide/NAD+ substrates, amplifying deacetylation efficiency. The directionality is STAC binding upstream of enhanced catalytic rate. This allosteric effect is the defining action of a STAC. It underlies the metabolic and longevity benefits attributed to these molecules.

nodes.label: NAD+ in tumor microenvironment
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins (overview, CD38 KO risks, cancer therapies).md
nodes.description: CD38 enzymatic activity depletes NAD+ in the tumor microenvironment and generates adenosine, suppressing anti-tumor T-cell and NK-cell responses. The directionality is CD38 upstream of NAD+ depletion and immunosuppression. This links CD38 to cancer immune evasion. Anti-CD38 antibodies both target myeloma and reshape the TME.

nodes.label: Anti-CD38 mAbs
nodes.description: Anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies eliminate CD38+ Tregs and MDSCs and reduce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression, restoring T- and NK-cell function in the tumor microenvironment. The directionality is anti-CD38 therapy upstream of TME reprogramming. This is both an anticancer action and a means to spare NAD+ for sirtuins. It illustrates the dual therapeutic logic of CD38 targeting.

nodes.label: FOXO3a (to induce BNIP3 mitophagy)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO3a, which transcriptionally induces BNIP3, forming the NAD+ → SIRT1 → FOXO3a → BNIP3 mitophagy axis that clears damaged mitochondria. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of BNIP3-dependent mitophagy. This protects cells from mitochondrial dysfunction and ROS. It is a refined mitophagic branch of the SIRT1–FOXO3a program.

nodes.label: HIF-2α
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates HIF-2α, modulating its stability and transcriptional output to influence metabolic adaptation to hypoxia (moderate confidence 0.75). The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic tuning of HIF-2α. This parallels SIRT1's regulation of HIF-1α. The lower confidence reflects less-complete characterization of this substrate.

nodes.label: Retinoblastoma Protein (Rb)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates the retinoblastoma protein (Rb) as part of its cell-cycle regulatory functions, influencing Rb's interaction with E2F and cell-cycle control (moderate confidence 0.75). The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic modification of Rb. This adds a cell-cycle dimension to SIRT1 beyond p53/E2F. The moderate confidence reflects incomplete mechanistic detail.

nodes.label: SIRT1/AMPK
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 and AMPK form a reciprocal regulatory loop in which each can activate the other, jointly promoting energy homeostasis and autophagic flux. The directionality is bidirectional: SIRT1 deacetylates/activates LKB1/PGC-1α and AMPK phosphorylates/activates SIRT1. This creates a self-reinforcing metabolic circuit. It is a central node integrating nutrient sensing and clearance.

nodes.label: Energy homeostasis and autophagy
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 and AMPK form a reciprocal regulatory loop in which each can activate the other, jointly promoting energy homeostasis and autophagic flux. The directionality is bidirectional: SIRT1 deacetylates/activates LKB1/PGC-1α and AMPK phosphorylates/activates SIRT1. This creates a self-reinforcing metabolic circuit. It is a central node integrating nutrient sensing and clearance.

nodes.label: SIRT1 (Ser27, Thr344)
nodes.description: Under low-energy conditions, AMPK directly phosphorylates SIRT1 at Ser27 and Thr344, enhancing its deacetylase activity and coupling energy deficit to sirtuin function. The directionality is AMPK upstream of SIRT1 activation. This closes the reciprocal loop with SIRT1. It ensures sirtuin responses track cellular AMP/ATP state.

nodes.label: p73
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates p73, suppressing its transcriptional activity and inhibiting apoptosis, analogous to its regulation of the related p53 family member. The directionality is SIRT1 enzymatic inactivation of p73. This promotes cell survival under stress but can be tumor-promoting. It extends SIRT1's control over the p53 family.

nodes.label: SIRT1 deacetylation of FOXO4
nodes.description: FOXO4 deacetylation by SIRT1 enhances expression of GADD45 and suppresses caspase-3/7 activity, promoting DNA repair over apoptosis. The directionality is SIRT1 → FOXO4 → GADD45 induction. This biases cells toward damage repair rather than death. It is a further example of SIRT1 steering stress responses toward survival and genome maintenance.

nodes.label: GADD45 expression
nodes.description: FOXO4 deacetylation by SIRT1 enhances expression of GADD45 and suppresses caspase-3/7 activity, promoting DNA repair over apoptosis. The directionality is SIRT1 → FOXO4 → GADD45 induction. This biases cells toward damage repair rather than death. It is a further example of SIRT1 steering stress responses toward survival and genome maintenance.

nodes.label: ASAH1
nodes.description: Acid ceramidase (ACase, aCDase) is encoded by ASAH1. It is a lysosomal hydrolase that cleaves ceramide into sphingosine and a free fatty acid.

nodes.label: Carmofur
nodes.description: Carmofur has IC50 29 nM against acid ceramidase, is clinically approved in Japan, crosses the BBB, and is a repurposing candidate for senolytic therapy.

nodes.label: NF-kappaB
nodes.description: AP-1 and NF-κB are co-regulators of inflammatory SASP genes. They share transcriptional targets including IL-6, IL-8, and TNFα.

nodes.label: CXCL5
nodes.description: AP-1 transactivates CXCL5 (a SASP chemokine), which feeds inflammaging. Caloric restriction suppresses inflammaging and activates autophagy via mTOR/AMPK.

nodes.label: Hydroxychloroquine
nodes.description: HCQ blocks cytoprotective autophagy in cancer cells and is combined with chemotherapy in clinical trials. Results have been modest and inconsistent across cancer types.

nodes.label: p62
nodes.description: SQSTM1/p62-mediated selective autophagy directly degrades p16 and p21 (independent of UPS), reversing the senescent phenotype in canine MMVD valve cells.

nodes.label: TRIAD
nodes.description: TRIAD (Test of Rapamycin In Aging Dogs) is a parallel-group, double-masked, randomized, placebo-controlled trial testing rapamycin's effect on lifespan and healthspan in companion dogs.

nodes.label: PAK2
nodes.description: PAK2 directly binds and phosphorylates Caspase-7 at Ser30, Thr173, and Ser239, neutralizing its effector function and promoting survival in breast cancer.

nodes.label: Pin1
nodes.description: Pin1 binding to phosphorylated BAX (Thr167) catalyzes a conformational change that locks Bax in an inactive state, preventing mitochondrial translocation and MOMP.

nodes.label: PTPN5
nodes.description: PTPN5 (STEP), along with PTPN2 and PTPN23, dephosphorylates BAK at Tyr108, licensing it for mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and apoptosis.

nodes.label: K-RAS
nodes.description: In K-RAS mutated cancers, hyperactive ERK1/2 phosphorylates and inactivates PTPN5, locking BAK in its inactive phosphorylated state and providing resistance to apoptosis.

nodes.label: Geraldol
nodes.description: Fisetin is metabolized by COMT to geraldol (3'-O-methylfisetin). This metabolic activation is concentration-dependent and consumes SAMe, generating SAH.

nodes.label: Cardiolipin
nodes.description: Cardiolipin stimulates DRP1 GTPase activity for fission AND is required for OPA1-mediated fusion — it has dual pro-fusion and pro-fission roles depending on context.

nodes.label: Mice
nodes.description: Male transgenic mice overexpressing SIRT6 show ~30% lifespan extension. SIRT6 KO mice die within ~4 weeks with dramatic progeroid phenotype. [ESTABLISHED: animal data]

nodes.label: PDE4
nodes.description: Resveratrol acts as a competitive inhibitor of cAMP phosphodiesterases (PDE4), leading to cAMP accumulation, Epac1 activation, Ca2+ release, and AMPK activation.

nodes.label: CDK5
nodes.description: CDK5 phosphorylates NOXA at Ser13, causing inactivation in metabolically regulated T-cell leukemia cells.

nodes.label: Trehalose
nodes.description: Trehalose activates TFEB via inhibiting Akt, increasing clearance of proteolipid aggregates in Batten disease and reducing cardiac hypertrophy/fibrosis in chronic MI models.

nodes.label: Celastrol
nodes.description: Celastrol activates TFEB via inhibiting mTORC1, reducing insoluble phosphorylated Tau aggregates and improving memory deficiency in Alzheimer's disease models.

nodes.label: Bleomycin
nodes.description: Bleomycin induces premature senescence via DNA breaks, activating p53-p21 and p16 pathways with SASP secretion.

nodes.label: Sodium Butyrate
nodes.description: Sodium butyrate (HDAC inhibitor) induces senescence-like state via p21 upregulation, which can be both p53-dependent and independent.

nodes.label: Lands cycle
nodes.description: The Lands cycle exchanges fatty acids into the sn-2 position of membrane phospholipids. ACase-liberated fatty acids enter this cycle, enriching PUFA-containing species.

nodes.label: Phospholipid
nodes.description: The Lands cycle exchanges fatty acids into the sn-2 position of membrane phospholipids. ACase-liberated fatty acids enter this cycle, enriching PUFA-containing species.

nodes.label: Sphingosine-1-phosphate
nodes.description: ACase overexpression raises sphingosine/S1P levels, which is classically anti-apoptotic and helps senescent cells resist apoptosis via SCAP pathways.

nodes.label: Huntingtin
nodes.description: Mutant huntingtin (mHTT) uncouples fission from degradation while disrupting autophagic flux. Broad-spectrum autophagy activators like rapamycin may be insufficient if downstream transport remains blocked.

nodes.label: PLK3
nodes.description: PLK3 phosphorylates BCL-XL at Ser49, causing cell cycle G2 arrest in lymphoma cells.

nodes.label: RSK
nodes.description: RSK phosphorylates APAF-1 at Ser268, causing inhibition in prostate cancer cells.

links.source_file: _document_ - Neuroprotective Actions of Methylene Blue and Its Derivatives.md
links.context: 2-Chlorophenothiazine, which consists of the phenothiazine nucleus without the amine side chains of methylene blue, acts as a direct free-radical scavenger independent of mitochondria and NADH. In the cell-free mitochondrial lysate oxidation assay it significantly reduced DCF fluorescence both with and without mitochondria/NADH, unlike MB which required both. Despite potent nanomolar neuroprotection against glutamate, IAA, and rotenone toxicity, it had no effect on oxygen consumption, anaerobic glycolysis, or the complex I-III electron shunt, and it did not upregulate complex IV expression, revealing a mechanism distinct from MB.

The conversion of adrenaline to adrenochrome is an oxidation reaction mediated by oxygen radicals (reactive oxygen species). In the adrenochrome pathway, ROS production by stimulated neutrophils stimulated the oxidation of adrenaline, transforming the catecholamine into its pink oxidation product adrenochrome and further into adrenolutin. Because the oxidation step does not require a dedicated enzyme, oxygen radicals can drive it whenever antioxidant defenses are overwhelmed. This ROS-mediated oxidation is the core chemical event of the pathway and is what links inflammatory oxidant production to catecholamine chemistry in the heart. It also explains the classical observation, first made in 1856, that adrenaline exposed to air or oxidizing conditions turns pink as adrenochrome forms, and why scavenging systems normally keep this reaction suppressed.

Reactive oxygen species activate NF-kappaB because oxidants (notably H2O2) modify cysteines on inhibitory proteins and upstream kinases, releasing NF-kappaB for nuclear translocation and target-gene expression. The transcription factor then induces genes that generate more ROS, establishing a feed-forward loop. The directionality is oxidant to transcriptional activation. A caveat is that ROS also activate many other pathways (MAPK, AP-1), and NF-kappaB can be either protective or pathogenic depending on context.

links.source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
links.context: Acetate is converted intracellularly into acetyl-CoA by ACSS2 and is not membrane-permeable acetyl-CoA itself. Acetate supplementation increases global nuclear acetylation including H3K27ac and induces expression of pro-inflammatory genes including IL6, IL8, IL1B and CCL2 without affecting cell cycle regulators p16 and p21. In mitochondria-depleted senescent cells, acetate increases histone acetylation and partially restores a subset of the mitochondrial-dependent SASP programme. However, acetate-induced SASP gene expression is suppressed by the STING inhibitor SN011, showing that chromatin accessibility alone cannot drive SASP transcription without innate immune activation.

links.source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
links.context: Cellular senescence is a key response to various cellular stresses characterized by a permanent cell cycle arrest and the secretion of a pro-inflammatory cocktail of factors known as the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Senescence serves protective roles in embryonic development, tumour suppression and tissue repair, but persistent SASP activation leads to chronic inflammation contributing to tissue dysfunction, ageing and a broad spectrum of age-related diseases including cancer. This dual nature makes SASP a focal point for understanding both the protective and detrimental effects of senescence.

links.source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
links.context: Many SASP-associated genes are linked to super-enhancer-like regions that are particularly sensitive to changes in histone acetylation, and such loci probably require sustained acetyl-CoA availability to maintain high transcriptional output, rendering them especially vulnerable to interventions that limit acetyl-CoA supply. SLC25A1 inhibition reduces chromatin accessibility at these SASP loci both in vitro and in vivo, selectively suppressing inflammatory gene expression. This positions mitochondrial metabolism as an upstream determinant of chromatin accessibility in senescent cells, aligning with previous reports linking citrate metabolism to SASP regulation.

Senescent stromal cells in the tumor microenvironment secrete soluble SASP factors that confer therapeutic resistance on residual cancer cells, including WNT16B, amphiregulin (AREG) and epiregulin (EREG). Conditioned media from bleomycin-senescent PSC27 stroma elevated viability, migration and invasion of prostate cancer lines (PC3, DU145, M12, LNCaP) and shifted their survival curves against mitoxantrone. Apigenin treatment of the stromal cells diminished this SASP-conferred resistance almost to basal levels and increased cancer cell apoptosis (caspase-3/7 activity).

links.source_file: _document_ - Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP.md
links.context: ChIP-seq analysis of histone H3 acetylation at lysine 27 (H3K27ac) showed that loci gaining acetylation during senescence are markedly reduced following mitochondrial clearance, and these regions are enriched for inflammatory and interleukin signalling pathways central to the SASP. A 51-gene SASP signature induced during senescence is suppressed upon mitochondrial removal, with genes such as IL6 and CCL2 showing coordinated decreases in chromatin acetylation and mRNA expression. Multiple nodes of the mitochondrial citrate-acetyl-CoA axis converge to control H3K27ac at SASP loci, selectively modulating inflammatory gene expression without affecting the senescence-associated cell cycle arrest.

NF-κB is the master transcriptional regulator of the SASP, controlling expression of the bulk of pro-inflammatory interleukins, chemokines, and growth factors. It is activated downstream of multiple senescence inputs including p38 MAPK, GATA4 (via TRAF3IP2), and cGAS-STING, and it cooperates with C/EBPbeta at SASP enhancers. Inhibition of NF-κB robustly suppresses the inflammatory arm of the SASP across many models. A caveat is that NF-κB is necessary but not sufficient -- full SASP establishment requires additional axes such as IL-1α/MyD88 and mTOR.

Chronic SASP secretion from accumulated senescent cells is a principal driver of inflammaging, the sterile, low-grade inflammation that rises with age. By continuously releasing IL-6, IL-1α, TNFalpha, and chemokines, senescent cells maintain a pro-inflammatory tissue milieu that disrupts homeostasis and promotes age-related disease. The relationship is causal and bidirectional with aging: inflammaging further impairs clearance mechanisms. Senolytics and senomorphics both reduce inflammaging by targeting either the source cells or their secretome.

The SASP is a hypersecretory state -- a specialized secretory phenotype -- in which senescent cells upregulate and release hundreds of factors including interleukins, chemokines, growth factors, proteases, and extracellular vesicles. This secreted output contrasts with the quiescent, low-turnover secretome of non-senescent cells and is a defining non-cell-autonomous feature of the senescent state. The composition of the SASP is variable, shaped by the senescence inducer, cell type, and tissue context. Its classification as a secretory phenotype emphasizes that senescence exerts its effects largely through communication with the microenvironment.

The cGAS-STING innate immune pathway is a key driver of the SASP, activated by cytoplasmic nucleic acids including mtDNA released via minority MOMP and chromatin from cytoplasmic chromatin fragments. cGAS senses cytosolic DNA, producing cGAMP that activates STING, which in turn drives type-I interferon and NF-κB signaling to amplify SASP factor production. This linkage connects mitochondrial dysfunction and genomic stress directly to inflammatory senescence output. Importantly, cGAS-STING also enhances immune surveillance, giving the pathway both pro- and anti-tumor consequences.

The mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) promotes SASP production chiefly by enhancing translation of key SASP factors such as IL-1α and by stabilizing SASP mRNAs through the MK2/ZFP36L1 axis. mTOR thereby couples the heightened biosynthetic demand of senescent cells to secretome output. Pharmacologic inhibition with rapamycin suppresses the SASP without necessarily reversing the cell-cycle arrest. This makes mTOR a central node linking metabolic state to the inflammatory phenotype of senescence.

p38 MAPK was the first kinase shown to activate the SASP independently of the canonical DDR, acting upstream of NF-κB to drive pro-inflammatory factor expression. It stabilizes SASP transcripts in the tumor microenvironment and integrates signals from oxidative stress and the ASAP-to-SASP transition. p38 MAPK inhibition suppresses SASP from fibroblasts of older donors, supporting its therapeutic relevance. Its activity is a convergence point for multiple senescence-inducing stresses rather than a single upstream trigger.

The JAK-STAT3 signaling axis promotes a pro-inflammatory SASP by interacting with p38 MAPK and mTOR and by transducing cues from SASP cytokines such as IL-6. STAT3 activation contributes to age-related frailty and to the immune-modulatory and tumor-promoting facets of the secretome. JAK1/2 inhibitors (e.g., ruxolitinib) reduce SASP cytokines IL-6 and IL-8, validating the axis as a senomorphic target. The pathway is especially important for the feed-forward, self-reinforcing inflammation characteristic of chronic senescence.

In most cellular contexts p53 restrains the pro-inflammatory arm of the SASP, limiting expression of cytokines and chemokines; loss or mutation of p53 dramatically amplifies SASP output. This restraint is mechanistically linked to p53's ability to suppress NF-κB-driven inflammation and to its role in DNA-damage-induced senescence. The directionality is suppressive: intact p53 yields a more contained secretome, whereas p53 deficiency yields an exaggerated, tumor-promoting SASP. This nuance explains why p53 status strongly shapes the net effect of senescence in tissues.

p16INK4a can induce a senescence program with a distinctive SASP profile that includes factors such as IGFBP3 and ISG15 and is relatively independent of a classical DNA damage response. This p16-associated secretory phenotype (PASP) is thought to be more p53-dependent for its composition and differs qualitatively from DDR-driven SASP. The relationship highlights that the SASP is not monolithic but varies with the upstream arrest pathway. p16 overexpression thus both enforces arrest and shapes the secretome character.

Cytoplasmic LINE-1 (L1) retrotransposon cDNA, arising from derepression of endogenous retroelements in senescence, triggers interferon signaling through the cGAS-STING pathway. This reinforces SASP factor production, particularly in deeper, more established senescence where retroelement activation is pronounced. The process is restrained by RB1 and SIRT6, whose decline permits L1 derepression. It represents a chromatin-immune feed-forward loop by which genomic destabilization amplifies the inflammatory secretome.

Cytoplasmic chromatin fragments (CCF) -- DNA-SCARS shed into the cytosol in therapy-induced and other senescence -- are sensed by cGAS-STING, activating NF-κB and type-I interferon signaling that induce a robust SASP. CCF formation links persistent DNA damage foci to innate immune activation in the senescent cell. They can also be transmitted to and activate SASP in neighboring recipient cells. The phenomenon is most established in genotoxic-stress-induced senescence, marking a key mechanism bridging damage to secretion.

Rapamycin suppresses the pro-inflammatory SASP by inhibiting mTOR, which reduces translation of SASP factors such as IL-1α and destabilizes SASP mRNAs, and by interfering with the p38 MAPK-IL-1α-NF-κB cascade. As an mTOR inhibitor and autophagy inducer, it also limits inflammasome activation and mitochondrial DAMPs. This senomorphic action reduces the paracrine and systemic consequences of senescence without eliminating the cells. Its broad pleiotropic effects (immunomodulation, metabolic) require careful dosing in therapeutic contexts.

Metformin inhibits NF-κB signaling in fibroblasts, macrophages, and senescent endothelial cells and activates AMPK, which suppresses mTOR-dependent SASP translation. By lowering the inflammatory secretome and improving mitochondrial function, it exerts senomorphic effects relevant to metabolic and vascular aging. Preclinical and epidemiologic data support its anti-inflammatory, potentially anti-aging actions. The magnitude of SASP suppression is context-dependent and generally more modest than dedicated SASP inhibitors.

Resveratrol inhibits pro-inflammatory SASP cytokines primarily through activation of the deacetylase SIRT1, which reduces H3K9 and H4K16 acetylation at SASP gene promoters and interferes with NF-κB. It also acts as an antioxidant, quenching mitochondrial ROS that would otherwise sustain SASP signaling. Evidence for SASP suppression is strong in several cell models but largely preclinical, and bioavailability in vivo is limited. Thus its senomorphic effect is well supported mechanistically though translationally uncertain.

Apigenin, a flavonoid, reduces SASP-driven breast cancer aggressiveness by inhibiting NF-κB-dependent SASP factors and the chemokine CXCL10. It also blocks the ASAP-to-SASP transition by disrupting ATM-HSPA8 and HSPA8-p38 MAPK crosstalk, and binds PRDX6 to inhibit its iPLA2 activity. These actions place apigenin at both the early stress-response and the established-secretome levels. Its effects are documented in specific cancer and fibroblast models, supporting a medium-to-high confidence senomorphic role.

Nutlin 3a suppresses the pro-inflammatory SASP by inhibiting MDM2, thereby stabilizing p53; p53 in turn restrains NF-κB-driven SASP factor expression. This mechanism exploits the natural tumor-suppressive rheostat of p53 rather than broadly blocking inflammation. The compound is primarily a research tool with limited clinical development, constraining its translational confidence. Mechanistically, its SASP-suppressive effect is well grounded in the p53 restraint of the secretome.

BRD4, a bromodomain-containing acetyl-lysine reader, is recruited to senescence-activated enhancers and super-enhancers where it promotes transcription of SASP factors. BET bromodomain inhibitors that displace BRD4 suppress enhancer-driven SASP expression, establishing it as a senomorphic target. Its action is downstream of the chromatin remodeling that licenses SASP loci. The reliance on BRD4 varies with the SASP gene, but it is a consistent, druggable component of the program.

KDM4 histone demethylases promote SASP factor expression by removing repressive H3K9me3 and H3K36me3 marks at SASP loci, thereby opening chromatin for transcription. Inhibition of KDM4 reduces the secretome, positioning it as a candidate senomorphic strategy. The effect is mechanistically coherent with the broad chromatin derepression of senescence, though the specificity and in vivo validation of KDM4 inhibitors as senomorphics are still emerging. Confidence is therefore moderate pending more clinical data.

EZH2, the catalytic subunit of the PRC2 complex, represses pro-inflammatory SASP factors including CCL2, CXCL9, and CXCL10 by depositing the H3K27me3 repressive mark at their loci. Loss or inhibition of EZH2 derepresses these chemokines, augmenting the SASP. This places polycomb-mediated silencing as a counterbalance to SASP activation. The relationship is fairly well established in specific contexts but is one of several layers of SASP control rather than a master switch.

SIRT1, a NAD+-dependent deacetylase, suppresses the SASP by reducing H3K9 and H4K16 acetylation at the promoters of IL-6 and IL-8, limiting their transcriptional activation. Through this chromatin-mediated restraint and via crosstalk with NF-κB, SIRT1 tempers the inflammatory secretome. Its activity is tied to cellular NAD+ availability, which declines with age, potentially loosening SASP control. The repression is well documented but operates as part of a broader sirtuin-mediated anti-inflammatory network.

AP-1 (e.g., FOS/JUN dimers) acts as a pioneer factor that opens SASP enhancers and cooperates with NF-κB to drive expression of SASP genes. It is required for establishing the senescence-associated enhancer landscape that licenses the secretome. AP-1 thereby bridges early stress signaling to the durable transcriptional program of the SASP. Its contribution is integral but operates in concert with other factors rather than alone.

SASP factors such as IL-1α, TGFβ, VEGF, and CCL2 can act in an autocrine and paracrine manner to reinforce the senescent state and induce growth arrest in neighboring healthy cells -- a process termed paracrine (or bystander) senescence. This spreads the arrested phenotype through tissues, amplifying the functional impact of a small senescent fraction. The directionality is outward: the secretome of one cell converts adjacent cells into a senescent state. A caveat is that paracrine senescence requires susceptible recipients and sufficient SASP magnitude, and it can be both tumor-suppressive and pathological.

SASP chemokines including CCL2, CCL5, CXCL1, and CXCL10 act as find-me signals that recruit natural killer (NK) cells to sites of senescence. NK cells then directly kill senescent cells via NKG2D recognition of stress-induced ligands (MICA, MICB, ULBP2). This recruitment is a key arm of senescence surveillance, converting the SASP into an immune-clearance stimulus. The efficiency of recruitment declines with immunosenescence, allowing senescent-cell accumulation.

SASP factors promote macrophage migration toward senescent cells and can polarize them toward a pro-inflammatory M1-like phenotype, facilitating phagocytosis of the arrested cells. Chemokines such as CCL2 are central to this recruitment, linking the secretome to innate immune clearance. Macrophage engagement is thus both a clearance mechanism and, when chronic, a contributor to tissue inflammation. The net effect depends on whether polarized macrophages resolve or sustain the inflammatory state.

SASP growth factors such as VEGF (and VEGF-C) stimulate angiogenesis, the formation of new blood vessels, in the local microenvironment. This is beneficial in wound healing and tissue repair but can support tumor vascularization and pathological neovascularization in chronic senescence. The directionality is pro-angiogenic via paracrine acting on endothelial cells. The dual nature means SASP-driven angiogenesis is context-dependent -- reparative acutely, deleterious when persistent.

Chronic SASP promotes fibrosis through TGFβ-mediated pro-fibrotic signaling and through matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) that remodel the extracellular matrix, activating resident fibroblasts and myofibroblasts. This contributes to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, liver, and renal fibrosis in aging and after tissue injury. The secretome thereby shifts tissue toward scar formation rather than regeneration. Fibrosis is one of the clearest pathological sequelae of persistent senescence.

Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a prototypical SASP cytokine and one of the most consistently upregulated and secreted factors in senescent cells. It acts as an essential mediator of paracrine senescence and immune modulation and is widely used as a biomarker of the senescent secretome and of aging.
