links.context: Stalled or collapsed replication forks generate single-stranded DNA gaps that engage the ATR-CHK1 cascade, activating a checkpoint that senses replication stress. In OIS, ATR signaling contributes to arrest and senescence establishment. The relationship is a canonical DNA-damage-checkpoint response. It links oncogene-driven hyper-replication to cell-cycle enforcement.

links.source_file: _document_ - Small molecule compounds that induce cellular senescence.md
links.context: DNA replication stress also activates the ATM-CHK2 cascade, converging on p53 stabilization and contributing to senescence induction alongside ATR. Dual ATM/ATR engagement ensures robust arrest under oncogenic stress. The relationship positions replication stress as a trigger of both major DDR kinases. It is supported by inhibitor and genetic studies in OIS.

Sir2 (silent information regulator 2) is the founding member of the sirtuin family, first identified in Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a regulator of mating-type locus silencing and replicative lifespan. The seven mammalian paralogues SIRT1–SIRT7 evolved from this ancestral NAD+-dependent deacetylase, retaining the conserved catalytic core while diversifying in subcellular localization and substrate repertoire. This phylogenetic continuity means insights from yeast Sir2 historically informed mammalian sirtuin biology, although the mammalian enzymes acquired lineage-specific regulatory domains. The relationship is directional: yeast Sir2 is the evolutionary precursor, not a downstream effector, of the SIRT1–7 family.

During the sirtuin-catalyzed deacetylation of a lysine, NAD+ is cleaved between its nicotinamide and ADP-ribose moieties, and the acetyl group is transferred to the ADP-ribose to generate 2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose (OAADPr) plus free nicotinamide. OAADPr is a stoichiometric by-product, released in equimolar amounts with the deacetylated substrate on every catalytic cycle. This molecule is not merely waste: it binds and activates the TRPM2 cation channel, linking sirtuin activity to calcium signaling and cellular stress responses. A caveat is that OAADPr accumulation can itself feed back on cellular metabolism, and its levels reflect the integrated deacetylase flux of the cell.

OAADPr (2'-O-acetyl-ADP-ribose) binds to the cytoplasmic N-terminal domain of the TRPM2 non-selective cation channel, promoting its opening and calcium influx into the cytosol. Because OAADPr is generated directly by sirtuin deacetylase activity, TRPM2 activation acts as a sensor of cellular sirtuin flux and NAD+ utilization. The directionality is unidirectional under basal conditions: sirtuin activity produces OAADPr, which then gates TRPM2, rather than TRPM2 regulating sirtuins. This coupling provides a mechanistic link between metabolic state, redox stress, and calcium-dependent processes such as insulin secretion and apoptotic signaling.

SIRT4 resides in the mitochondrial matrix and acts mainly as a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase on metabolic enzymes such as GDH and MTPα. Its mitochondrial localization enables direct control of amino-acid and fatty-acid fueling of the TCA cycle. The directionality is SIRT4 positioned to brake mitochondrial anabolism. Its activity often opposes the protective actions of SIRT3.

SIRT4 functions principally as a mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase, using NAD+ to attach a single ADP-ribose group to target lysines rather than removing acetyl marks. Its best-characterized ADP-ribosylation target is glutamate dehydrogenase, whose activity it inhibits to dampen amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion. This enzymatic orientation means SIRT4 generally acts as a metabolic suppressor within mitochondria, opposing anabolic and growth signals. A caveat is that SIRT4's deacetylase activity is weak in vitro, so ADP-ribosylation is its physiologically dominant modality.

SIRT4 mono-ADP-ribosylates glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH), inhibiting its oxidative deamination of glutamate to α-ketoglutarate and thereby slowing anaplerotic carbon entry into the TCA cycle. This restrains amino-acid-derived ATP production and insulin secretion in β-cells. The directionality is SIRT4 enzymatic inhibition of GDH. SIRT4 thus acts as a mitochondrial brake on amino-acid catabolism, opposing anabolic fueling of secretion.

SIRT4 inhibits glutamate dehydrogenase by mono-ADP-ribosylation, reducing conversion of glutamate to α-ketoglutarate and limiting anaplerotic carbon entry into the TCA cycle. The directionality is SIRT4 enzymatic suppression of GDH. This restrains amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion and mitochondrial ATP generation. It marks SIRT4 as a metabolic brake within mitochondria.

SIRT4 inhibits glutamine metabolism in colorectal cancer cells—for example by restraining GDH-dependent anaplerosis—acting as a tumor suppressor that limits nutrient fueling of proliferation. The directionality is SIRT4 upstream of suppressed glutamine catabolism. This constrains the glutamine addiction of many tumors. It illustrates SIRT4's context-dependent tumor-suppressive role.

SIRT4 mono-ADP-ribosylates MnSOD, inhibiting its activity and sustaining elevated superoxide levels within mitochondria. The directionality is SIRT4 enzymatic suppression of MnSOD. This is the opposite of SIRT3's activation of MnSOD, underscoring their antagonism. It positions SIRT4 as a promoter of mitochondrial oxidant stress.

SIRT4 contributes to cardiac fibrosis; global SIRT4 knockout in mice confers resistance to angiotensin-II infusion by suppressing fibrotic deposition. The directionality is SIRT4 upstream of profibrotic signaling. This aligns with SIRT4's general tendency to promote pathological remodeling. It contrasts with the antifibrotic SIRT1/SIRT3/SIRT6 members.

SIRT4 acts as a tumor suppressor by inhibiting GDH and restricting glutamine-derived anaplerosis into the TCA cycle, starving cancer cells of carbon for proliferation. The directionality is SIRT4 upstream of suppressed glutamine metabolism. This limits the glutamine addiction of tumors. It is a context where SIRT4 opposes, rather than promotes, growth.

SIRT4 suppresses fatty-acid oxidation in liver by inhibiting the mitochondrial trifunctional protein α subunit (MTPα), promoting lipid accumulation under nutrient-replete conditions. The directionality is SIRT4 upstream of reduced β-oxidation. This contrasts with SIRT3/SIRT5, which support fat oxidation. It positions SIRT4 as a mitochondrial anabolic brake.

SIRT4 is classified in phylogenetic Class II, which includes sirtuins from bacteria, insects, nematodes, mould, and protozoa—among the most ancient sirtuin lineages. The directionality is evolutionary placement, not a causal pathway. This antiquity implies conserved mitochondrial metabolic roles. It situates SIRT4 early in sirtuin evolution.

SIRT4 suppresses fatty-acid oxidation in liver by inhibiting the mitochondrial trifunctional protein α subunit (MTPα), promoting lipid accumulation under nutrient-replete conditions. The directionality is SIRT4 upstream of reduced β-oxidation. This contrasts with SIRT3/SIRT5, which support fat oxidation. It positions SIRT4 as a mitochondrial anabolic brake.

SIRT5 localizes to the mitochondrial matrix and is specialized for removing lysine succinyl, malonyl, and glutaryl groups from metabolic enzymes including CPS1, HMGCS2, and β-oxidation/TCA enzymes. Its mitochondrial residence makes it a key regulator of catabolic flux during fasting. The directionality is SIRT5 sensing mitochondrial acylation state to optimize energy production. It is the sole mammalian member of an ancient prokaryotic sirtuin class.

SIRT5 desuccinylates and activates carbamoyl phosphate synthase 1 (CPS1), the rate-limiting enzyme of the urea cycle, enhancing ammonia detoxification into urea. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of CPS1. This is especially important during fasting or high-protein load when nitrogen must be cleared. It exemplifies SIRT5's role as a regulator of mitochondrial acyl-metabolism.

SIRT5 inhibits preadipocyte differentiation and lipid deposition by activating AMPK and repressing MAPK signaling pathways. The directionality is SIRT5 upstream of AMPK activation. AMPK engagement shifts cells away from lipogenesis and toward catabolism. This positions mitochondrial SIRT5 as a negative regulator of adipogenesis.

SIRT5 inhibits preadipocyte differentiation and lipid deposition by activating AMPK and repressing MAPK signaling pathways. The directionality is SIRT5 upstream of suppressed adipogenesis. This keeps progenitors from becoming lipid-laden fat cells. It positions mitochondrial SIRT5 as a negative regulator of fat accumulation.

SIRT5-induced deacetylation of lactate dehydrogenase B (LDHB) triggers hyperactivation of autophagy, a process implicated in tumorigenesis. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic modification of LDHB → autophagy surge. This connects mitochondrial acyl-metabolism control to lysosomal clearance. The net effect can be context-dependent in cancer biology.

SIRT5 desuccinylates and activates carbamoyl phosphate synthase 1 (CPS1), the rate-limiting enzyme of the urea cycle, enhancing ammonia detoxification into urea. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of CPS1. This is especially important during fasting or high-protein load when nitrogen must be cleared. It exemplifies SIRT5's role as a regulator of mitochondrial acyl-metabolism and nitrogen homeostasis.

SIRT5 inhibits preadipocyte differentiation by activating AMPK and repressing MAPK signaling, analogous to its broader adipogenesis-blocking role. The directionality is SIRT5 upstream of AMPK activation in adipogenic progenitors. Activated AMPK shifts cells away from lipogenesis. It reaffirms SIRT5 as a negative regulator of fat formation.

Unlike SIRT1–SIRT3, SIRT5 is relatively resistant to inhibition by physiological concentrations of nicotinamide, making its desuccinylase activity less sensitive to the natural feedback brake. The directionality is nicotinamide failing to strongly inhibit SIRT5. This may preserve SIRT5's metabolic functions even when NAD+ salvage flux generates nicotinamide. It distinguishes SIRT5's regulatory wiring from other sirtuins.

SIRT5 desuccinylates and activates HMGCS2 (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase 2), the rate-limiting enzyme of ketone-body synthesis, supporting energy production during fasting. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of HMGCS2. This promotes ketogenesis when carbohydrate is scarce. It is a fasting-adaptive function of SIRT5.

SIRT5 desuccinylates multiple fatty-acid β-oxidation enzymes including LCAD and ACADS, coordinating mitochondrial lipid catabolism. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of these acyl-CoA dehydrogenases. This supports energy harvest from fat. It exemplifies SIRT5's broad desuccinylase control of metabolism.

SIRT5 desuccinylates TCA-cycle enzymes IDH2 and SDHA, tuning their activity and coordinating mitochondrial energy metabolism. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic modulation of TCA flux. This helps match oxidation to demand during fasting or stress. It reinforces SIRT5's role as a central mitochondrial metabolic regulator.

SIRT5 activates superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) through desuccinylation, enhancing NADPH production and glutathione recycling for ROS detoxification. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of SOD1. This bolsters cytosolic antioxidant capacity. It extends SIRT5's protective actions beyond the mitochondria's own enzymes.

SIRT5 activates IDH2 through desuccinylation, enhancing its NADPH-producing activity and thereby supporting glutathione reduction and ROS scavenging. The directionality is SIRT5 upstream of IDH2-dependent redox buffering. This complements SOD1 activation in antioxidant defense. It shows SIRT5's desuccinylation broadly strengthens reductive capacity.

SIRT5 is the sole mammalian member of phylogenetic Class III, a group distributed widely across prokaryotes, marking it as one of the most ancient mammalian sirtuins. The directionality is evolutionary classification. Its prokaryotic origin aligns with SIRT5's fundamental mitochondrial metabolic functions. This situates SIRT5 at the root of sirtuin biology.

SIRT5 regulates ketogenesis by desuccinylating HMGCS2, the rate-limiting enzyme of ketone-body synthesis, enabling fuel production during fasting. The directionality is SIRT5 enzymatic activation of HMGCS2. This is a fasting-adaptive, energetically protective action. It reaffirms SIRT5's role in coordinating catabolic flux.

SIRT7 is concentrated in the nucleolus, the site of ribosomal DNA transcription and ribosome biogenesis, where it deacetylates histone H3K18 and regulates RNA polymerase I. Its nucleolar residence positions it to control rRNA synthesis and, consequently, protein synthetic capacity and growth. SIRT7 also deacetylates extra-nucleolar targets such as GATA4 and SMAD3, linking it to cardiac and fibrotic pathways. Deficiency of SIRT7 yields extensive myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyopathy, revealing its importance in stress responses of the heart.

SIRT7 expression is significantly elevated in breast carcinoma compared with normal breast tissue, and high SIRT7 correlates with poorer prognosis in several tumor types. Its overexpression supports tumor growth and ribosomal biogenesis, and it can deacetylate oncogenic transcription factors such as GATA4. The directionality is that increased SIRT7 abundance is associated with and likely promotes malignant phenotypes. A caveat is that sirtuin roles in cancer are context-dependent, and SIRT7 can be either tumor-promoting or, in some tissues, tumor-suppressive.

SIRT7 activates RNA polymerase I-mediated transcription of ribosomal DNA, driving ribosome biogenesis and protein synthetic capacity in proliferating cells. It does so in part through deacetylation of histone H3K18 at rDNA and by stabilizing the Pol I transcriptional apparatus. The directionality is SIRT7 → enhanced rRNA production → increased ribosome output. Because uncontrolled ribosome biogenesis fuels tumor growth, this activity aligns with SIRT7's oncogenic associations.

SIRT7 regulates rRNA transcription by activating RNA polymerase I and deacetylating histone H3K18 at ribosomal DNA, controlling ribosome biogenesis and protein synthetic capacity. The directionality is SIRT7 upstream of Pol I activity and ribosome production. Because excessive ribosome biogenesis fuels proliferation, this activity aligns SIRT7 with growth and, in cancer, with tumor promotion. It also ties SIRT7 to nucleolar stress responses.

SIRT7 is highly localized to the nucleolus and deacetylates histone H3K18 (H3K18ac), a mark associated with active rDNA transcription, thereby repressing ribosome biogenesis when deacetylated. The directionality is SIRT7 enzymatic removal of H3K18ac. Because excess ribosome production fuels growth and cancer, this repressive action can be tumor-suppressive in some contexts. It also stabilizes pericentric heterochromatin, supporting genome stability.

Knockdown of SIRT7 promotes nuclear translocation of NF-κB p-p65 and increases downstream inflammatory cytokines, whereas SIRT7 overexpression has the opposite effect by retaining NF-κB cytoplasmically. The directionality is SIRT7 upstream of blocked p65 nuclear entry. This reveals a non-canonical, deacetylation-independent mode of NF-κB control by SIRT7. It ties SIRT7 to tissue inflammation, including in kidney.

SIRT7 ameliorates stress-induced cardiac hypertrophy by interacting with and deacetylating GATA4, a key cardiac transcription factor, modulating its target-gene program. The directionality is SIRT7 enzymatic regulation of GATA4. This counters maladaptive hypertrophic signaling. It is a nuclear mechanism by which SIRT7 protects the myocardium.

Enhanced expression and phosphorylation of SIRT7 promotes cardiac fibrosis via activation of Smad2 and ERK signaling pathways. The directionality is SIRT7 upstream of fibrogenic signaling. This reveals a pathological, profibrotic side of SIRT7 in the heart, contrasting its nucleolar homeostatic roles. Thus SIRT7 can be maladaptive under stress despite protecting against hypertrophy in other settings.

SIRT7 regulates vascular smooth-muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation and migration through the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, limiting the neointimal hyperplasia that drives vascular disease. The directionality is SIRT7 upstream of VSMC quiescence. By restraining VSMC activation, SIRT7 protects against atherosclerotic and restenotic remodeling. It adds a vascular-stability role to SIRT7.

SIRT7 directly deacetylates SMAD3, reducing its transcriptional activity and pro-fibrotic output downstream of TGF-β1. The directionality is SIRT7 enzymatic inhibition of SMAD3. This reveals an antifibrotic, deacetylation-based action of SIRT7 that can oppose TGF-β1 signaling. It adds nuance to SIRT7's otherwise sometimes profibrotic cardiac role.

SIRT7 possesses NAD+-dependent deacetylase activity with high selectivity for histone H3 lysine 18 acetylation (H3K18ac), a mark of active transcription at rDNA and elsewhere. The directionality is SIRT7 enzymatic removal of H3K18ac. Deacetylation at pericentric heterochromatin maintains genomic stability and silences repetitive elements. This substrate specificity underlies SIRT7's roles in ribosome biogenesis and chromatin integrity.

SIRT7 deacetylates H3K18ac at pericentric heterochromatin, maintaining heterochromatic compaction and suppressing transcription of repetitive elements to preserve genomic stability. The directionality is SIRT7 upstream of heterochromatin stabilization. Loss of SIRT7 derepresses retrotransposons and increases genomic instability. This chromatin role complements SIRT7's nucleolar functions.

Overexpression of SIRT7 extends the replicative lifespan of primary human cells by maintaining rDNA stability and reducing mitochondrial dysfunction. The directionality is SIRT7 gain upstream of prolonged cellular lifespan. This mirrors the pro-longevity roles of other sirtuins. It supports a broadly conserved lifespan-promoting function for the family.

Integration of an extra SIR2 copy in yeast increases replicative lifespan by up to about 30%, implicating Sir2 dosage directly in longevity. The mechanism involves reinforced silencing at rDNA repeats, which reduces spurious recombination and the accumulation of extrachromosomal rDNA circles that drive aging. This is a gain-of-function, directional relationship: more Sir2 yields longer lifespan, though the effect saturates and very high doses can be detrimental. The finding established the foundational idea that boosting sirtuin activity can extend lifespan in a simple eukaryote.

A chromosomal duplication that increases sir-2.1 dosage in C. elegans extends lifespan by up to approximately 50%, paralleling the yeast finding in a multicellular organism. The longevity effect depends on intact insulin/IGF-1-like signaling, because sir-2.1 acts downstream of the DAF-2 pathway to promote stress resistance. The relationship is directional: elevated sir-2.1 produces the lifespan gain. A key caveat is that the requirement for DAF-16 (FOXO) ties sirtuin longevity to the conserved FOXO transcription-factor network.

The lifespan extension produced by sir-2.1 overexpression in C. elegans is strictly dependent on the forkhead transcription factor DAF-16, the worm FOXO ortholog. DAF-16 is the downstream effector that induces stress-resistance and xenobiotic-detoxification genes once sir-2.1 releases it from repression. Mechanistically, sir-2.1 deacetylates and cooperates with DAF-16 to drive the longevity transcriptional program. Thus the directionality is sir-2.1 → DAF-16 → lifespan, and removing DAF-16 abolishes the benefit.

Ubiquitous overexpression of the Drosophila Sir2 ortholog extends female lifespan by about 29%, with a more modest or absent effect in males. The sexually dimorphic response reflects differences in nutrient sensing and reproductive physiology between the sexes. Directionally, increased dSir2 acts upstream to produce the longevity phenotype, consistent with the conserved sirtuin-CR axis. As in worms, the effect is intertwined with insulin/FOXO signaling and dietary restriction pathways.

By deacetylating p53, SIRT1 lowers p53's transcriptional activation of BH3-only proteins and other apoptotic effectors, suppressing programmed cell death after oxidative or genotoxic stress. This creates a survival bias that helps cells tolerate damage but can also protect incipient cancer cells from elimination. The directionality is that SIRT1 activity on p53 is upstream of reduced apoptosis. A caveat is that chronic suppression of p53-dependent apoptosis is a double-edged sword: protective in normal tissue but potentially tumor-promoting.

HIC1 (hypermethylated in cancer 1) is a tumor suppressor that binds the SIRT1 promoter via its POZ domain and directly represses SIRT1 transcription. Because p53 transactivates HIC1, a negative feedback loop exists: p53 induces HIC1, which then restrains SIRT1, preventing excessive p53 deacetylation and preserving p53 tumor-suppressive capacity. The directionality is HIC1 → SIRT1 repression, upstream of SIRT1's inhibition of p53. Disruption of this loop in cancer can unleash SIRT1 to silence p53.

Once deacetylated by SIRT1, Ku70 binds the BH3 domain of the pro-apoptotic protein Bax and retains it in the cytosol, preventing Bax translocation to and permeabilization of mitochondria. This sequestration blocks the intrinsic apoptosis cascade downstream of many stress signals. The relationship is directional: deacetylated Ku70 is the binding partner that neutralizes Bax. The net effect is cytoprotection, though as with p53 suppression this can also shield damaged cells in oncogenic contexts.

The E2F1 transcription factor binds directly to the SIRT1 promoter and activates its transcription, particularly under proliferative or DNA-damage signals. This positions SIRT1 as a downstream effector of E2F1-driven programs that balance cell-cycle progression with survival. The directionality is E2F1 → SIRT1 gene activation. Notably, the relationship is reciprocal, because SIRT1 then feeds back to inhibit E2F1's apoptotic function.

links.context: Deacetylation of RelA/p65 by SIRT1 lowers NF-κB transactivation, thereby reducing expression of cytokines, chemokines, and adhesion molecules that propagate inflammation. This directly opposes the pro-inflammatory program and underlies many of SIRT1's protective effects in metabolic, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative contexts. The directionality is SIRT1 deacetylation → suppressed NF-κB signaling. A caveat is that excessive NF-κB suppression could impair host defense, so the effect is beneficial within physiological ranges.

SIRT2 protein levels rise dramatically as cells enter mitosis and the enzyme is hyperphosphorylated at the G2/M boundary, timing its activity to chromosome condensation and division. This cell-cycle coupling links SIRT2 to proper mitotic progression and genomic stability. The directionality is that the G2/M transition drives SIRT2 upregulation and activation. Loss or dysregulation of this peak is associated with mitotic defects and, in some cancers, genomic instability.

Mice lacking SIRT6 develop a striking premature-aging syndrome with reduced size, loss of subcutaneous fat, lymphopenia, colitis, and spinal curvature, dying early. The phenotype reflects defective base-excision repair, genomic instability, and metabolic and inflammatory dysregulation. The directionality is SIRT6 deficiency → multisystem premature aging. This makes SIRT6 one of the clearest single-gene links between sirtuins and mammalian longevity.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: Because deacetylated Tat is a more potent transactivator, SIRT1-mediated deacetylation at Lys50 boosts HIV-1 transcription from the proviral LTR. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts on Tat to amplify viral gene expression. This positions host SIRT1 as a cofactor that HIV exploits, a caveat to the generally beneficial reputation of SIRT1 activation. Targeting this interaction is of interest for antiviral strategies.

Repression of UCP2 by SIRT1 preserves mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP synthesis in pancreatic β-cells, which raises the ATP/ADP ratio and closes KATP channels to trigger insulin release. Mice overexpressing SIRT1 in β-cells show enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. The directionality is SIRT1 → UCP2 downregulation → stronger insulin secretion. This links SIRT1 to improved glucose homeostasis and protection against diabetes.

By inhibiting GDH, SIRT4 blunts the ability of amino acids such as leucine to stimulate insulin release from pancreatic β-cells, because less α-ketoglutarate is generated to elevate ATP and trigger secretion. The relationship is directional: SIRT4-mediated GDH inhibition → reduced amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion. This positions SIRT4 as a physiological negative regulator of nutrient-particular insulin release.

In mice on a high-calorie diet, resveratrol increases mitochondrial number and function, an effect accompanied by elevated SIRT1 and PGC-1α activity. This shift counters diet-induced metabolic dysfunction by improving oxidative capacity. The directionality is resveratrol upstream, activating SIRT1/PGC-1α to drive mitochondrial biogenesis. The finding helped popularize resveratrol as a CR-mimetic against diet-induced obesity.

A polymorphism in an intron-5 enhancer of the SIRT3 gene is associated with exceptional longevity (age beyond 90 years) specifically in men. The variant is thought to alter SIRT3 expression or regulation, conferring enhanced mitochondrial stress resistance. The directionality is genetic variation associated with, and putatively causal of, prolonged lifespan. As a correlation, it supports but does not prove that higher SIRT3 activity promotes human longevity.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: Several single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the human SIRT1 gene are significantly associated with systemic energy expenditure in Finnish cohorts, suggesting that SIRT1 variation influences metabolic rate. These variants may alter SIRT1 expression or activity, shifting how individuals burn fuel. The directionality is genetic SIRT1 variation linked to energy-expenditure phenotype. As with most GWAS associations, effect sizes are modest and context-dependent.

Nmnat, the NAD+-biosynthetic enzyme, protects axons from Wallerian degeneration largely by raising NAD+ and thereby activating SIRT1, which supports axonal survival after injury. The protection is upstream of SIRT1-dependent maintenance of mitochondrial and chromatin function in neurons. The directionality is Nmnat → NAD+ → SIRT1 → axonal protection. This established a key NAD+/sirtuin axis in neuronal resilience.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: By promoting degradation of Smad7, SIRT1 deacetylation tempers TGF-β signaling in glomerular mesangial cells and protects them from TGF-β-dependent apoptosis. The relationship is directional: SIRT1 acts on Smad7 to relieve a pro-apoptotic TGF-β output. This renoprotective mechanism is relevant to diabetic nephropathy and other glomerulopathies. It illustrates how sirtuin control of a single substrate can determine cell fate in injury.

SIRT1-mediated deacetylation and degradation of H2A.Z helps protect the heart from failure by removing a histone variant that drives maladaptive cardiac hypertrophic gene programs. The directionality is SIRT1 → H2A.Z loss → attenuated hypertrophy. This is a mechanistically plausible explanation for why SIRT1 activation is cardioprotective, though the in vivo evidence carries moderate confidence (0.75). It links chromatin dynamics directly to heart disease resistance.

In hepatocarcinoma, p33ING1b binds SIRT1 and blocks its ability to deacetylate p53, thereby preserving p53's transcriptional activity, including repression of α-fetoprotein (AFP). This relieves SIRT1-mediated inhibition of p53 tumor suppression. The directionality is p33ING1b antagonizing SIRT1 at the p53 node. The interaction reveals a tissue-specific brake on SIRT1's pro-survival, potentially oncogenic, action.

Administration of adiponectin to obese, high-fat-fed mice improves insulin sensitivity and lowers blood glucose, reflecting its role as a insulin-sensitizing adipokine. It acts through AdipoR1/2 receptors to activate AMPK and PPAR-α pathways that enhance fatty-acid oxidation. The directionality is adiponectin upstream of improved insulin action. Because SIRT1 raises adiponectin, this forms part of SIRT1's anti-diabetic circuitry.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: Mice lacking PGC-1α are markedly more sensitive to neuronal loss induced by MPTP (a dopaminergic toxin) and kainic acid (an excitotoxin), revealing PGC-1α's role in neuronal stress resistance. Because SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, this sensitivity indirectly implicates the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis in neuroprotection. The directionality is PGC-1α deficiency → heightened vulnerability. The phenotype mirrors features of Parkinson's and other neurodegenerative models.
Daratumumab is a clinically approved IgG1 antibody for multiple myeloma that binds and neutralizes CD38. Potential repurposing at low doses for NAD+ preservation. [HYPOTHESIS: repurposing proposal]

Daratumumab is a frontline anti-CD38 antibody therapy for multiple myeloma, where CD38 is highly expressed on malignant plasma cells. Its clinical efficacy stems from direct and immune-mediated elimination of these cells. The directionality is daratumumab upstream of myeloma cell clearance. Beyond oncology, its CD38 inhibition has the secondary effect of sparing NAD+ pools that sirtuins depend on.

Isatuximab (Sarclisa) is an IgG1 anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody, approved around 2020/2021, that binds a different CD38 epitope than daratumumab. It mediates direct apoptosis and immune effector functions against CD38+ multiple myeloma cells. The directionality is antibody → CD38 engagement → tumor cell death. Like daratumumab, it also lowers CD38 ectoenzyme activity, indirectly preserving NAD+ for sirtuins.

Inhibiting PDE4 prevents cAMP degradation, so intracellular cAMP accumulates after resveratrol exposure. The directionality is PDE4 inhibition → elevated cAMP. Elevated cAMP then activates the exchange protein Epac1, propagating a calcium and AMPK signal that ultimately boosts NAD+ and SIRT1. This pathway explains how resveratrol can activate SIRT1 even through non-allosteric means.

High intracellular cAMP activates Epac1 (Exchange Protein directly Activated by cAMP), a guanine-nucleotide-exchange factor that triggers downstream signaling independent of PKA. The directionality is cAMP upstream of Epac1 activation. Epac1 then stimulates calcium release from the ER, linking cAMP to Ca2+-dependent kinases. This step is pivotal in resveratrol's indirect SIRT1-activation cascade.

Epac1 activation induces calcium release from the endoplasmic reticulum into the cytoplasm, raising cytosolic Ca2+ that serves as a second messenger. The directionality is Epac1 upstream of cytoplasmic Ca2+ elevation. The Ca2+ surge then activates CaMKKβ, bridging cAMP signaling to AMPK. This couples resveratrol's PDE4 inhibition to metabolic kinase activation.

The cytoplasmic calcium surge activates calmodulin-dependent protein kinase kinase β (CaMKKβ), which phosphorylates and activates AMPK, the central cellular energy sensor. The directionality is Ca2+ → CaMKKβ → AMPK phosphorylation. Activated AMPK then induces NAMPT and raises NAD+, closing the loop on SIRT1 activation. This is a key branch point linking calcium flux to metabolic homeostasis.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: Activated AMPK increases expression of NAMPT, the rate-limiting enzyme of the NAD+ salvage pathway that converts nicotinamide to NMN. The directionality is AMPK upstream of NAMPT induction. More NAMPT elevates intracellular NAD+, the obligate co-substrate for sirtuins. This AMPK→NAMPT→NAD+ axis is a major indirect route by which resveratrol and exercise activate SIRT1.

NAMPT is the rate-limiting enzyme in the NAD+ salvage pathway, so its upregulation raises cellular NAD+ levels and fuels sirtuin activity. The directionality is NAMPT increase → NAD+ increase → enhanced sirtuin function. This is the terminal step of resveratrol's indirect activation cascade. Preserving NAD+ via NAMPT (or CD38 inhibition) is a common theme across sirtuin-activating strategies.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: Deacetylated FOXO3a transcriptionally upregulates endogenous antioxidant enzymes, prominently mitochondrial SOD2 and catalase, bolstering ROS scavenging. The directionality is SIRT1/FOXO3a upstream of increased antioxidant capacity. This reduces oxidative damage in resveratrol-treated cells and animals. It is a central mechanism for sirtuin-mediated protection against aging and metabolic disease.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: By deacetylating NF-κB, SIRT1 reduces transcription of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, dampening the inflammatory transcriptome. The directionality is SIRT1/NF-κB upstream of lower cytokine output. This is mechanistically important in atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration, and metabolic inflammation. Resveratrol leverages this axis to curb chronic low-grade inflammation.

Resveratrol-activated endothelial SIRT1 increases eNOS expression and deacetylates/activates it, enhancing nitric-oxide production and promoting vasodilation. The directionality is SIRT1 upstream of eNOS activation. Improved NO bioavailability lowers vascular tone and protects against endothelial dysfunction. This underlies resveratrol's cardiovascular and 'French paradox' associations.

Through the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α pathway, resveratrol reduces hepatic steatosis in diet-induced obesity models by enhancing fatty-acid oxidation and mitochondrial function while limiting lipogenesis. The directionality is SIRT1 activation upstream of reduced liver fat accumulation. This demonstrates a translational metabolic benefit of sirtuin activation. Human efficacy, however, is limited by resveratrol's poor bioavailability.

Dihydromyricetin (DHM), a flavonoid from vine tea, activates SIRT3 mitochondrial deacetylase activity, leading to MnSOD deacetylation and lowered ROS. The directionality is DHM upstream of SIRT3 activation. This mitochondrial action underlies DHM's hepatoprotective and metabolic benefits. DHM also activates AMPK, synergizing with SIRT3 via NAD+ elevation.

DHM activates AMPK, which synergistically raises NAD+ via NAMPT upregulation and thereby further potentiates SIRT3 activity. The directionality is DHM → AMPK → NAD+ → SIRT3. This dual SIRT3/AMPK engagement amplifies mitochondrial and metabolic defenses. It mirrors the indirect resveratrol cascade, suggesting convergent circuitry among polyphenols.

Vine tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata) leaves contain 20–30% dihydromyricetin (DHM) by weight, so 1–1.5 g dry leaf suffices for a ~300 mg therapeutic dose. The directionality is botanical source upstream of DHM availability. DHM is a potent SIRT3/AMPK activator. This makes vine tea a practical natural source of the compound.

UBCS039 is a pyrrolo[1,2-a]quinoxaline reported as the first synthetic activator of SIRT6 deacetylase activity (EC50 = 38 μM), binding the distal hydrophobic pocket. The directionality is UBCS039 allosterically enhancing SIRT6. It stimulates chromatin compaction, glycolysis suppression, and antifibrotic programs. UBCS039 validated SIRT6 as a druggable longevity target.

MDL-801 is a potent, cell-permeable synthetic allosteric activator of SIRT6 that binds the hydrophobic pocket and stimulates its deacetylase activity (EC50 ≈ 10.3 μM). The directionality is MDL-801 upstream of SIRT6 activation. It mirrors UBCS039 but with greater potency and cell permeability. MDL-801 mitigates kidney fibrosis and suppresses glycolytic, tumor-promoting metabolism.

Cyanidin, a natural anthocyanidin from red berries, increases SIRT6 activity by over 50-fold in certain in vitro assays, making it one of the most powerful natural SIRT6 activators. The directionality is cyanidin upstream of SIRT6 stimulation. Its potency suggests strong binding to the SIRT6 activation pocket. This links berry polyphenols to SIRT6-dependent metabolic and anti-aging effects.

Direct SIRT2 activation is generally avoided therapeutically because overactivity is linked to neurotoxicity in neurodegenerative contexts, where excessive deacetylation may impair microtubule and protein-homeostasis defenses. The directionality is SIRT2 overactivity associated with neuronal damage. Consequently, SIRT2 inhibitors are pursued for Parkinson's and Huntington's disease. This contrasts with most other sirtuins, where activation is sought.

Selective SIRT2 inhibitors such as AGK2, AK-7, and SirReal2 are investigated in neurodegenerative disease models because blocking SIRT2 preserves α-tubulin acetylation and protects neurons from aggregation toxicity. The directionality is SIRT2 inhibition → microtubule stability → neuroprotection. These agents rescue dopaminergic neurons from α-synuclein toxicity and confer ischemic protection. The approach exploits the inverse therapeutic logic of SIRT2 versus other sirtuins.

NMN is a direct NAD+ precursor that, once converted to NAD+, serves as a universal indirect pan-sirtuin activator by supplying the obligate co-substrate for all seven sirtuins. The directionality is NMN → NAD+ → sirtuin activation. It raises NAD+ levels that decline with age, restoring sirtuin function systemically. NMN (with NR) is a leading nutraceutical strategy to counteract age-related sirtuin attenuation.

Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is an NAD+ precursor that raises cellular NAD+ and thereby indirectly activates all seven sirtuins by supplying their shared co-substrate. The directionality is NR → NAD+ → pan-sirtuin activation. Like NMN, NR reverses age-related NAD+ decline and restores sirtuin-dependent maintenance. It is a leading nutraceutical approach to broadly engage sirtuin biology.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: Kidney-specific SIRT7 knockout mice show diminished inflammation with reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 and suppressed nuclear NF-κB p65 accumulation, indicating SIRT7 normally promotes renal NF-κB activation. The directionality is SIRT7 loss → less nuclear p65 → lower inflammation. This is somewhat counterintuitive given SIRT7's usual anti-inflammatory renal role elsewhere, underscoring context dependence. It suggests SIRT7 can be pro-inflammatory in specific renal settings.

The microRNA miR-217 negatively regulates SIRT1 by binding its 3'UTR and repressing translation, thereby diminishing SIRT1's anti-inflammatory and metabolic functions. The directionality is miR-217 upstream of lowered SIRT1. Downregulation of miR-217 mitigates inflammatory responses via the SIRT1/AMPK/NF-κB axis. This exemplifies miRNA fine-tuning of sirtuin abundance.

miR-543 represses SIRT1 expression post-transcriptionally, and its downregulation reduces inflammation by strengthening the SIRT1/AMPK/NF-κB signaling pathway. The directionality is miR-543 upstream of SIRT1 suppression. This places miR-543 among miRNAs that calibrate inflammatory tone. Modulating such miRNAs is a potential anti-inflammatory strategy.

miR-378 reduces SIRT1 activity and facilitates NF-κB-TNFα inflammatory signaling, in part by targeting the 5'-AMPK subunit gamma-2. The directionality is miR-378 → SIRT1 inhibition → NF-κB activation. This links a metabolic miRNA to sirtuin-controlled inflammation. It illustrates how miRNA networks gate sirtuin protective effects.

MCPIP1 (monocyte chemoattractant protein-induced protein 1), an RNase, alleviates inflammatory responses by promoting SIRT1 expression through modulation of miR-9. The directionality is MCPIP1 upstream of increased SIRT1. Higher SIRT1 then suppresses NF-κB-driven inflammation. This reveals an anti-inflammatory circuit centered on SIRT1 induction.

MDL-800 is a bis-benzenesulfonamide prodrug and potent, selective SIRT6 activator (EC50 = 10.3 μM) that stimulates SIRT6 deacetylase activity. The directionality is MDL-800 allosteric activation of SIRT6. It mirrors UBCS039 but with greater potency and cell permeability, mitigating kidney fibrosis and tumor glycolysis. It is a lead chemical tool for SIRT6 biology.

The SIRT6 activator MDL-800 mitigates unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO)-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis, validating SIRT6 activation therapeutically. The directionality is MDL-800 → SIRT6 activation → renal protection. This complements other evidence that SIRT6 restrains TGF-β/Smad3 fibrogenesis. It supports SIRT6 as a target for chronic kidney disease.

EX-527 (Selisistat) is the first known selective, cell-permeable SIRT1 inhibitor (IC50 = 0.098 μM) with minimal activity against SIRT2/3. The directionality is EX-527 blocking SIRT1 catalysis. It is used to dissect SIRT1-dependent phenotypes and was explored clinically for Huntington's disease. As a SIRT1 blocker, its effects contrast with STACs like resveratrol.

SirReal2 is a potent SIRT2 inhibitor (IC50 = 0.14 μM) with minimal effects on SIRT1 and SIRT3, exploiting a SIRT2-specific binding pocket. The directionality is SirReal2 blocking SIRT2 deacetylase activity. It is a key chemical probe for SIRT2 biology in neurodegeneration and cancer. Selectivity makes it valuable for isolating SIRT2-specific effects.

Suramin, a polyanionic urea derivative, inhibits sirtuins with IC50 values of ~297 nM, 1150 nM, and 22 μM for SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT5 respectively, showing relative selectivity for SIRT5 at higher concentrations. The directionality is suramin blocking sirtuin catalysis. Its broad activity limits specificity, but it remains a tool to probe SIRT5. Clinically, suramin is an antiparasitic and anticancer agent with off-target sirtuin effects.

SIRT6 deficiency in macrophages increases acetylation and stability of FoxO1, leading to sustained FoxO1 protein and an inflammatory state. The directionality is SIRT6 loss → hyperacetylated, stabilized FoxO1. Because SIRT6 normally deacetylates FoxO1, its absence prolongs FoxO1 signaling. This reveals a macrophage-intrinsic mechanism linking SIRT6 to inflammation resolution.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: Deacetylation of LDHB by SIRT5 hyperactivates autophagy, accelerating cellular self-digestion and influencing tumor cell survival and metabolism. The directionality is SIRT5/LDHB upstream of autophagic hyperactivation. This can support tumor cell fitness under stress but may also provoke cell-death programs. It exemplifies SIRT5's role at the autophagy–metabolism interface.

links.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
links.context: Nuclear SIRT1, enhanced by resveratrol, induces superoxide dismutase in cardiomyocytes, an antioxidant enzyme that suppresses cell death under stress. The directionality is nuclear SIRT1 upstream of SOD induction. This is a cardiomyoprotective output of resveratrol's SIRT1 activation. It complements SIRT1's eNOS and metabolic cardiac actions.

SIRT3-deficient mice develop severe cardiac hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis when challenged with a hypertrophic stimulus, revealing SIRT3's protective role in the heart. The directionality is SIRT3 loss → pathological cardiac remodeling. This is driven by elevated ROS and impaired mitochondrial function. It mirrors the resistance seen when SIRT3 is overexpressed.

Transgenic mice overexpressing SIRT3 are significantly resistant to stimuli-induced cardiac hypertrophy, the inverse of the SIRT3-null phenotype. The directionality is SIRT3 gain → hypertrophy resistance. This protection arises from better mitochondrial ROS control and metabolic flexibility. It validates SIRT3 as a cardiac therapeutic target.

SIRT7-deficient mice show extensive myocardial fibrosis, high basal apoptosis, and cardiomyopathy, reflecting SIRT7's role in maintaining cardiac homeostasis. The directionality is SIRT7 loss → fibrotic cardiomyopathy. This contrasts with contexts where SIRT7 promotes fibrosis under stress. It indicates SIRT7 is overall required for myocardial integrity.

links.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
links.context: Resveratrol achieves efficacious levels only when ingested within the red-wine matrix, which contains co-constituents that slow its metabolism and improve exposure. The directionality is matrix components upstream of better resveratrol bioavailability. This helps resolve discrepancies between in vitro potency and in vivo human trials. It supports whole-food over isolated-compound approaches.

links.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin System The Holy Grail of Resveratrol?.md
links.context: Quercetin and ethanol, red-wine constituents, augment resveratrol activity possibly by inhibiting its catabolic enzymes and improving exposure (moderate confidence 0.75). The directionality is these co-compounds upstream of enhanced resveratrol effect. This helps explain the matrix/bioavailability phenomenon. It suggests combination formulations could improve efficacy.

The French paradox describes lower cardiovascular-disease incidence in some French populations despite high-fat diets, often attributed in part to moderate wine (and resveratrol) consumption. The directionality is moderate wine intake upstream of reduced CVD in this epidemiological observation. Causality is debated, with diet and lifestyle confounders. Resveratrol's vascular actions provide a plausible—but not proven—mechanism.

SIRT1-mediated downregulation of AT1R expression produces antihypertensive effects; in vivo, resveratrol-driven SIRT1 elevation reduces angiotensin-II-induced hypertension. The directionality is SIRT1/AT1R suppression upstream of lower blood pressure. This couples SIRT1 activation to vascular tone control. It is a mechanistic basis for resveratrol's antihypertensive actions.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: Beclin1 scaffolds four class III PI3K complexes (I/Atg14L, II/UVRAG, III/UVRAG+Rubicon, IV/Bif-1) that regulate autophagy at initiation, nucleation, and maturation stages. The directionality is Beclin1 upstream of autophagosome machinery assembly. SIRT1 deacetylates Beclin1 to enhance Vps34 activity. This makes Beclin1 a hub integrating sirtuin signals into autophagy.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: TGF-β1 binds the type II receptor (TβRII), which recruits and phosphorylates the type I receptor (TβRI), leading to phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of SMAD2/3 to drive fibrotic transcription. The directionality is TGF-β1 upstream of SMAD3 activation. This canonical pathway is the main driver of pathological fibrosis across organs. Sirtuins such as SIRT6 and SIRT7 intersect this axis at multiple points.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: TGF-β1 activates SMAD3-dependent transcription of pro-fibrotic genes (COL1A1, COL3A1, FN1, ACTA2, TIMP1), driving collagen deposition and tissue scarring in multiple organs. The directionality is TGF-β1 upstream of fibrogenesis. This makes TGF-β1 a central target in fibrosis therapeutics. Sirtuins that inhibit SMAD3 signaling (SIRT6, SIRT7) are antifibrotic.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: Hyperactivated SMAD3 binds the 3'-UTR of the TFEB gene and inhibits its transcription, reducing lysosomal biogenesis and autophagic flux during fibrosis. The directionality is SMAD3 upstream of TFEB repression. This links TGF-β1 signaling to impaired autophagy and waste clearance. Sirtuin modulation of SMAD3 can therefore influence TFEB-dependent homeostasis.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: BRCA1 is recruited to DNA double-strand breaks by the MRN complex, promotes end resection, and facilitates RAD51 loading via PALB2/BRCA2 to execute homologous recombination repair. The directionality is BRCA1 upstream of high-fidelity DSB repair. Loss of BRCA1 cripples HR, increasing mutation and cancer risk. Sirtuins such as SIRT2 support BRCA1 localization to damage sites.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: Loss of BRCA1 triggers increased autophagy as a compensatory survival mechanism in breast and ovarian cancers, buffering the viability impact of defective homologous recombination. The directionality is BRCA1 deficiency upstream of autophagic upregulation. This metabolic rewiring can be co-opted by tumors. It connects genome-maintenance failure to lysosomal clearance pathways.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: BRCA1-deficient tumors are exquisitely sensitive to PARP inhibitors because blocking base-excision (PARP) repair in the setting of defective homologous recombination causes catastrophic, lethal DNA damage (synthetic lethality). The directionality is BRCA1 mutation upstream of PARP-inhibitor vulnerability. This is a cornerstone of precision oncology. It illustrates how repair-pathway context determines therapeutic selectivity.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: Germline loss-of-function mutations in STK11 (LKB1) cause Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, characterized by hamartomatous polyps and elevated cancer risk. The directionality is LKB1 deficiency upstream of this cancer predisposition. This highlights LKB1 as a critical tumor suppressor and metabolic regulator. Its connection to AMPK/sirtuin axes explains the metabolic features.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: The BH3 domain of Beclin1 binds anti-apoptotic Bcl-2/Bcl-xL proteins, which sequester it and inhibit autophagy, linking apoptosis and autophagy regulation. The directionality is Bcl-2 upstream of Beclin1 sequestration. SIRT1 deacetylation of Beclin1 modulates this interaction. This illustrates the molecular crosstalk between cell-death and clearance pathways.

Black elderberries provide roughly 350–450 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100 g fresh fruit, with ~70–85 g reaching a 300 mg therapeutic dose. The directionality is berry content upstream of anthocyanin intake. Cyanidin is a powerful natural SIRT6 activator. It positions elderberry as a dietary SIRT6-modulating food.

Tenovin-6 inhibits SIRT2 with IC50 = 10 µM, making SIRT2 its more potent sirtuin target compared with SIRT1. The directionality is Tenovin-6 blocking SIRT2 catalysis. By inhibiting SIRT2 deacetylation, it can protect neurons and reactivate p53. It is a chemical probe distinguishing SIRT2 from other sirtuins.

Tenovin-6 shows moderate inhibitory activity against SIRT3 with IC50 = 67 µM, weaker than its SIRT2 effect. The directionality is Tenovin-6 blocking SIRT3. This broader sirtuin inhibition contributes to its anticancer phenotype. Selectivity remains limited, so effects on SIRT1/2/3 overlap.

By inhibiting SIRT1/SIRT2-mediated deacetylation, Tenovins promote p53 hyperacetylation and reactivation of p53-dependent transcriptional networks. The directionality is Tenovin-mediated sirtuin inhibition upstream of p53 activation. This restores p53 tumor-suppressive function in cells where sirtuins silence it. It is the basis for Tenovins' anticancer activity.

Tenovin-1 and Tenovin-6 significantly delay tumor growth in human cancer mouse xenografts (BL2 and ARN8) at single-digit micromolar concentrations. The directionality is Tenovin treatment upstream of reduced tumor growth. This effect is attributed to p53 reactivation and sirtuin inhibition. It validates sirtuin inhibition as an anticancer strategy in p53-wild-type tumors.

Splitomicin inhibits human SIRT1 with IC50 = 96 µM in vitro by blocking NAD+-dependent deacetylation. The directionality is Splitomicin upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It is an early-tool sirtuin inhibitor used to probe SIRT1 phenotypes. Its moderate potency limits in vivo utility.

Splitomicin inhibits human SIRT2 with IC50 = 113 µM in vitro, similar in range to its SIRT1 activity. The directionality is Splitomicin blocking SIRT2. This dual SIRT1/2 inhibition raises NF-κB acetylation and inflammation. It is a research probe rather than a selective therapeutic.

Splitomicin reduces intracellular deacetylase activity, causing hyperacetylation and enhanced nuclear translocation of NF-κB p65, amplifying inflammatory transcription. The directionality is Splitomicin (sirtuin inhibition) upstream of increased NF-κB signaling. This demonstrates the converse of SIRT1's normal anti-inflammatory action. It shows experimentally that sirtuin tone sets inflammatory set-points.

In ischemic-preconditioning models, Splitomicin reverses protective lysine deacetylation and abolishes preconditioning-induced cardioprotection. The directionality is Splitomicin (sirtuin inhibition) upstream of lost cardiac protection. This indicates sirtuin deacetylase activity is required for ischemic tolerance. It argues that sirtuin activation, not inhibition, protects the heart.

Cambinol inhibits human SIRT1 with IC50 = 56 µM by blocking access to both NAD+ and acetyl-lysine substrate-binding regions. The directionality is Cambinol upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It also inhibits SIRT2, with minimal activity against SIRT3 or class I/II HDACs. Cambinol sensitizes cancer cells to chemotherapy and suppresses invasion.

Cambinol inhibits human SIRT2 with IC50 = 59 µM and minimal activity against SIRT3 or other HDACs. The directionality is Cambinol blocking SIRT2. Combined with SIRT1 inhibition, it reactivates apoptotic programs in cancer. This dual inhibition underlies its anticancer phenotype.

In hepatocellular and lung cancer cells, Cambinol impairs migration and invasion in a dose-dependent manner, consistent with sirtuin inhibition reducing metastatic behaviors. The directionality is Cambinol upstream of suppressed motility. This suggests sirtuin blockers may limit metastasis. It complements Cambinol's chemotherapy-sensitizing effects.

Cambinol combination with chemotherapeutic agents dramatically sensitizes cancer cells to chemotherapy-induced apoptosis. The directionality is Cambinol upstream of enhanced chemosensitivity. By inhibiting SIRT1/2, it removes survival signals that protect tumor cells. This supports sirtuin inhibition as a chemosensitization strategy.

Salermide is a potent synthetic sirtuin inhibitor with improved potency against SIRT1 relative to the parent compound sirtinol. The directionality is Salermide blocking SIRT1 deacetylase activity. This reactivates proapoptotic genes silenced by SIRT1 in cancer. It is a research and anticancer chemical probe.

Salermide also potently inhibits SIRT2 compared with sirtinol, broadening its sirtuin-blocking profile. The directionality is Salermide upstream of SIRT2 inhibition. Combined SIRT1/2 blockade shifts cells toward apoptosis and differentiation. This dual action underlies its anticancer effects.

Salermide inhibits SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of H4K16, leading to epigenetic reactivation of proapoptotic genes aberrantly repressed in cancer cells. The directionality is Salermide → H4K16 hyperacetylation → apoptosis gene expression. This removes a chromatin-based survival brake. It is a mechanistic rationale for sirtuin-inhibitor cancer therapy.

Salermide induces robust apoptosis in leukemia (MOLT4), breast (MDA-MB-231), and colon (RKO) cancer cells, validating broad antitumor activity. The directionality is Salermide treatment upstream of cancer-cell death. This is consistent with SIRT1/2 inhibition removing survival signaling. It supports sirtuin blockers as anticancer agents.

Salermide inhibits colorectal carcinoma cancer-stem-cell self-renewal and reduces tumorigenesis, targeting the resilient stem-cell fraction. The directionality is Salermide upstream of stem-cell suppression. This is important because stem cells drive relapse. It extends sirtuin-inhibitor effects to the tumor-initiation compartment.

Sirtinol inhibits SIRT1 with IC50 ≈ 131 µM, preventing deacetylation of histones and non-histone targets. The directionality is Sirtinol upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. It is the parent compound of salermide and a classic sirtuin research tool. Its weaker potency spurred development of derivatives like salermide.

Sirtinol inhibits SIRT2 with IC50 ≈ 38–68 µM across assays, showing comparable or stronger activity against SIRT2 than SIRT1. The directionality is Sirtinol blocking SIRT2. This dual inhibition drives senescence and cell death phenotypes. It established the sirtuin-inhibitor chemical scaffold.

Sirtinol induces senescence-like growth arrest in human lung cancer H1299 cells, consistent with sirtuin inhibition engaging tumor-suppressive programs. The directionality is Sirtinol upstream of growth arrest. This phenotype mirrors aspects of SIRT1 loss. It suggests sirtuin blockers can blunt proliferation.

In MCF-7 breast cancer cells, sirtinol triggers both apoptotic and autophagic programmed cell death, reflecting disrupted survival homeostasis. The directionality is Sirtinol upstream of dual cell-death activation. This is attributed to SIRT1/2 inhibition removing anti-apoptotic deacetylation. It illustrates the pleiotropic anticancer potential of sirtuin blockers.

78c is a highly potent, selective, orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of CD38 NAD+-glycohydrolase activity. The directionality is 78c upstream of CD38 blockade. By stopping NAD+ consumption, it spares the co-substrate for sirtuins. This is a leading age-reversal NAD+-preservation strategy.

By selectively inhibiting CD38, 78c prevents age-related NAD+ degradation, keeping cellular pools high in aged animals. The directionality is CD38 inhibition upstream of preserved NAD+. Higher NAD+ then fuels sirtuin and other NAD+-dependent enzymes. This reverses a hallmark of aging.

78c indirectly boosts SIRT1 and SIRT3 by maintaining NAD+ co-substrate availability, restoring their deacetylase function in aged tissue. The directionality is NAD+ preservation upstream of sirtuin reactivation. This is an indirect 'pan-sirtuin' approach distinct from direct STACs. It links CD38 pharmacology to longevity pathways.

links.relation: extends lifespan in male mice by
links.context: Administration of 78c to naturally aged male mice yields about a 14% lifespan extension, demonstrating in vivo geroprotective efficacy. The directionality is CD38 inhibition upstream of prolonged lifespan. This effect is attributed to restored NAD+/sirtuin function. It validates CD38 as a longevity drug target.

78c enhances the efficacy of NAD+ precursors NMN and NR by preventing their rapid CD38-mediated degradation, combining supply and preservation. The directionality is 78c + precursors upstream of amplified NAD+ and sirtuin activation. This synergy is a rational anti-aging combination. It overcomes the limited durability of precursors alone.

Distinctively, fucoidan preferentially stimulates SIRT6's ADP-ribosyltransferase activity rather than its deacetylase activity. The directionality is fucoidan upstream of SIRT6 ADP-ribosylation. This recruits KAP1/HP1α to silence repetitive elements. It makes fucoidan a mechanistically unique SIRT6 activator.

Fucoidan-FV (50–100 µg/mL) reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria (HGPS) patient-derived fibroblasts, indicating suppressed retrotransposition. The directionality is fucoidan/SIRT6 upstream of LINE-1 silencing. This addresses a progeria-associated chromatin defect. It supports SIRT6 in repetitive-element control.

SIRT6-activating fucoidan extends healthspan and lifespan in aged wild-type mice, confirming in vivo geroprotection. The directionality is fucoidan upstream of improved survival and function. This mirrors the longevity association of centenarian SIRT6 variants. It positions fucoidan as a natural SIRT6-targeted intervention.

ML385 binds the NRF2 bZIP domain, blocking its heterodimerization with small Maf proteins and preventing ARE-driven antioxidant transcription. The directionality is ML385 upstream of NRF2 inhibition. Because SIRT1 activates NRF2, ML385 can be used to disrupt that axis experimentally. It is a tool to dissect NRF2-dependent cytoprotection.

AGK2 is a highly selective SIRT2 inhibitor (IC50 = 3.5 µM) with over 10-fold selectivity over SIRT1 and SIRT3. The directionality is AGK2 blocking SIRT2. Its selectivity makes it the preferred probe for SIRT2-specific biology. It rescues neurons in Parkinson's models, supporting SIRT2 inhibition therapeutically.

AGK2-mediated SIRT2 inhibition prevents deacetylation of α-tubulin and microtubule elements, suppressing aggregation and protecting dopaminergic neuron viability in Parkinson's models. The directionality is AGK2/SIRT2 inhibition upstream of neuronal rescue. This targets the microtubule instability underlying synuclein toxicity. It is a leading SIRT2-inhibition neurodegenerative strategy.

AGK2 confers neuroprotection under ischemic/hypoxic conditions by suppressing phospho-JNK and FOXO3a and preventing caspase-3 cleavage. The directionality is AGK2/SIRT2 inhibition upstream of reduced neuronal death. This broadens AGK2's neuroprotective utility beyond proteinopathy. It reinforces the inverse therapeutic logic for SIRT2.

Centenarian-associated SIRT6 variants (N308K/A313S) elevate endogenous SIRT6 protein through a weakened interaction with vimentin, independent of mRNA changes. The directionality is variant → reduced vimentin binding → higher SIRT6. This suggests protein stability, not expression, drives the longevity phenotype. It links a human genetic finding to SIRT6 abundance.

The N308K substitution selectively reduces SIRT6–vimentin interaction, which normally promotes SIRT6 degradation, thereby increasing SIRT6 protein levels. The directionality is N308K upstream of weakened vimentin binding. This stabilizes SIRT6 and enhances its functional output. It is the molecular explanation for the centenarian variant phenotype.

Vimentin interaction with SIRT6 promotes its proteasomal degradation; weakening this interaction in centenarian variants elevates SIRT6 levels. The directionality is vimentin upstream of SIRT6 turnover. This makes vimentin a negative regulator of SIRT6 abundance. It is the converse of the SIRT6-stabilizing variant mechanism.

AAV-mediated delivery of centenarian SIRT6 reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts, validating the variant's silencing function in progeria. The directionality is CentSIRT6 expression upstream of LINE-1 reduction. This is a proof-of-concept gene-therapy approach to laminopathy. It extends the SIRT6/LINE-1 axis to a treatable model.

SIRT6-mediated mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1 recruits HP1α to package LINE-1 retrotransposons into heterochromatin, silencing their expression. The directionality is SIRT6/KAP1 upstream of HP1α tethering. This protects genome stability by containing mobile elements. It explains how SIRT6 loss derepresses LINE-1.

The phosphatase CDC14B dephosphorylates SIRT2, triggering its ubiquitination and 26S proteasomal degradation, which promotes exit from mitosis. The directionality is CDC14B upstream of SIRT2 destabilization. This couples SIRT2 turnover to cell-cycle progression. It ensures SIRT2 levels fall as cells complete division.

The ICE (Induced Changes in Epigenetics) Mouse uses inducible I-PpoI expression to introduce targeted double-strand breaks that are repaired without introducing mutations. The directionality is I-PpoI upstream of controlled DSB formation. This lets researchers trigger DNA damage alone, isolating epigenetic from mutational effects. It is the experimental engine of the RCM model.

Induction of DSBs in the ICE Mouse, followed by repair, produces accelerated epigenetic aging and physiological decline without mutagenesis, supporting the RCM (rizortho/Reversible-Cellular-Memory) hypothesis. The directionality is DSB repair upstream of epigenetic aging. This argues aging can arise from information loss, not just damage. It is a cornerstone experiment for the Information Theory of Aging.

DSB induction in the ICE Mouse shifts the epigenetic (DNA-methylation) clock, consistent with chromatin modifiers such as SIRT1 relocalizing away from native sites during repair. The directionality is DSB repair upstream of clock acceleration. This provides a quantitative readout of epigenetic drift. It links the RCM model to measurable aging biomarkers.

Because the ICE Mouse phenotype occurs without mutations, it is attributed to loss of epigenetic information rather than hardware damage, supporting the Information Theory of Aging. The directionality is mutation-free DSB repair upstream of information loss. This reframes aging as a software, not hardware, failure. It is a foundational claim of Sinclair's theory.

I-PpoI recognizes and cleaves a specific ~15–20 bp sequence within rRNA gene repeats, generating sequence-specific double-strand breaks. The directionality is I-PpoI upstream of targeted DSBs. Its specificity makes it ideal for the ICE Mouse's controlled damage. This enables reproducible epigenetic-aging studies.

David Sinclair identified SIRT1 as a mediator of caloric-restriction benefits and, in a landmark 2003 study, discovered resveratrol as a sirtuin-activating compound (STAC). The directionality is the discovery establishing SIRT1/STAC centrality to longevity. This launched the modern sirtuin field. It connects basic yeast findings to mammalian therapeutics.

In 2003, Sinclair showed resveratrol extends yeast lifespan via Sir2 and later demonstrated parallel effects in higher organisms, discovering it as the first STAC. The directionality is the discovery upstream of the STAC concept. This catalyzed decades of sirtuin-drug development. It remains a seminal finding in geroscience.

Sinclair co-founded Sirtris Pharmaceuticals (later acquired by GlaxoSmithKline) to develop STACs such as SRT1720 and SRT2104 as therapeutics. The directionality is the academic discovery translated into a company. This drove clinical translation of sirtuin activators. It illustrates the bench-to-bedside path of sirtuin research.

The Sinclair lab developed the ICE Mouse to test the RCM hypothesis using mutation-free double-strand breaks. The directionality is the model enabling tests of epigenetic aging. This provided key evidence for the Information Theory of Aging. It is a methodological contribution alongside the theoretical framework.

Sinclair proposed the information-theory-of-aging framework, positing that aging results from loss of epigenetic information (the 'software') rather than mere damage accumulation. The directionality is the theory explaining aging as reversible information loss. Sirtuins such as SIRT1 are central because they relocalize during repair, driving epigenetic drift. It is a unifying hypothesis motivating NAD+/sirtuin restoration.

SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, which co-activates the BDNF promoter, linking mitochondrial biogenesis to neurotrophic support. The directionality is SIRT1/PGC-1α upstream of BDNF transcription. This couples energy metabolism to neuronal growth-factor expression. It reinforces the metabolic–neurotrophic axis of SIRT1.

The positive histone acetyltransferases PCAF and GCN5 acetylate the myogenic transcription factor MyoD, enhancing its DNA-binding and recruitment of transcriptional machinery. The directionality is PCAF/GCN5 upstream of MyoD activation. This promotes muscle differentiation. SIRT1 opposes this by deacetylating both PCAF and MyoD.

Upon oncogenic stress, the PML-IV isoform recruits both p53 and SIRT1 into PML nuclear bodies, assembling a stress-responsive regulatory hub. The directionality is PML-IV upstream of p53/SIRT1 compartmentalization. Within these bodies, SIRT1 deacetylates p53 to shape the senescence/apoptosis decision. It connects PML bodies to sirtuin-mediated tumor suppression.

PML-IV overexpression is sufficient to induce p53-dependent premature senescence, and loss of PML accelerates tumorigenesis, establishing PML as a tumor suppressor. The directionality is PML upstream of senescence. This process engages SIRT1 and p53 at PML nuclear bodies. It contextualizes SIRT1's role in proliferation arrest.

The Mediterranean Diet's resveratrol content is proposed to activate SIRT1, linking the dietary pattern to longevity pathways (moderate confidence 0.75). The directionality is diet-derived resveratrol upstream of SIRT1 activation. This is one of several polyphenol-mediated mechanisms of the diet. Human causality is inferential rather than proven.

The PREDIMED trial showed that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with olive oil or nuts significantly reduced major cardiovascular events. The directionality is dietary pattern upstream of lower CVD incidence. Polyphenols including resveratrol may engage SIRT1, but the effect is multifactorial. It is a clinically validated dietary intervention.

The Mediterranean Diet raises HDL while reducing LDL oxidation through its polyphenol-rich components, improving the overall lipid profile. The directionality is diet upstream of favorable lipid changes. This contributes to its cardiovascular protection. Resveratrol and other polyphenols are putative SIRT1-engaging contributors.

The SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio defines the hormetic window—the dose range over which mitochondrial stress triggers adaptive responses rather than damage. The directionality is the ratio upstream of the adaptive-vs-harmful threshold. Because SIRT3 is protective and SIRT4 is detrimental, a high ratio broadens resilience. Caloric restriction and youth raise this ratio; aging lowers it.

Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) such as resveratrol lower the Km of SIRT1 for its peptide/NAD+ substrates, amplifying deacetylation efficiency. The directionality is STAC binding upstream of enhanced catalytic rate. This allosteric effect is the defining action of a STAC. It underlies the metabolic and longevity benefits attributed to these molecules.

Anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies eliminate CD38+ Tregs and MDSCs and reduce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression, restoring T- and NK-cell function in the tumor microenvironment. The directionality is anti-CD38 therapy upstream of TME reprogramming. This is both an anticancer action and a means to spare NAD+ for sirtuins. It illustrates the dual therapeutic logic of CD38 targeting.

links.context: SIRT1 and AMPK form a reciprocal regulatory loop in which each can activate the other, jointly promoting energy homeostasis and autophagic flux. The directionality is bidirectional: SIRT1 deacetylates/activates LKB1/PGC-1α and AMPK phosphorylates/activates SIRT1. This creates a self-reinforcing metabolic circuit. It is a central node integrating nutrient sensing and clearance.

FOXO4 deacetylation by SIRT1 enhances expression of GADD45 and suppresses caspase-3/7 activity, promoting DNA repair over apoptosis. The directionality is SIRT1 → FOXO4 → GADD45 induction. This biases cells toward damage repair rather than death. It is a further example of SIRT1 steering stress responses toward survival and genome maintenance.
Carmofur has IC50 29 nM against acid ceramidase, is clinically approved in Japan, crosses the BBB, and is a repurposing candidate for senolytic therapy.
HCQ blocks cytoprotective autophagy in cancer cells and is combined with chemotherapy in clinical trials. Results have been modest and inconsistent across cancer types.
SQSTM1/p62-mediated selective autophagy directly degrades p16 and p21 (independent of UPS), reversing the senescent phenotype in canine MMVD valve cells.
TRIAD (Test of Rapamycin In Aging Dogs) is a parallel-group, double-masked, randomized, placebo-controlled trial testing rapamycin's effect on lifespan and healthspan in companion dogs.
PAK2 directly binds and phosphorylates Caspase-7 at Ser30, Thr173, and Ser239, neutralizing its effector function and promoting survival in breast cancer.
Pin1 binding to phosphorylated BAX (Thr167) catalyzes a conformational change that locks Bax in an inactive state, preventing mitochondrial translocation and MOMP.
PTPN5 (STEP), along with PTPN2 and PTPN23, dephosphorylates BAK at Tyr108, licensing it for mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization and apoptosis.
In K-RAS mutated cancers, hyperactive ERK1/2 phosphorylates and inactivates PTPN5, locking BAK in its inactive phosphorylated state and providing resistance to apoptosis.
Cardiolipin stimulates DRP1 GTPase activity for fission AND is required for OPA1-mediated fusion — it has dual pro-fusion and pro-fission roles depending on context.
CDK5 phosphorylates NOXA at Ser13, causing inactivation in metabolically regulated T-cell leukemia cells.
Trehalose activates TFEB via inhibiting Akt, increasing clearance of proteolipid aggregates in Batten disease and reducing cardiac hypertrophy/fibrosis in chronic MI models.
Celastrol activates TFEB via inhibiting mTORC1, reducing insoluble phosphorylated Tau aggregates and improving memory deficiency in Alzheimer's disease models.
Bleomycin induces premature senescence via DNA breaks, activating p53-p21 and p16 pathways with SASP secretion.
Sodium butyrate (HDAC inhibitor) induces senescence-like state via p21 upregulation, which can be both p53-dependent and independent.
The Lands cycle exchanges fatty acids into the sn-2 position of membrane phospholipids. ACase-liberated fatty acids enter this cycle, enriching PUFA-containing species.

Mutant huntingtin (mHTT) uncouples fission from degradation while disrupting autophagic flux. Broad-spectrum autophagy activators like rapamycin may be insufficient if downstream transport remains blocked.
PLK3 phosphorylates BCL-XL at Ser49, causing cell cycle G2 arrest in lymphoma cells.
RSK phosphorylates APAF-1 at Ser268, causing inhibition in prostate cancer cells.
